the clause is conjoined to the preceding one. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name, genitive; [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to (mutaʿalliq) برزوا. ﴿الْواحِدِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of الله. ﴿الْقَهَّارِ﴾ a second adjective. ﴿وَتَرَى﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif, its fāʿil being latent. ﴿الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مُقَرَّنِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿فِي الْأَصْفادِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to مقرنين. ﴿سَرابِيلُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ قَطِرانٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَتَغْشى﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility. ﴿وُجُوهَهُمُ﴾ a fronted mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿النَّارُ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:51-52.t: ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ اللَّهُ﴾ the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of causation; the preposition and its genitive noun — made up of the lām of causation, the implied an and what follows it, interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) — are attached to (mutaʿalliq) برزوا; the Divine Name is fāʿil (agent). ﴿كُلَّ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿نَفْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ما﴾ a relative in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَسَبَتْ﴾ a past verb, the tāʾ is for the feminine, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسابِ﴾ inna, the Divine Name is its noun, سريع its khabar (predicate), and الحساب is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿هذا﴾ the hāʾ is for alerting (tanbīh), and ذا is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بَلاغٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to بلاغ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلِيُنْذَرُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and the lām is causal, and a passive imperfect verb, accusative by an implied an after the lām of causation, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; an and what follows it, interpreted as a maṣdar, are genitive by the lām of causation, and [they are] attached to an omitted [verb], its implied form being "لينصحوا ولينذروا". «[Translator's note: so in the source ("fāʿil"); with a passive verb the wāw would ordinarily be called nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).]» ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ينذروا. ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied an after the lām of causation, and the wāw is the fāʿil; it is conjoined. ﴿أَنَّما﴾ the restraining and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿هُوَ إِلهٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; anna and what follows it take the place of the two objects of يعلموا. ﴿واحِدٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of إله. ﴿وَلِيَذَّكَّرَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and the lām is causal, and an imperfect verb, accusative by an; it is conjoined to what preceded. ﴿أُولُوا﴾ fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw because it is treated like the sound masculine plural. ﴿الْأَلْبابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

dervis-irab:13-18.t:
* Vocabulary:
(عادٍ): It has many meanings, and here it means "became" (ṣāra), so it takes the same rule and works like it. One says: عاد إليّ من فلان مكروه, meaning "something disagreeable came to me from so-and-so." Among its meanings: عاده يعوده عودا, "he turned him away"; عاد السائل, "he sent the beggar away"; عاد فلانا بالمعروف, "he did a kindness to so-and-so"; and عاده عودا, "he made it a habit"; likewise عاد يعود عودا وعيادا وعيادة, and عوادة المريض means "he visited the sick person," so he is a visitor (ʿāʾid). In al-Qāmūs: عاد يعود الشيء عودا وعيادا means "he began it and did it a second time." It is said that the proverb derives from this:
«العود أحمد» ("the return is more praiseworthy").
(اسْتَفْتَحُوا): They asked Allah for victory over their enemies, as in the words of the Exalted: «إن تستفتحوا فقد جاءكم الفتح» ("If you seek a decision, the decision has come to you"). It is also said that it means they asked Allah to judge and sought His ruling between them, from al-fatāḥa, meaning "judgement," as in the words of the Exalted: «ربنا افتح بيننا وبين قومنا بالحق» ("Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth"). In al-Qāmūs: al-fatḥ, like al-fatāḥa (with ḍamma or kasra on the fāʾ), means:
judgement between two disputants.
(صَدِيدٍ): It is what flows from the skins of the people of the Fire.
(يَتَجَرَّعُهُ): He forces himself to gulp it down, that is, to swallow it. In al-Asās: "I gulped the water and I swallowed it in one go (ajtaraʿtuhu), and I gulped it (tajarraʿtuhu) a little at a time; he gave me to drink only a gulp, a small gulp, or a gulping; we spent the night at al-Ajraʿ and at al-Jarʿāʾ, and they alighted at al-Ajāriʿ, which are rough lands topped with sand."
(يُسِيغُهُ): From asāgha al-ṭaʿām or al-sharāb, "he made the food or drink go down easily"; that is, its passage into the throat is easy.

* I'rab:
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِرُسُلِهِمْ لَنُخْرِجَنَّكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِنا): قال الذين: a verb and an agent; the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); لرسلهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قال; the lām is the one that prepares for an oath; نخرجنكم: a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; من أرضنا: attached to نخرجنكم; and the sentence is the content of what was said (maqūl al-qawl).
(أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِي مِلَّتِنا): أو is a conjunction meaning "unless" (illā); more on أو will come in the section on Benefits.
ولتعودن is conjoined to نخرجنكم, except that the verb here is declined (muʿrab) [Translator's note: the source prints "معروب"; "muʿrab" is evidently intended] because the nūn of emphasis is not in direct contact with it. It is nominative, and the sign of its being nominative is the presence of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of similar letters, and the wāw of the group, which has been dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent. The doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis, and parallels for it have already preceded. في ملتنا: attached to تعودن or to its predicate (khabar).
(فَأَوْحى إِلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ لَنُهْلِكَنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; أوحى إليهم ربهم: a verb and an agent; ولنهلكن: the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; نهلكن الظالمين: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, a latent agent and a direct object; the clause has no grammatical position because it is explicative.
(وَلَنُسْكِنَنَّكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ): The wāw is a conjunction; نسكننكم: an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, an agent and a direct object; الأرض is accusative by removal of the preposition, or it is a direct object by extension (ʿalā l-ittisāʿ). What was said about دخل, سكن and the like has already preceded. ومن بعدهم: a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(ذلِكَ لِمَنْ خافَ مَقامِي وَخافَ وَعِيدِ): ذلك is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and لمن the khabar (predicate); the clause خاف is the ṣila, and its agent is latent, its implied form being "he"; ومقامي is the direct object, and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to the agent, that is, "my standing over him with watchfulness," or it is a noun of place. Al-Zajjāj said: "the place of his standing before Me for the reckoning." وخاف is also a past verb, and وعيد is a direct object, accusative, and the sign of its being accusative is the fatḥa implied on the letter before the omitted yāʾ of the first-person speaker, omitted out of regard for the verse endings (fawāṣil).
(وَاسْتَفْتَحُوا وَخابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ): واستفتحوا: a past verb, and the wāw is the agent. The pronoun refers to the messengers, meaning "and they asked Allah for victory over their enemies." It is also said that it refers to the disbelievers, meaning "and the disbelievers asked for a decision against the messengers." The better view is that it refers to both parties, because each side seeks victory over the other. The wāw is resumptive and the clause is a resumptive one. وخاب كل جبار: a verb and an agent, and عنيد is an adjective of جبار. The meaning of خاب is "he perished" or "he lost." Al-ʿanīd is the one who opposes the truth and keeps away from it; it is taken from al-ʿind, which is "the side," that is, he takes to his own side, turning away. The poet said:
إذا نزلت فاجعلوني وسطا ... إني كبير لا أطيق الغدا
("When you camp, put me in the middle; I am old and cannot bear the morning meal.")
And al-Zajjāj said: al-ʿanīd is the one who swerves from the right course. (مِنْ وَرائِهِ جَهَنَّمُ وَيُسْقى مِنْ ماءٍ صَدِيدٍ): من ورائه is a fronted predicate and جهنم a delayed subject. The meaning of من ورائه is "from before him," that is, in front of him and behind him; the clause is a second adjective of جبار. ويسقى: the wāw is a conjunction on something implied, as an answer to a questioner's question, as if it were said: "What will happen then?" and it was said: "He will be thrown into it and given to drink." ويسقى is an imperfect passive verb; ومن ماء is attached to يسقى; and صديد is a badal (substitute) for ماء or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it, as if He had said "and he is given to drink of water," then wished to make clear what He had left vague, so He followed with His word صديد, because al-ṣadīd is water, but specifically what flows from the skins of the people of the Fire. Abū Ḥayyān said: "Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: it is an adjective of ماء, as you say 'this is a ring of iron,' though it is not water; but since it takes the place of water in our custom, meaning that water is applied to it. It is also said to be an adjective with the particle of comparison dropped, as you say 'I passed a man, a lion,' the implied being 'like a lion,' so 'like pus.' According to Ibn ʿAṭiyya's view it is pus itself and not truly water; according to this view it is not pus but something resembling pus. And al-Zamakhsharī said: ṣadīd is an ʿaṭf bayān of ماء; he said: 'and he is given to drink of water,' so He left it vague, then made it clear by His word ṣadīd.'" The Basrans do not permit ʿaṭf bayān with indefinite nouns, while the Kufans permit it and al-Fārisī followed them, so he parsed زيتونة as an ʿaṭf bayān of شجرة مباركة. The clause يسقى is conjoined to something omitted, its implied form being: "Before him is Hell, in which he is thrown whatever is thrown, and water of intense kind that is distinguished from its torment by what is harsher and more painful."
(يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلا يَكادُ يُسِيغُهُ): The clause is an adjective of ماء; ويتجرعه: a verb, a latent agent and a direct object. There is no harm in making the clause resumptive, set forth as a reply to a question, as if it were said: "So what does he do with it?" and it was said: "He gulps it down," that is, he forces himself to swallow it time after time to quench the violence of thirst and the heat of burning. ولا: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative; ويكاد is one of the verbs of proximity (afʿāl al-muqāraba), its noun is latent, its implied form being "he," and the clause يسيغه is its predicate. More on this wondrous construction will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(وَيَأْتِيهِ الْمَوْتُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكانٍ): The wāw is a conjunction; ويأتيه الموت: a verb, a delayed agent and a fronted direct object, meaning the causes of death, as if they had joined forces against him, so they come to him from every place. The preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, meaning they come to him surrounding him from all his sides.
(وَما هُوَ بِمَيِّتٍ وَمِنْ وَرائِهِ عَذابٌ غَلِيظٌ): The wāw is the wāw of ḥāl; ما is the negative Ḥijāzī mā, and هو is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and ميت is genitive in form and accusative in position as the predicate of ما; ومن ورائه is a fronted predicate and عذاب a delayed subject, and غليظ an adjective of عذاب.
(مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ أَعْمالُهُمْ كَرَمادٍ اشْتَدَّتْ بِهِ الرِّيحُ فِي يَوْمٍ عاصِفٍ): مثل الذين is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, according to Sībawayh, its implied form being "and in what is related to you is the likeness"; parallels have already preceded. The clause كفروا بربهم is the ṣila; وأعمالهم is a mubtadaʾ, and the kāf, meaning "like" (mithl), is the khabar; or it is a particle with its genitive noun in the position of nominative as the khabar. The sentence is resumptive, answering an implied question that arose from the mention of the likeness, as if he had said: "And what is that likeness?" and it was said: "Their deeds are like ashes." It is also possible that مثل is a mubtadaʾ, أعمالهم a second mubtadaʾ and كرماد the khabar of the second, the second with its khabar being the khabar of the first. Abū Ḥayyān rejected this view, saying: "It is not permissible, because the clause that occurs as a predicate of the mubtadaʾ which is مثل is bare of a link referring back to مثل, and it is not the same as the mubtadaʾ in meaning, so it does need a link." And it is possible, and it is a fine view, that مثل is a mubtadaʾ and أعمالهم a badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) for it, and كرماد the khabar of both مثل and أعمالهم together. The clause اشتدت به الريح is an adjective of رماد, and في يوم عاصف is a ḥāl from الريح.
(لا يَقْدِرُونَ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا عَلى شَيْءٍ ذلِكَ هُوَ الضَّلالُ الْبَعِيدُ): The clause is a ḥāl from the agent of كفروا; ويقدرون: a verb and an agent; ومما كسبوا is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of شيء and was fronted before it; وعلى شيء is attached to يقدرون; the clause كسبوا is the ṣila; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, هو a second mubtadaʾ and الضلال the khabar of the second, the second with its khabar being the khabar of the first; and البعيد is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there are many varieties of rhetoric, which we set out below:
1- In the words of the verses, which come as threat and menace, there is murāʿāt al-naẓīr (harmony of related terms), which has already been discussed; all their words combine to express what is frightening and shatters hearts.
2- In His words (يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلا يَكادُ يُسِيغُهُ) there are many arts, the most important of which are the following:
(a) Al-istiqṣāʾ (exhaustive treatment): it is that the speaker takes up a meaning and treats it exhaustively, that is, he brings all its accidents and necessary attributes after exhausting all its essential qualities, so that he leaves nothing to say about it to anyone who takes it up after him. He has exhausted the meaning he intended in the verse, namely the loathsomeness of the pus that he drinks, in that he "gulps it down." There are several possibilities in this: first, that it is the reflexive form (muṭāwiʿ) of جرعته with doubling, like علمته فتعلم; second, that it denotes effort (takalluf), and we chose it in the parsing, meaning "he forces himself to swallow it," and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned no other; third, that it denotes gradualness, as in تفهمته, meaning he takes it little by little in gulps, as one comes to understand little by little through instruction; and fourth, that it has the meaning of the simple form جرعه. In all these cases He has covered the utmost that a water-drinker can undergo.
(b) Exaggeration (mubālagha) in His words «ولا يكاد»: the verb يكاد enters for exaggeration, meaning "he does not come near to swallowing it," so how could swallowing happen? It is like «لم يكد يراها» ("he can hardly see it"), meaning he did not come near to seeing it, so how could he see it?
(c) The mention of death while meaning its causes; this is a figurative usage (majāz).
(d) Describing the punishment as "thick" (ghalīẓ) is a kināya (metonymy) for its strength and continuity, because thickness implies strength and calls for continuity, in which all times are joined, with no separation between them.
(e) Hyperbole (ghuluww) by mentioning كاد. This holds in every speech in which a particle of proximity is used, as in the words of al-Farazdaq:
يكاد يمسكه عرفان راحته ... ركن الحطيم إذا ما جاء يستلم
("The recognition of his palm almost holds him, the corner of al-Ḥaṭīm, when he comes to touch it.")
And Abū l-ʿAlāʾ went to excess in using it. He said:
تكاد قسيه من غير رام ... تمكن في سيوفهم النبالا
("His bows almost, without any archer, set arrows into their swords.")
تكاد سوابق حملته تغني ... تجد إلى رقابهم انسلالا
("The foremost of his charge almost suffice, finding a way of slipping to their necks.")
تكاد سوابق حملته تغني ... عن الأقدار صونا وابتذالا
("The foremost of his charge almost make one independent of fates, in preserving and in spending.")
سرى برق المعرة بعد وهن ... فبات براحة يصف الكلالا
("The lightning of al-Maʿarra travelled after a spell of night, and passed the night with relief describing weariness.")
شجا ركبا وأفراسا وإبلا ... وزاد فكاد أن يشجو الرحالا
("It grieved riders, horses and camels, and increased, so it almost grieved the saddles.")
And Ibn Khafāja al-Andalusī has verses in which كاد here is a "dancer" (murqiṣa):
وأهيف قام يسعى ... والسكر يعطف قده
("A slender one rose to walk about, while drunkenness bent his stature.")
وقد ترنح غصنا ... وحمر الكأس ورده
("He swayed like a branch, and the red of the cup was his rose.")
وألهب السكر خدا ... أورى به الوجد زنده
("Drunkenness inflamed a cheek, whose flint passion made spark.")
فكاد يشرب نفسي ... وكدت أشرب خدّه
("So he almost drank my soul, and I almost drank his cheek.")
All of this is acceptable hyperbole, because it is accompanied by the particle, and its beauty increases when it includes a fine kind of imagination (takhyīl), as in the words of al-Mutanabbī:
عقدت سنابكها عليه عثيرا ... لو تبتغي عنقا عليه أمكنا
("Their hooves knotted dust above him; had it sought a neck upon it, it would have been possible.")
And Abū l-ʿAlāʾ in describing the sword:
يذيب الرعب منه كل عضب ... فلولا الغمد يمسكه لسالا
("Terror of it melts every sword; were it not for the scabbard that holds it, it would flow.")
And he said describing horses:
ولما لم يسابقهن شيء ... من الحيوان سابقن الظلالا
("And since no living thing raced them, they raced shadows.")
As for unacceptable hyperbole, it is of two kinds. One kind art finds tolerable, as in the words of al-Mutanabbī:
ولو قلم ألقيت في شقّ رأسه ... من السقم ما غيرت من خط كاتب
("Were a pen placed in the parting of his head, from illness, it would not have changed a scribe's script.")
And the words of Abū Nuwās:
وأخفت أهل الشرك حتى انه ... لتخافك النطف التي لم تخلق
("You frightened the people of polytheism until even the sperm-drops not yet created fear you.")
And tatmīm (completion): we have spoken of it as well and will explain it here. We say: tatmīm is of three kinds: completion of deficiency, completion of precaution and completion of exaggeration. He said يتجرعه, and had He said جرعه it would not have conveyed the meaning intended, because "he drank down the water" does not point to the meaning of loathing; but when He brought the tāʾ in the pattern of tafaʿʿul, it conveyed that he forces himself to drink it with effort, and that he suffers from drinking it what description cannot reach of nausea and loathing. Then He took precaution, because it might suggest that he forced himself to drink it and then the matter became easy for him afterwards, so He brought kaydūda (the "almost"), that is, he forced himself to drink it yet he can hardly drink it. Had He been content with kaydūda the meaning would have been sound without exaggeration, but when يسيغه came it conveyed that he cannot swallow it but chokes on it, so he drinks it after great difficulty, gulp after gulp, and his torment is prolonged, now by the heat and now by the thirst.
3- The simile of representation (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī) in His words «والذين كفروا أعمالهم كرماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف»: the thing compared is composite, namely those who disbelieved and their good deeds that they perform in their lives, such as kinship ties by which they support the needy, charity by which they mend the broken, and knowledge whose benefit extends to the servants; and the thing compared to is ashes, which is what the fire has crushed of bodies, together with the intensity of the wind and the stormy day. The point of likeness is that the stormy wind blows the ashes away and scatters their parts so that no trace remains of them; likewise their disbelief nullified their deeds and made them vain, so that no trace of them remains.
4- Intellectual metaphor (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī) in attributing the storming to the day, as in their saying "his day is fasting and his night is standing in prayer." Their praiseworthy works and glorious generosities, and what they undertook, such as helping the distressed, freeing slaves, releasing the captive, ransoming prisoners and slaughtering camels for guests, and the like, were likened, in their being nullified and going as scattered dust because they were built on no foundation of knowing Allah and believing in Him, to ashes that the wind blew away on the day to which the storming was attributed.
5- Describing error (ḍalāl) as "far" has been discussed recently, so renew your acquaintance with it.

* Benefits:
«أو» is a conjunction with several meanings, which we set out below:
(a) Doubt, as in «لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم» ("We stayed a day or part of a day").
(b) Vagueness (ibhām), as in «وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين» ("and indeed we or you are upon guidance or in manifest error"), where the evidence is in the first أو.
(c) Permission (ibāḥa), which occurs before what allows combination, as in: "Sit with the scholars or the ascetics."
(d) Choice (takhyīr), which occurs before what prevents combination, as in: "Marry Hind or her sister," and "Go on foot or riding."
(e) Absolute joining, like the wāw, as in the verse:
وقد زعمت ليلى بأني فاجر ... لنفسي تقاها أو عليها فجورها
("Laylā claimed that I am wicked; for her soul is its piety, or upon it is its wickedness.")
Some denied it here and said it is for vagueness, meaning she knows that she possesses both attributes and meant to leave the listener in vagueness. This is rejected, because piety being for the soul and wickedness being against it are two things that coexist in reality, as the Exalted said: «لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت» ("For it is what it earned, and against it what it earned"). Among its occurrences for absolute joining is the verse of Jarīr:
جاء الخلافة أو كانت له قدرا ... كما أتى ربه موسى على قدر
("He came to the caliphate, or it was destined for him, as Moses came to his Lord by decree.")
And the famous verse of al-Nābigha in his Muʿallaqa:
قالت ألا ليتما هذا الحمام لنا ... إلى حمامتنا أو نصفه فقد
("She said: would that this dove were ours, together with our dove, or half of it, then it would suffice.")
In this sense some scholars took أو in the words of the Exalted «وأرسلناه إلى مائة ألف أو يزيدون» ("And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more"), and there are other views on it that will come in their place, if Allah wills.
(f) Iḍrāb (turning away), like «بل». Sībawayh stipulated two conditions for allowing it: a preceding negation or prohibition, and repetition of the governing element, as in "Zayd did not stand, or ʿAmr did not stand," and he cited as evidence the words of the Exalted: «ولا تطع منهما آثما أو كفورا». Others besides Sībawayh did not stipulate these two conditions, and cited the verse of Jarīr:
كانوا ثمانين أو زادوا ثمانية ... لولا رجاؤك قد قتلت أولادي
("They were eighty, or they increased by eight; were it not for hope in you, I would have killed my children.")
It is also said that this is what is intended by the words of the Exalted «وأرسلناه إلى مائة ألف أو يزيدون». Al-Farrāʾ said that the first report is according to what appears to people, to repel the objection of how iḍrāb could be allowed when He knows their number and that they are more; so it is a report from Him, the Exalted, based on what people estimate without verification, then He proceeds to verification, turning away from what people err in on the basis of the apparent estimate. More of this valuable discussion will come when we speak on this verse.
(g) Division (taqsīm), as in: "A word is a noun or a verb or a particle." Some called it tafrīq (separation), as in the words of the Exalted: «وقالوا كونوا هودا أو نصارى» ("And they said: Be Jews or Christians"), and this is preferable to the term "division," because using the wāw for division is better.
(h) Meaning "except" (illā) in exception; after it the imperfect is put in the accusative by an implied an, as in the words of Ziyād al-Aʿjam:
وكنت إذا غمزت قناة قوم ... كسرت كعوبها أو تستقيما
("When I pressed the spear-shaft of a people, I broke its joints unless it became straight.")
This verse (i.e., the one under discussion) is of this kind, but the accusative is excluded because of the entry of the lām that denotes the present, so the implying of an, which denotes the future, is excluded lest a contradiction arise.
(i) Meaning "until" (ilā), which is like the preceding in that the imperfect after it is accusative by an implied an, as in the verse:
لأستسهلنّ الصعب أو أدرك المنى ... فما انقادت الآمال إلا لصابر
("I will make the difficult easy until I reach my hopes; hopes yield only to the patient.")
(j) Denoting nearness (taqrīb), as in "I do not know whether he said salām or farewell." Al-Ḥarīrī said in Durrat al-Ghawwāṣ: "They do not distinguish between their saying: 'I do not know which of us performed the iqāma or the adhān' and their saying 'I know whether he performed the iqāma or the adhān.' The difference between them is that when you pronounce أم you are in doubt about what he did of the iqāma and the adhān, and when you use أو you have established that he did both, except that because of the speed and closeness between them he became like one who did neither the iqāma nor the adhān."
(k) Conditional, as in: "I will surely strike him, whether he lives or dies," meaning if he lives after the striking and if he dies.
(l) Partition (tabʿīḍ), mentioned by some who cited the words of the Exalted «وقالوا كونوا هودا أو نصارى»; but this is sheer affectation.

dervis-irab:5-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَسُومُونَكُمْ): they make you taste. Its origin is from sāma al-silʿata yasūmu sawman and sawāman, meaning he offered it and mentioned its price; sāma al-mushtarī al-silʿata means he asked to sell it or asked its price; sāmat al-māshiya means the cattle went out to pasture; sāmahu al-amra means he charged him with it; sāmahu khasfan means he humiliated him. ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm said:
إذا ما الملك سام الناس خسفا ... أبينا أن نقر الذل فينا
(When the king subjects people to humiliation, we refuse to let humiliation settle among us.)
Sāma al-ṭayru ʿalā l-shayʾi means the bird hovered over the thing; sāmat al-rīḥu means the wind passed and continued; sāma nāqatahu ʿalā l-ḥawḍi means he presented his she-camel to the trough.
Figuratively, samtu l-marʾata l-muʿānaqa means I wanted it from her and offered it to her. The sīn together with the wāw, as first and second radical, has a wonderful property: the two give the word the meaning of encompassing a thing, dominating it, including it and covering it, because that which encompasses things includes them and dominates them. Thus al-sūʾ is ugliness, and it encompasses its possessor and wraps him, just as it encompasses those to whom it extends and whom it strikes. Allah the Exalted said «عليهم دائرة السوء» ("upon them is the turn of evil"). And it is said "so-and-so encompasses the good with the bad", and "this is of what grieves you (sāʾaka) and burdens you (nāʾaka)", and "of what harms you (yasūʾuka) and burdens you (yanūʾuka)". Al-Jāḥiẓ said: it is from al-sūʾ, meaning leprosy (baraṣ). Abū Zubayd said:
لم يهب حرمة النديم وحقّت ... يا لقومي للسوءة السواء
(He did not respect the sanctity of the drinking companion, and it was due... O my people, for the ugly disgrace!)
Sawwaja and sayyaja l-karma and the like, or ʿalā l-karmi, means he made a fence around it which encloses and protects it; al-siyāj, with kasra on the sīn, is the wall, and whatever is put around a vineyard and the like; the plural of al-siyāj is siyājāt, aswija and sūj. Noah's ark was made of sāj, which is a black, heavy wood that the earth hardly decays. They wore al-saylasān, which are the wide round shawls. Al-sāḥa is open space between the houses of the quarter that surrounds it, with no building or roof in it; its plural is sāḥ, sūḥ and sāḥāt. They say "the sky has reddened and the courtyards have turned dusty" when drought occurs. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
وكان سيّان أن لا يسرحوا نعما ... أو يسرحوه بها واغبرت السّوح
(It was all the same whether they did not send out their cattle or sent them out, with the courtyards turned dusty.)
Sākhat qawāʾimu l-dābbati fī l-arḍi means the beast's legs sank into the ground; "this is land in which feet sink"; sākhat bihim al-arḍu means the earth swallowed them. Sāda qawmahu yasūduhum is as though he encompassed them with his favour and his dominance; sādahu means he overcame him in a contest. Al-sawād is the opposite of whiteness, a colour that surrounds a body or a thing; al-sawād is also a person's figure; sawād al-balda is what surrounds it of countryside and villages, and from it sawād al-ʿIrāq for what lies between Basra and Kufa and the villages around them. Shawqī was inventive when he said:
قف تمهل وخذ أمانا لقلبي ... من عيون المها وراء السواد
(Stop, wait, and take safety for my heart from the eyes of the wild oryx behind the black.)
Al-aswad is well known; al-aswad is also the great black snake known as the ḥanash. "So-and-so is aswad al-kabid" means an enemy; "they are sūd al-akbād" means enemies. Al-sawdāʾ and al-suwaydāʾ, with the physicians, is a humour whose seat is the spleen, the disease of melancholia, which is a corruption of thought with sorrow; sawdāʾ al-qalb and suwaydāʾuhu is its core. Sāwarahu means he leapt upon him; "he has a sawra in war" (a surge of attack); tasawwartu l-ḥāʾiṭa means I scaled the wall; al-sūr is the wall that goes around a city and encloses it; sawrat al-khamr and its sūrāt mean its sharpness; al-siwār is an ornament like a collar which a woman wears on her forearm, and it is with kasra or ḍamma on the sīn, and one also says al-iswār. The ruler yasūsu l-raʿiyya (governs the subjects) and yasūsu their affairs, and one says suwwisa fulān amra qawmihi, in the passive. Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
لقد سوّست أمر بنيك حتى ... تركتهم أدق من الطحين
(You have managed the affairs of your sons so that you left them finer than flour.)
Al-siyāsa is the reform of creatures by guiding them to the road that saves them in the near or the far term; and without doubt he who governs a people encompasses their affairs. Sāṭahu yasūṭuhu sawṭan means he struck him with the whip, and one strikes only one who is dominated by the other and is subordinate to him. Al-sāʿa is the known time, and it encompasses all existing things so that nothing escapes it. Sāgha l-sharāb means the drink went down easily, as though it prevailed so that nothing stands in its way. Sāfa l-shayʾa means he smelled it, and it has the sense of encompassing and dominating; sawwafahu means he put him off, and said to him "time after time"; and "how long is the distance (masāfa) of this land", and the distance encompasses what the owner of the land possesses; and "between them are masāwif", plural of masāfa. Dhū l-Rumma said:
فقام إلى حرف طواها بطية ... بها كل لمّاع بعيد المساوف
(He rose to a lean she-camel and folded her up in a long journey, in which every gleaming one is far from the distances.)
Sāqa l-niʿama fa-nsāqat means he drove the livestock and it was driven; al-sūq (the market) is well known, and it encompasses the persons, goods and wares that are displayed in it; sāka yasūku sawkan means he rubbed; sawwala lahu l-shayṭānu amran means the Devil overcame him in his affair and made evil seem fair to him; sawwā bayna l-nās means he made them equal; sawwaytu l-miʿwaja fa-stawā means I straightened the crooked and it became straight; «الرحمن على العرش استوى» means he took control (istawlā); "he saw him in the sawāʾ of the place" means in its middle; suwiya l-rajul means the man's affair became straight, and an affair is not straight except for one who has prevailed; "they are sawāʾ" and "they are sawāsiya in evil". And this is among the wonders of this language.
(يَسْتَحْيُونَ): they spare alive.
[Translator's note: the etymological digression in the entry for يَسُومُونَكُمْ is the author's own and ranges over many roots built on s-w; the entries are translated as printed, with the verse quotations glossed in parentheses.]

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا): A resumptive clause, introduced to begin the detailed account of what He stated in summary about the messengers in His saying «وما أرسلنا من رسول». The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; أرسلنا is a verb and agent, موسى is a direct object, and بآياتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "accompanied by Our signs and strengthened by them". (أَنْ أَخْرِجْ قَوْمَكَ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ): أن is explicative (mufassira), and the rule for it is satisfied, namely that it be preceded by a clause that has the sense of saying without its letters; and أرسلنا has the sense of "We said", that is, "We said to him: bring out". It may also be the maṣdar أن that governs the verb in the subjunctive. It is proper for it to be joined to an imperative verb because the purpose is to join it with what is, together with it, interpretable as a maṣdar, namely the verb; and the imperative and others are alike in being verbal. With what follows it, it would be accusative by removal of the preposition, the implied form being بأن اخرج قومك, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to an omitted accusative ḥāl, that is, "saying to him: bring out your people". On this view, parsing it as explicative is less laborious, as long as the two estimations go back to one origin. وقومك is a direct object of أخرج, and من الظلمات إلى النور is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخرج. (وَذَكِّرْهُمْ بِأَيَّامِ اللَّهِ): The wāw is a conjunction; ذكرهم is an imperative verb, a latent agent pronoun and a direct object; and بأيام الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ذكرهم. You will see a useful discussion on His saying "the days of Allah" in the section on benefits. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ): إن is a particle resembling the verb (inna); في ذلك is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; آيات is the postponed ism of إن; لكل is an adjective (naʿt), صبار is a muḍāf ilayhi, and شكور is an adjective of صبار. (وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ): The adverbial is attached to an omitted verb that is explained by what comes after it, namely اذكروا, that is, "remember"; the clause قال موسى is the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverbial; ولقومه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قال; اذكروا is an imperative verb with the wāw as agent; نعمة الله is a direct object; and عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "being upon you". (إِذْ أَنْجاكُمْ مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ): The adverbial is attached to نعمة الله if it is in the sense of the bestowing of favour (inʿām), that is, His bestowing it at that time; it may also be a badal (substitute) for النعمة, because the favour includes the deliverance, so it would be a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl); and من آل فرعون is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنجاكم. (يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذابِ وَيُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْناءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِساءَكُمْ): Three ḥāl clauses, from the House of Pharaoh or from the pronoun of those addressed. (وَفِي ذلِكُمْ بَلاءٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ): The wāw is a conjunction; وفي ذلكم is a fronted khabar; بلاء is a postponed mubtadaʾ; ومن ربكم is an adjective of بلاء; and عظيم is a second adjective.

* Benefits:
(The "days of Allah") means, as in al-Qāmūs, His favours; and yawm ayyūm means severe, and the last day of the month. In al-Mukhtār: "They may have expressed severity by 'day'." This is a case of rational figurative usage (majāz ʿaqlī), the reason being that the Arabs use figurative language by attributing the event to time, so they annex it to it, as in their saying "his day is fasting and his night is standing in prayer" and "the scheming of the night". The interpretation of "the days of Allah" as His trials and His favours is preferred, while al-Zamakhsharī inclined to interpreting the days of Allah as His events that befell the nations before them, the people of Noah, ʿĀd and Thamūd. He said: from it come the days of the Arabs, for their wars and battles, such as the Day of Dhū Qār and the Day of al-Fijār and others. ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm expressed them in his saying:
وأيام لنا غر طوال ... عصينا الملك فيها أن ندينا
(And we have glorious, long days in which we refused the king that we should submit.)

dervis-irab:19-22.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَحِيصٍ): A refuge and a place of escape. Al-maḥīṣ may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), like al-maghīb and al-mashīb, or a noun of place, like al-mabīt and al-maṣīf. In al-Mukhtār: ḥāṣa ʿanhu means "he turned aside and swerved," of the pattern bāʿa, and its verbal nouns are ḥuyūṣ, maḥīṣ, maḥāṣ and ḥayaṣān (with fatḥa on the yāʾ). One says mā ʿanhu maḥīṣ, meaning "there is no way of swerving from it and no escape," and al-inḥiyāṣ is the same. Among their sayings: وقع في حيص بيص, meaning "he fell into a confusion with no way out, and a turmoil that surges with its people." They are two nouns compounded into one noun and built (indeclinable) like khamsata ʿashar; what made their indeclinability necessary is the implied wāw in them. Al-ḥayṣ is falling behind and fleeing, and al-bawṣ is taken from their saying bāṣa yabūṣu, meaning "he escaped and went ahead," because when confusion and turmoil occur, some of them escape and some flee. By analogy it ought to be said ḥayṣ bawṣ, but they made the second follow the first. It has many dialects, the most famous being ḥayṣa bayṣa with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and the bāʾ and on the final letters of both, as indeclinable, as mentioned above. Al-Aṣmaʿī recited from Umayya ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Hudhalī:
قد كنت خراجا ولوجا صرفا ... لم تلتحصني حيص بيص لحاص
("I was one who went out and went in, a skilled one; the confusion of ḥayṣ bayṣ did not entangle me, for it was a way of escape.")
And they said ḥiyṣa biyṣa, with kasra on the first letters and fatḥa on the finals, and some build both on the kasra, as sounds are given kasra, like ghāqi ghāqi. There are other dialects that we have refrained from mentioning.
(بِمُصْرِخِكُمْ): By one who aids you. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "ṣarakha yaṣrukhu, of the pattern qatala, ṣurākhan, so he is ṣārikh and ṣarīkh, when he cries out; and ṣarakha, so he is ṣārikh, when he asks for help; and astaṣrakhtuhu, so he aided me (aṣrakhanī), meaning I asked him for help and he helped me, so he is ṣarīkh, that is, one who helps, and muṣrikh regularly." It is both the helper and the one who asks for help, so it is among the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād), as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: al-mustaghīth (one who seeks help) and al-muṣrikh (one who aids).

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ): The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb jussive by لم; أن and what falls within its scope stand in the place of the two objects of تر. السموات is the object of خلق, and it is said to be an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq); you will see an interesting discussion in the section on Benefits. بالحق: attached to خلق or to something omitted as a ḥāl; so the bāʾ is of causation on the first view and of accompaniment on the second.
(إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ وَيَأْتِ بِخَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ): إن is conditional; ويشأ is the protasis; ويذهبكم is the apodosis, and the kāf is the direct object; ويأت is conjoined to يذهبكم; بخلق is attached to يأت; and جديد is an adjective. (وَما ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ بِعَزِيزٍ): The wāw is a conjunction or of ḥāl; ما is the negative Ḥijāzī mā; ذلك is its noun; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عزيز; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and عزيز is genitive in form and accusative in position as the predicate of ما. (وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ جَمِيعاً): The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, to affirm their being raised from the graves. He expressed it in the past form although its meaning is future, because everything that Allah reports is true and veracious, bound to come about, so it became as if it had already occurred and entered into existence. وبرزوا: a verb and an agent; ولله is attached to برزوا; and جميعا is a ḥāl. (فَقالَ الضُّعَفاءُ لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا لَكُمْ تَبَعاً): The fāʾ is a conjunction; وقال الضعفاء: a verb and an agent; وللذين is attached to قال; the clause استكبروا is the ṣila; the clause إنا is the content of what was said; إن and its noun, and the clause كنا is its predicate; كان and its noun; ولكم is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of it and then was fronted; and تبعا is the predicate of كنا, and it is a plural of tābiʿ, like their saying khādim and khadam.
(فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُغْنُونَ عَنَّا مِنْ عَذابِ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; هل is an interrogative particle; أنتم is the mubtadaʾ and مغنون the khabar; عنا is attached to مغنون; ومن عذاب الله is a ḥāl; the second من is redundant; and شيء is a direct object in position, genitive by من in form. This is the best of the many parsings. (قالُوا لَوْ هَدانَا اللَّهُ لَهَدَيْناكُمْ سَواءٌ عَلَيْنا أَجَزِعْنا أَمْ صَبَرْنا): قالوا: a verb and an agent; لو is a particle of prevention; هدانا الله: a verb, a direct object and an agent; لهديناكم: the lām occurs in the apodosis, and هديناكم is a verb, an agent and a direct object; سواء is a fronted khabar and أجزعنا a delayed mubtadaʾ, because it is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, since the hamza is for equalisation and the verb after it is interpreted as a maṣdar; أم is a connected (muttaṣila) conjunction; and صبرنا is conjoined to جزعنا. (ما لَنا مِنْ مَحِيصٍ): ما is the negative Ḥijāzī mā; لنا is a fronted predicate; من is a redundant preposition; and محيص is genitive in form and, in position, the noun of ما.
(وَقالَ الشَّيْطانُ لَمَّا قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمْ وَعْدَ الْحَقِّ): The wāw is a conjunction; وقال الشيطان: a verb and an agent; لما is a temporal adverbial of time (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya) or a linking particle; قضي الأمر: a verb and a deputy agent, and the clause is annexed to لما, or has no position; إن and its noun, and the clause وعدكم is its predicate; ووعد is an absolute object and الحق is the muḍāf ilayhi; the clause إن الله is the content of what was said, and it is from the speech of Iblīs, said in reply to the people of the Fire who began to blame and rebuke him. (وَوَعَدْتُكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُكُمْ): Something omitted must be implied, namely "and He kept His promise to you" (fa-ṣadaqakum). ووعدتكم is conjoined to وعدكم; فأخلفتكم is conjoined to وعدتكم, and it is a verb, an agent and a direct object. (وَما كانَ لِي عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطانٍ إِلَّا أَنْ دَعَوْتُكُمْ فَاسْتَجَبْتُمْ لِي): The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; كان is a defective past verb; لي is its fronted predicate; عليكم is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of سلطان; من is a preposition and سلطان genitive in form and the noun of كان in position; إلا is a particle of exception; أن and what falls within its scope is the excepted, because a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) must be accusative even if the speech is not affirmative, and because the call is not of the genus of authority; فاستجبتم is conjoined to دعوتكم; and لي is attached to استجبتم.
(فَلا تَلُومُونِي وَلُومُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ): The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), as if it were said: "If you know that you hastened in answering me, then you are the ones to blame." لا is prohibitive; تلوموني is an imperfect verb jussive by the prohibitive لا; the wāw is the agent, the nūn is the protective nūn (wiqāya) and the yāʾ is the direct object; ولوموا is an imperative verb and an agent; and أنفسكم is the direct object. (ما أَنَا بِمُصْرِخِكُمْ وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُصْرِخِيَّ): ما is the negative Ḥijāzī mā; أنا is its noun; بمصرخكم: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and مصرخكم is the predicate of ما in position; وما أنتم بمصرخي is conjoined to its counterpart. The origin of بمصرخي is بمصرخين لي, the plural of muṣrikh; the yāʾ of the plural is quiescent and the yāʾ of annexation is likewise quiescent, so the lām was dropped for lightness and the nūn for annexation, and two quiescent letters met, namely the two yāʾs, so the yāʾ of the plural was assimilated into the yāʾ of annexation; then the yāʾ of annexation was given a fatḥa, seeking lightness and avoiding a succession of three kasras. (إِنِّي كَفَرْتُ بِما أَشْرَكْتُمُونِ مِنْ قَبْلُ): إن and its noun, and the clause كفرت is its predicate; the bāʾ is a preposition; ما is maṣdarī (a maṣdar particle), interpreted with أشركتموني as a maṣdar genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to كفرت, meaning "I disbelieved in your associating me"; it is also possible that it is a relative noun, but the first is better, as we have established; the yāʾ is the object of أشركتموني; ومن قبل is attached to أشركتموني; and the meaning of their associating him with Allah the Exalted will come in the section on Rhetoric. (إِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): إن and its noun; لهم is a fronted predicate; عذاب a delayed mubtadaʾ; أليم an adjective; and the nominal clause is the predicate of إن.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «إني كفرت بما أشركتموني» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): obedience is likened to association (shirk) and placed in its position, because they obeyed him in works of evil as Allah is obeyed in works of good; or because, when they associated idols and the like through their following him in that, it is as if they had associated him, since he was the one who made the worship of idols attractive to them. Then the thing likened was omitted and the thing likened to was kept, in the manner of the explicit derivative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya al-tabaʿiyya).
With the clarity of this metaphor it becomes clear that Satan stood before them on this day in a position that breaks their backs and cuts their hearts, for he made plain to them:
First, that his promises, with which he used to promise them in the world, were false and opposed to the true promise from Allah, Glory be to Him.
Second, that he broke what he had promised them of those promises and fulfilled none of them.
Third, he made clear to them that they had accepted his word on grounds that do not make acceptance obligatory and that no sane mind approves, for lack of the proof that a sane person must have in accepting what another says.
Fourth, he made clear to them that nothing came from him but a bare call devoid of proof, empty of the slightest thing by which the rational hold fast.
Fifth, then he reproached them for what they had fallen into and repelled their blame of him, and commanded them to blame themselves, for they were the ones who accepted pure falsehood whose falsity is not hidden from anyone with the least grasp of reason.
Sixth, he made clear to them that he has no help, no aid, and cannot bring them benefit or ward off harm from them, but is like them in falling into affliction and being unable to be free of this ordeal.
Seventh, then he declared to them that he had disbelieved in what they believed and affirmed of him, so regrets multiplied upon them and calamities followed one another upon them.
And if the sentence «ان الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم» is part of his speech, as some exegetes held, then it is an eighth kind of his speech with which he addressed them.

* Benefits:
The parsing of "Allah created the heavens":
This is an interesting discussion, even if it has no real substance. ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī objected to parsing "Allah created the heavens," "the world" and the like, saying:
"Al-ʿālam (the world) here is a maṣdar, not a direct object, because the direct object is what already existed or on which the agent had some other effect by his act, while the maṣdar is what did not exist but was pure nonexistence, and the agent brings it into being and brings it out from nonexistence to existence by his act. The world in our saying 'Allah created the world' is like that, so it is a maṣdar." It was objected to him that if it were a maṣdar it would be the very act of creating, and that cannot be, for two reasons. One is that we know the world while doubting that it is created by Allah the Exalted, until we know that by a separate proof; so the world is known on this view, while its being created by Him, the Exalted, is not known, since it depends on the proof, and the known is different from what is not known; so creating is other than the world. The second reason is that Allah the Exalted is described by creating, so if creating were the world, Allah would be described by the world, which is not permissible, because it would necessitate describing the eternal by the originated, or the eternity of the world. This is a sophistry with no benefit in it. The truth is that what ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī put forward collapses from its foundation, because the discussion concerns the technical usage of the grammarians, and this terminology concerns only what befalls the ends of words of nominative, accusative and genitive, owing to a word's being described at one time as agent, at another as object, at another as annexed, and so on. So when we say "Allah created the heavens and the earth," we say: these composite, audible words we call in our technical usage a verb, an agent and a direct object; so we made the name of Allah the Exalted nominative as agent, and we made "the heavens and the earth" accusative as objects because the agent's act falls upon them. It does not follow for us from this expression that we have applied to these words that the meaning in the origin has occurred and been newly renewed, because words are indicators of meanings, and the indicator is other than the thing indicated, and the name is other than the named; otherwise the mouth of one who pronounced "fire" would burn, and it would follow that when we say "Allah annihilated the world, and established the Resurrection, and caused Zayd to die," all this had occurred now and been renewed, and we find that false.
We believe that Imam ʿAbd al-Qāhir believed what he put forward to be false, and put it forward only as a fallacy and to display the craft of debate, nothing more.
What puts the direct object in the accusative:
Here we must put forward a fine discussion, namely: what is it that puts the direct object in the accusative?
The school of Sībawayh holds that it is the verb, and for that reason objects are multiple according to the requirement of the verb, for if the verb requires one object it puts it in the accusative, or two it puts both, or three it puts all three. Ibn Hishām said: it is the agent, because it is what affects it in meaning, so it affects it in form.
I say: this is nothing, because the agent can be latent, and the latent does not act upon the overt; and because they divided the verb into intransitive and transitive, which shows that the operation belongs to it.
As for al-Farrāʾ, he chose that the verb and the agent together are what put the object in the accusative, by analogy with the mubtadaʾ and khabar. This is a dispute with no benefit in it; we put forward these theoretical discussions only because they polish the mind and exercise it. And the words of the Exalted refute all of them: «أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة يتيما ...» ("or feeding on a day of hunger an orphan..."), since there is no agent and no verb here; and the discussion of this does not fit in this place.

dervis-irab:7-12.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَأَذَّنَ): He announced (adhina). Its parallels are tawaʿʿada and awʿada ("he threatened"), and tafaḍḍala and afḍala ("he bestowed favour"). The form tafaʿʿala must carry an added meaning that afʿala does not, because of the effort and intensity that are in tafaʿʿul.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ): وإذ is conjoined to نعمة الله عليكم, as if it had been said: "And when Moses said to his people: remember the favour of Allah upon you, and remember when your Lord proclaimed..." It may also be conjoined to إذ أنجاكم. The clause تأذن is the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverbial, and ربكم is the agent of تأذن. The clause لئن شكرتم is the content of an omitted saying, or تأذن is made to run the course of قال because it is a kind of saying, so there is no need to estimate "saying". The lām prepares for an oath, إن is conditional, and شكرتم is the protasis. In لأزيدنكم the lām is the answer to the oath, and the clause لأزيدنكم has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath, while the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath, in accordance with the rule. (وَلَئِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ إِنَّ عَذابِي لَشَدِيدٌ): A clause conjoined to its like. The answer to the oath is omitted, but it is implicitly indicated by His saying «إن عذابي لشديد», that is, "I shall surely punish you". He omitted it here and made it explicit in the case of gratitude because it is the custom of Allah, the Generous, to state the promise plainly and to allude to the threat. إن with its ism and khabar.
(وَقالَ مُوسى إِنْ تَكْفُرُوا أَنْتُمْ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ): وقال موسى is a verb and agent, and the clause إن تكفروا is the content of the saying. إن is conditional, تكفروا is the protasis with the wāw as agent, أنتم is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the wāw, من is conjoined to the wāw, في الأرض is the ṣila of من, and جميعا is a ḥāl. The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ (of the apodosis), إن with its ism, the shifted lām, and حميد is its khabar. (أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَبَؤُا الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ): The hamza is for confirmatory interrogation, لم is a particle of negation, inversion and jussion, يأت is an imperfect verb jussive by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the kāf is a direct object, نبأ is the agent, الذين is a muḍāf ilayhi, and من قبلكم is an adjective. (قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعادٍ وَثَمُودَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ لا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّهُ): قوم is a badal of الذين, نوح is a muḍāf ilayhi, and عاد and ثمود are conjoined. والذين من بعدهم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يعلمهم إلا الله is the khabar; the nominal clause is parenthetical between the explained, which is نبأ الذين من قبلكم, and its explanation, which is جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات. [Translator's note: the Arabic reads «معترضة بن المفسر», which appears to be a misprint for «بين المفسَّر»; the sense is rendered as "between the explained".] It is also permissible for والذين من بعدهم to be conjoined to what precedes it, namely قوم نوح or الذين من قبلكم, and His saying لا يعلمهم إلا الله is then parenthetical. (جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ): A resumptive clause, or a second khabar of الذين; رسلهم is the agent, and بالبينات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاءتهم. (فَرَدُّوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِي أَفْواهِهِمْ وَقالُوا: إِنَّا كَفَرْنا بِما أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; ردوا is a verb and agent, أيديهم is a direct object, and في أفواههم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ردوا or to an omitted ḥāl; a discussion of this expression will come in the section on rhetoric. وقالوا is conjoined to ردوا; إن with its ism; the clause كفرنا is the khabar; بما is attached to كفرنا; the clause أرسلتم is the ṣila, and به is attached to أرسلتم. (وَإِنَّا لَفِي شَكٍّ مِمَّا تَدْعُونَنا إِلَيْهِ مُرِيبٍ): وإنا is conjoined to the preceding إنا; إن and its ism, the shifted lām, and في شك is the khabar; مما is attached to شك or is an adjective of it; the clause تدعوننا is the ṣila, and إليه is attached to تدعوننا; and مريب is an adjective of شك. (قالَتْ رُسُلُهُمْ أَفِي اللَّهِ شَكٌّ): A resumptive clause built on an implied question that the context calls for, as if it had been said: "What then did their messengers say?" and the answer was that they said, in denial. The interrogative hamza is for denial of their foolish statement; في الله is a fronted khabar and شك is a postponed mubtadaʾ. It has also been said that شك is the agent of «أفي الله», because of its reliance on the interrogative, and this is preferred by the early grammarians and all the parsers, so that it should not be necessary, on the first view, to separate the adjective from the described by a foreign element, which is the mubtadaʾ, unlike the agent, which is like a part of its governor. The truth is that all of this has no basis, and the first view is the right one.
(فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَدْعُوكُمْ لِيَغْفِرَ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ): فاطر is an adjective of الله or a badal of it; the clause يدعوكم is a ḥāl clause, that is, "while He calls you to faith in His sending us". The lām is causal; يغفر is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يدعوكم; and من ذنوبكم is attached to يغفر, and it is in the sense of partitive "some". Al-Zamakhsharī said in al-Kashshāf: "If you ask what the meaning of the partitive is in His saying «من ذنوبكم», I say: I have not known it to occur except thus in addressing unbelievers", so as not to equate them with the believers. Al-Rāzī said: "As for the statement of the author of al-Kashshāf that the intention is to distinguish the address to the believer from the address to the unbeliever, it is among the calamities, because if this partition occurs, there is no need to mention the answer, and if it does not occur, this speech is invalid." Some said it is for substitution, that is, "in place of the punishment of your sins"; it is also possible that يغفر is made to include the meaning of "frees", that is, "frees you from your sins". Abū ʿUbayda preferred its being redundant (zāʾida), following al-Akhfash, who allows its redundancy in the affirmative. (وَيُؤَخِّرَكُمْ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى): ويؤخركم is conjoined to يغفر; إلى أجل is attached to يؤخركم, and مسمى is an adjective of أجل. (قالُوا: إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنا): إن is negative, أنتم is a mubtadaʾ, إلا is a particle of restriction, بشر is the khabar, and مثلنا is an adjective.
(تُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَصُدُّونا عَمَّا كانَ يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا): The clause تريدون is a second adjective of بشر, or it is resumptive; تريدون is a verb and agent; أن and what is within its scope is the object of تريدون; عما is attached to تصدونا; the clause كان is a ṣila, the clause يعبد is the khabar of كان, and آباؤنا is the agent of يعبد. (فَأْتُونا بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ): The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ faṣīḥa); ائتونا is an imperative verb, agent and direct object; بسلطان is attached to أتونا, and مبين is an adjective. (قالَتْ لَهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ إِنْ نَحْنُ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ): قالت لهم رسلهم is a verb and agent, ولهم is attached to قالت; إن is negative, نحن is a mubtadaʾ, إلا is a particle of restriction, بشر is the khabar, and مثلكم is an adjective. (وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَمُنُّ عَلى مَنْ يَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ): The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a conjunction; لكن with its ism, and the clause يمن is its khabar; على من is attached to يمن, the clause يشاء is a ṣila, and من عباده is a ḥāl. (وَما كانَ لَنا أَنْ نَأْتِيَكُمْ بِسُلْطانٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): The wāw is a conjunction, كان is a defective past verb, ولنا is the fronted khabar of كان, and أن with its scope, interpreted as a maṣdar, is the postponed ism of كان; بسلطان is attached to نأتيكم, إلا is a particle of restriction, and بإذن الله is a ḥāl, that is, "bound up with the permission of Allah". (وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ): The wāw is a conjunction; وعلى الله is attached to يتوكل; the fāʾ is also a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; يتوكل is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command; and المؤمنون is the agent of يتوكل. (وَما لَنا أَلَّا نَتَوَكَّلَ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدانا سُبُلَنا): The wāw is a conjunction; ما is interrogative, and the interrogative here means negation, that is, "there is nothing to prevent us and no excuse we could cling to". It is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and لنا is the khabar; أن and what is within its scope is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, that is, the preposition and its genitive noun, and it is accusative by removal of the preposition. The wāw is circumstantial, qad is a particle of confirmation, هدانا is a verb, latent agent and direct object, and سبلنا is accusative by removal of the preposition. The meaning is: "while He has guided us and done for us what requires and calls for trust in Him, in that He guided us to our ways", that is, He guided each of us to his path and course. (وَلَنَصْبِرَنَّ عَلى ما آذَيْتُمُونا): The wāw is a conjunction, the lām is the answer to an omitted oath, and نصبرن is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; in على ما, على is a preposition and ما is maṣdarī (verbal-noun forming); آذيتمونا is a verb, agent and object, and the wāw is for prolongation (ishbāʿ). It is also possible for ما to be relative, that is, "for that by which you have harmed us". (وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ): Its parsing has been given before. The command to trust was repeated because the first is for initiating trust and the second for establishing it.

* Rhetoric:
The "returning of the hands into the mouths" in His saying «فردوا أيديهم في أفواههم», biting the fingertips and gnashing the molars, is a metonymy for rage and vexation at the occurrence of what the soul dislikes and does not want. Abū ʿUbayda said: it is a proverb, that is, they did not believe and did not respond; the Arabs say of a man when he refrains from answering and falls silent:
"He has returned his hand to his mouth." Al-Akhfash said the same. Al-Qutaybī objected to this, saying: no one has heard any of the Arabs say "he returned his hand to his mouth" for one who abandons what he was commanded. It was also said that what is meant by returning the hands into the mouths here is laughter and mockery, like one overcome by laughter who puts his hand on his mouth. It was said too that what is meant by "hands" and "mouths" is something other than the two bodily organs: it was said that the "hands" are favours, and the meaning is that they rejected what, had they accepted it, would have been a favour to them (one says "so-and-so has a yad with me", meaning a favour), and that the "mouths" are their denial of the messengers, so the meaning is that they denied with their mouths and rejected their words. There are other opinions which we have passed over, because the strongest view is the first: for their driving the messengers to despair of their believing, in word and deed, by putting the hand in the mouth, is what suits their envy in unbelief; and the opening of the wording with the emphatic particle, and the facing of the messengers with the pronoun of address and repeating it, as an intensification of emphasis, indicate their complete despair.

dervis-irab:23-27.t:
* I'rab:
(وَأُدْخِلَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها): After explaining the states of the wretched disbelievers, He began to explain the states of the fortunate believers. وأدخل is a passive past verb; الذين is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); وعملوا is conjoined to آمنوا, and it is a verb and an agent; الصالحات is a direct object; جنات is a second direct object by extension (ʿalā l-ittisāʿ); and the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is an adjective of جنات. (بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ تَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيها سَلامٌ): بإذن: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أدخل; ربهم is annexed to إذن; وتحيتهم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); فيها is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and سلام is the khabar (predicate) of تحيتهم. (أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا): The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb jussive by لم, and its agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; and ضرب الله مثلا is a verb, an agent and a direct object, and the ḥāl is from the direct object. (كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ أَصْلُها ثابِتٌ وَفَرْعُها فِي السَّماءِ): كلمة is a badal (substitute) of مثلا, or it is accusative by an omitted verb, meaning "He made a good word"; or, by including in ضرب the meaning of "made" (jaʿala), it becomes a second direct object; كشجرة is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, meaning "it is like a good tree"; طيبة is an adjective of شجرة; أصلها is a mubtadaʾ and ثابت the khabar, and the clause is a second adjective of شجرة; and وفرعها في السماء is conjoined to أصلها ثابت. It is also possible that His words كشجرة are a second adjective of كلمة طيبة.
(تُؤْتِي أُكُلَها كُلَّ حِينٍ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّها): The clause is a third adjective of شجرة; تؤتي is an imperfect verb and the agent is latent, its implied form being "she"; أكلها is a direct object; كل حين is an adverbial (ẓarf) attached to تؤتي, and an account of the good tree will come; and بإذن ربها is attached to تؤتي or to something omitted as a ḥāl, meaning "connected with the permission of its Lord." (وَيَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثالَ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ): ويضرب الله الأمثال: an imperfect verb, an agent and a direct object; وللناس is attached to يضرب; لعل and its noun; and the clause يتذكرون is its predicate.
(وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ اجْتُثَّتْ مِنْ فَوْقِ الْأَرْضِ ما لَها مِنْ قَرارٍ): ومثل is a mubtadaʾ; كلمة is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive complement); خبيثة is an adjective; كشجرة is the khabar of مثل; خبيثة is an adjective; the clause اجتثت من فوق الأرض is a second adjective of شجرة; the clause مالها من قرار is a third adjective of شجرة; ما is the negative, Ḥijāzī or Tamīmī; لها is a fronted predicate; من is redundant; and قرار is a delayed mubtadaʾ, or the delayed noun of ما. (يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ): A resumptive clause, set forth to establish the state of each of those meant by the two preceding likenesses; يثبت is an imperfect verb; الله is the agent; الذين is the direct object; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila; بالقول is attached to يثبت; الثابت is an adjective (naʿt) of القول; and في الحياة الدنيا is a ḥāl. (وَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ الظَّالِمِينَ وَيَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ): ويضل الله الظالمين: a verb, an agent and a direct object; ويفعل الله ما يشاء: a verb, an agent and a direct object; and the clause يشاء is the ṣila.

* Rhetoric:
1- The simile of representation (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī) in likening the good word, which is described by three attributes, one of which is the yielding of its fruit "at every time," that is, from the time it is eaten until the time it ends. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: it is the date palm, because its fruit is eaten always, by night and by day, in summer and in winter: its pith (jumār), its spathe (ṭalʿ), its unripe dates (balaḥ), its half-ripe dates (busr), its part-ripe dates (munaṣṣaf) and its fresh dates (ruṭab) are eaten, and after that the dry dates (tamr) are eaten until the time of the fresh ones; so eating from it is continuous at every time. On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said one day: "Allah has made the likeness of the believer a tree, so tell me what it is." The people fell to thinking of the trees of the desert, and I was a boy, and it occurred to my heart that it was the date palm, but I was shy before the Messenger of Allah to say it, being the youngest of the people. It is reported: "ʿUmar's presence prevented me from saying it, and I was ashamed." Then ʿUmar said to me: "My son, had you said it, it would have been dearer to me than red camels." The point of likeness in representing faith by a tree is that a tree is not a tree except through three things: a firm root, a standing trunk and a high branch. So too faith is not complete except through three things: affirmation by the heart, speech by the tongue and action by the limbs. The existence of the three attributes on the side of the thing compared to is sensory, while on the side of the thing compared it is abstract.
2- A simile of representation also in likening the evil word to the evil tree, which is not firm, as if it had been uprooted, or as if it had been cast on the surface of the earth, so it does not sink into the ground but its roots lie on the surface of the earth, and it has no branches that stretch upward to the sky; and this is the meaning of His words «ما لها من قرار».
3- Intellectual metaphor (majāz ʿaqlī) in His words «تؤتي أكلها»: the act of giving is attributed to other than its true agent, because the date palm does not give the fruit, in the manner of the words of al-Ṣaltān al-ʿAbdī:
أشاب الصغير وأفنى الكبير كر الغداة ومرّ العشي
("The return of the morning and the passing of the evening turned the young grey and made the old perish.")
The metaphor occurs in the affirmation of greying as an act of the return of the morning and the passing of the evening, while in truth it is the act of Allah the Exalted.

dervis-irab:28-34.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْبَوارِ): Perdition. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "bāra al-shayʾ yabūru būran (with ḍamma) means 'it perished,' and bāra al-shayʾ bawāran means 'it stagnated (kasada),' by way of metaphor, because when a thing is left it becomes of no use, so it resembles what has perished in this respect." In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: "Al-būr (with fatḥa on the bāʾ):
land before it is fit for sowing, or land that is left fallow for a year to be sown the next; also al-ikhtibār, like al-ibtiyār; and perdition (halāk), 'Allah destroyed him' (abārahu Allāh); and slackness of the market is like al-bawār in both [senses], and the plural of bāʾir. With ḍamma (būr): the corrupt man, and the one who has perished, in whom there is no good; the dual, the plural and the feminine are the same in it; and land that has lain fallow and not been cultivated, like al-bāʾir and al-bāʾira." In al-Asās: "'So-and-so has its light and upon you is its būr,' that is, its perdition; 'a people of būr'; 'they took up residence in the abode of perdition (dār al-bawār)'; and 'Bawār came down upon the disbelievers.' Abū Mikʿat al-Asadī said:
قتلت فكان تظالما وتباغيا ... إن التظالم في الصديق بوار
("You were killed, so it was mutual wrongdoing and aggression; wronging a friend is perdition.")
لو كان أول ما أتيت تهارشت ... أولاد عرج عليك عند وجار
("Had it been the first time you came, the sons of ʿAraj would have swarmed upon you at a den.")
He made it a proper name for hyenas, so definiteness and femininity combined. And among the figurative usages: bārat al-bayyiʿāt, 'sales went slack,' and 'a slack market (sūq bāʾira),' and bārat al-ayyim, when widows are not desired; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge from the slackness of widows (bawār al-ayyim); and bārat al-arḍ, when the land is not sown, 'barren land' (arḍ bawār) and 'barren lands' (arāḍūn būr)."
(يَصْلَوْنَها): They enter it. In al-Miṣbāḥ: ṣaliya bi-l-nār and ṣaliyahā ṣaliyan, of the pattern taʿiba, means "he felt its heat"; al-ṣalāʾ, of the pattern kitāb, is the heat of fire; and ṣalaytu al-laḥm aṣlīhi, of the pattern ramā, means "I roasted the meat."
(خِلالٌ): mukhālla, that is, friendship. So al-Zamakhsharī, al-Jalāl and others explained it, which implies that it is singular. In al-Qurṭubī: it is the plural of khulla (with ḍamma), like qulla and qilāl. In al-Asās there is what supports its being singular; he says: "He is my khalīl, my khill and my khulla; they are my akhillāʾ and khillān; and between us is an old khulla; and I befriended him, mukhālla and khilāl." And what supports its being a plural, he says: "This is a good khulla, and in him are good khilāl."

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ بَدَّلُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ كُفْراً وَأَحَلُّوا قَوْمَهُمْ دارَ الْبَوارِ): The hamza is for the interrogative of wonder, meaning "do you not marvel at the doing of these disbelievers, which does not issue from anyone with the least understanding?" لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; إلى الذين is attached to تر; the clause بدلوا is the ṣila; نعمة الله is a second direct object, because it is the one which the preposition enters, meaning "with the favour of Allah," and كفرا is the first object. Abū Ḥayyān said: "Al-Ḥawfī and Abū l-Baqāʾ claimed that كفرا is the second object of بدلوا, and that is not correct, because baddala is among the sisters of ikhtāra, so what the preposition directly touches is the second object, and what the verb reaches by itself, not by means of a preposition, is the first object." وأحلوا is conjoined to بدلوا; قومهم is the first direct object and دار البوار the second direct object. (جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَها وَبِئْسَ الْقَرارُ): جهنم is a badal or ʿaṭf bayān of دار البوار, or accusative by an omitted verb that what follows explains, meaning "they enter Hell"; the clause يصلونها is a ḥāl on the first view and explicative on the second; the wāw is of ḥāl; وبئس القرار: a verb and an agent, and the specified one of blame is omitted, meaning "it." (وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنْداداً لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ): The wāw is a conjunction; وجعلوا: a verb and an agent; ولله is in the position of accusative as a second direct object of جعلوا; and أندادا is the first direct object; you may also attach لله to something omitted as a ḥāl. Regarding ليضلوا, it is said that the lām is the lām of consequence ('āqiba) or of becoming (ṣayrūra); and it is said to be on its proper footing as the lām of cause, but that is not a real aim of theirs in taking rivals; rather, since it is the result of it, it was likened to an aim and the lām was brought upon it by way of derivative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tabaʿiyya); and يضلوا is accusative by an implied أن after the lām of consequence or of cause, and the wāw is the agent; and عن سبيله is attached to يضلوا. (قُلْ تَمَتَّعُوا فَإِنَّ مَصِيرَكُمْ إِلَى النَّارِ): قل is an imperative verb; the clause تمتعوا is the content of what was said; تمتعوا is an imperative verb and its agent; فإن: the fāʾ is of reason; إن and its noun; and إلى النار is its predicate. (قُلْ لِعِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ): Most parsers agreed that the content of what was said is omitted, indicated by its answer (jawāb), meaning "Say to them: Establish the prayer and spend." What some objected to this view will come in the section on Rhetoric. الذين is an adjective of عبادي; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila; and يقيموا is jussive as the answer to the imperative, meaning "if you say to them 'Establish the prayer and spend,' etc., they will establish the prayer and spend." They also allowed that يقيموا and ينفقوا mean ليقيموا and لينفقوا, so both are jussive by the lām of command and this is the content of what was said; an interesting discussion on this will come in the section on Rhetoric. الصلاة is the direct object.
The wording of Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī: "The majority hold that the jussive in the verse, that is, «قل لعبادي», is like your saying 'Come to me, I will honour you.' There are three views on this:
1- The first, of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, is that it is by the request itself, because of the meaning of the conditional إن it includes, just as the conditional nouns are jussive for that reason.
2- The second, of al-Sīrāfī and al-Fārisī, is that it is by the request, because it stands in the place of the jussive-causing element, which is the implied condition, just as the accusative in ضربا in your saying ضربا زيدا is because it stands in for أضرب, and not because it includes its meaning.
3- The third, of the majority, is that it is by an implied condition after the request, and this is stronger than the first, because omission and inclusion, though both share in being contrary to the original, yet in inclusion there is a change of the original meaning and not so in omission; also, the inclusion in a verb of the meaning of a particle is either not found or not frequent; and from the second, because the substitute of a thing conveys its meaning, and the request does not convey the meaning of a condition. Ibn Mālik invalidated, by the verse, that the jussive could be in the answer of an implied condition, because supposing it would necessitate that no one to whom that is said should fail to comply, whereas failure occurs. His son answered that the ruling is ascribed to them in general terms, not to every individual, so it is possible that the original was 'most of them establish,' then the muḍāf was dropped and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, so it became nominative and joined to the verb; and by the possibility that the servants described as having faith are not meant absolutely, but rather the sincere among them, and every sincere believer to whom the Messenger said 'establish the prayer' established it. Al-Mubarrad said: the implied form is 'Say to them: Establish, they will establish,' and the jussive is in the answer to the implied 'Establish,' not in the answer to 'Say.' This is refuted by the fact that the answer must differ from what it answers, either in verb and agent, as in 'Come to me, I will honour you,' or in the verb, as in 'Accept Islam, you will enter Paradise,' or in the agent, as in 'Stand, I will stand'; it is not permissible for them to agree in both; moreover, the implied imperative is for the second person and يقيموا is for the third person. It is also said that يقيموا is indeclinable (mabnī) because it takes the place of أقيموا, which is indeclinable, and that is nothing. The Kufans and Abū l-Ḥasan claimed that the lām of request was dropped with consistent omission in such as قم and اقعد, and that the origin is لتقم and لتقعد, so the lām was dropped for lightness and the imperfect prefix followed it; and by their statement I say: because the imperative is a meaning, its due is to be conveyed by a particle; because it is the brother of prohibition, which is indicated only by a particle; because the verb was set down only to limit the event by the realised time, and its being a command or a report is outside its purpose; and because they have pronounced that origin, as in the verse «لتقم أنت يا ابن خير قريش» ('Let you rise, O son of the best of Quraysh')."
(وَيُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلانِيَةً): وينفقوا is conjoined to يقيموا; ومما رزقناهم is attached to ينفقوا; and سرا وعلانية are accusative as a ḥāl, meaning "possessing secrecy and possessing openness," in the sense of "doing so secretly and openly"; or as a maṣdar, meaning "spending of secrecy and openness"; or as an adverbial, meaning "at times of secrecy and openness"; or by removal of the preposition, meaning "in secret and in public." (مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلا خِلالٌ): من قبل is attached to ينفقوا; أن and what falls in its scope is a maṣdar annexed to قبل; يوم is the agent of يأتي; لا is the lā of generic negation, disregarded because it is repeated, as in لا حول ولا قوة, and the views on it have already preceded; بيع is a mubtadaʾ and فيه the khabar; and ولا خلال is conjoined to لا بيع.
