﴿وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون﴾: the واو is a conjunction; ﴿على الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يتوكل﴾; the فاء is also a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; يتوكل is an imperfect verb made jussive by the lām of command; المؤمنون is the fāʿil of يتوكل.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وما لنا ألا نتوكل على الله﴾: the واو is a conjunction; ما is interrogative, in the position of nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); أن together with what falls in its scope is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿على الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نتوكل﴾.
﴿وقد هدانا سبلنا﴾: the واو is for the ḥāl; قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); هدانا is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); سبلنا is accusative by removal of the preposition.
﴿ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا﴾: the واو is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; ﴿نصبرن﴾ is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; ﴿على ما﴾: على is a preposition, and ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya; آذيتمونا is a verb, its fāʿil and its object, the واو being for lengthening (ishbāʿ); it is also said that ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun, i.e. "for that with which you have harmed us".
﴿وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون﴾: the واو is a conjunction; ﴿على الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يتوكل﴾; the فاء is also a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; ﴿يتوكل﴾ is an imperfect verb made jussive by the lām of command; المتوكلون is the fāʿil of يتوكل.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿وقال الذين كفروا لرسلهم لنخرجنكم من أرضنا﴾: ﴿قال الذين﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; ﴿لرسلهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قال﴾; the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath; نخرجنكم is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿من أرضنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نخرجنكم﴾; the clause is the speech reported by the verb "said" (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿أو لتعودن في ملتنا﴾: أو is a conjunction meaning إلا (unless); لتعودن is conjoined to نخرجنكم, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters; the واو of the plural, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil; the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; ﴿في ملتنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿تعودن﴾, or it is its khabar (predicate).
﴿فأوحى إليهم ربهم لنهلكن الظالمين﴾: the فاء is a conjunction; أوحى إليهم ربهم is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿لنهلكن﴾: the lām is the answer to the omitted oath. ﴿نهلكن الظالمين﴾ is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. The clause ﴿لنهلكن الظالمين﴾ is the answer to an implied oath, with no grammatical position. The oath and its answer form an explicative clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿ولنسكننكم الأرض من بعدهم﴾: the واو is a conjunction; نسكننكم is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الأرض is accusative by removal of the preposition, or a mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); ﴿من بعدهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نسكننكم﴾; it is also said to be a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد﴾: ذلك is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لمن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); the clause خاف is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو"; ﴿مقامي﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi; خاف is a past verb; وعيد is the mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the first-person ياء, which is dropped to observe the verse endings (fawāṣil).

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿واستفتحوا﴾: the واو is a conjunction; استفتحوا is a past verb meaning "they sought victory", and the واو is the fāʿil (agent); the pronoun refers to the messengers; it is also said to refer to the unbelievers.
﴿وخاب كل جبار عنيد﴾: the واو is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; خاب كل جبار is a verb and its fāʿil; عنيد is an adjective (ṣifa) of جبار.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t: ﴿من ورائه جهنم ويسقى من ماء صديد﴾: ﴿من ورائه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, advanced khabar (predicate); جهنم is the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is a second adjective (ṣifa) of جبار; ﴿ويسقى﴾: the واو conjoins to something implied; يسقى is an imperfect verb in the passive (built on the form whose agent is not named); ﴿من ماء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يسقى﴾; صديد is a badal (substitute) from ماء, or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it; it is also said to be a naʿt (adjective) of ماء, and it is also said to be a naʿt with the particle of comparison dropped, the implied form being "مثل صديد" (like pus); the clause يسقى is conjoined to something omitted, its implied form being: "behind him is Hell, in which he meets what he meets, of severe water distinguished from its punishment" [Translator's note: so in the source: ماء شديد يتميز عن عذابها].

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه﴾: the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of ماء; يتجرعه is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); it is also said that the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿ولا﴾: the واو is a conjunction, and لا is negative; ﴿يكاد﴾ is one of the verbs of approximation (afʿāl al-muqāraba), and its noun is latent, its implied form being "هو"; the clause ﴿يسيغه﴾ is the khabar (predicate).
﴿ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان﴾: the واو is a conjunction; يأتيه الموت is a verb, a delayed fāʿil and an advanced object; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted that is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "the causes of death come to him, surrounding him from all sides".
﴿وما هو بميت ومن ورائه عذاب غليظ﴾: the واو is for the ḥāl; ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negative particle, operating like ليس; ﴿هو﴾ is the noun of ما; ﴿بميت﴾: the باء is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition, and ﴿ميت﴾ is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative by position and genitive in form by the باء; ﴿من ورائه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, advanced khabar; عذاب is the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); غليظ is an adjective of عذاب.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿مثل الذين كفروا بربهم أعمالهم كرماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف﴾: مثل الذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "and among what is narrated to you is the likeness"; the clause ﴿كفروا بربهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; أعمالهم is a mubtadaʾ, and the كاف is the khabar, meaning مثل (like), or it is a particle that, with its genitive noun, is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. It is also said: ﴿مثل﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, أعمالهم a second mubtadaʾ, and ﴿كرماد﴾ the khabar of the second, the second with its khabar being the khabar of the first. It is also said: ﴿مثل﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, أعمالهم is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from it, and ﴿كرماد﴾ is the khabar of ﴿مثل﴾ and ﴿أعمالهم﴾ together. The clause اشتدت به الريح is an adjective (ṣifa) of رماد; ﴿في يوم عاصف﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿اشتدت﴾; it is also said to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الريح.
﴿لا يقدرون مما كسبوا على شيء﴾: the clause is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of كفروا; يقدرون is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿مما كسبوا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from ﴿شيء﴾; ﴿على شيء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يقدرون﴾; the clause كسبوا is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿ذلك هو الضلال البعيد﴾: ذلك is a mubtadaʾ; ﴿هو﴾ is a second mubtadaʾ; الضلال is the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ, the second with its khabar being the khabar of the first; ﴿البعيد﴾ is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿ألم تر أن الله خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, inversion (of tense) and jussive; ﴿تر﴾ is an imperfect verb made jussive by ﴿لم﴾; أن together with what falls in its scope takes the place of the two objects of ﴿تر﴾; السماوات is the object of خلق; ﴿بالحق﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلق, the باء being causal, or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), the باء being for accompaniment (muṣāḥaba).
﴿إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد﴾: إن is conditional; يشأ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿يذهبكم﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the كاف is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); يأت is conjoined to يذهبكم; ﴿بخلق﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يأت﴾; جديد is an adjective (ṣifa).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض﴾: ﴿الله﴾ is a badal (substitute) from, or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to, العزيز الحميد; ﴿الذي﴾ is its adjective (ṣifa); ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, advanced khabar (predicate); ﴿ما﴾ is the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي, with no grammatical position; ﴿في السماوات﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿وما في الأرض﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ما في السماوات﴾.
﴿وويل للكافرين من عذاب شديد﴾: ويل is the mubtadaʾ, and the clause is one of imprecation (duʿāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿للكافرين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; ﴿من﴾ is explicative (bayāniyya), and ﴿من عذاب﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ويل﴾; or ﴿من﴾ is for making transitive (taʿdiya), and ﴿من عذاب﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿ويل﴾; شديد is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿وما ذلك على الله بعزيز﴾: the واو: a conjunction, or for the ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negative particle, operating like ليس; ﴿ذلك﴾ is the noun of ما; ﴿على الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عزيز﴾; ﴿بعزيز﴾: the باء is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition, and ﴿عزيز﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative by position and genitive in form by the باء.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿وبرزوا لله جميعا﴾: the واو is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; برزوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿برزوا﴾; جميعًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿فقال الضعفاء للذين استكبروا﴾: the فاء is a conjunction; ﴿قال الضعفاء﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿للذين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿قال﴾; the clause استكبروا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position.
﴿إنا كنا لكم تبعا﴾: إنّا: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause ﴿إنا﴾ is the speech reported by the verb "said" (maqūl al-qawl); كنا is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause ﴿كنا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إن; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; تبعًا is the khabar of كنا.
﴿فهل أنتم مغنون عنا من عذاب الله من شيء﴾: the فاء is a conjunction; هل is an interrogative particle; أنتم is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and مغنون the khabar; ﴿عنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿مغنون﴾; ﴿من عذاب الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the second ﴿مِن﴾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant); شيء is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by position, genitive in form by من.
﴿قالوا لو هدانا الله لهديناكم سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا﴾: قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil; لو is a particle of non-occurrence (imtināʿ); ﴿هدانا الله﴾ is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi and its fāʿil; ﴿لهديناكم﴾: the lām occurs in the answer of the condition, and هديناكم is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿سواء﴾ is the advanced khabar; ﴿أجزعنا﴾ is the delayed mubtadaʾ, because it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), since the hamza is for equalization (taswiya) and the verb after it is interpreted as a maṣdar; أم is a connected (muttaṣila) conjunction; صبرنا is conjoined to جزعنا.
﴿ما لنا من محيص﴾: ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿لنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, advanced khabar; ﴿مِن﴾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; ﴿محيص﴾ is the delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative by position and genitive in form by ﴿مِن﴾.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿وقال الشيطان لما قضي الأمر﴾: the واو is a conjunction; قال الشيطان is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); لما is adverbial, temporal (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya), or a linking particle (rābiṭa); ﴿قضي الأمر﴾ is a verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is in the position of genitive through the annexation of the adverb to it, or has no grammatical position.
﴿إن الله وعدكم وعد الحق﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the Name of Majesty is its noun, and the clause ﴿وعدكم﴾ is its khabar (predicate); ﴿وعد﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and الحق is the muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿إن الله﴾ is the speech reported by the verb "said" (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿ووعدتكم فأخلفتكم﴾: the واو is a conjunction; وعدتكم is conjoined to وعدكم; فأخلفتكم is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is conjoined to وعدتكم.
﴿وما كان لي عليكم من سلطان إلا أن دعوتكم فاستجبتم لي﴾: the واو is a conjunction; ما is negative; كان is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb; ﴿لي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted, advanced khabar; ﴿عليكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective (ṣifa) of سلطان; من is a preposition, and سلطان is genitive in form and the noun of كان by position; إلا is a particle of exception; أن together with what falls in its scope is the excepted (mustathnā); فاستجبتم is conjoined to دعوتكم; ﴿لي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿استجبتم﴾.
﴿فلا تلوموني ولوموا أنفسكم﴾: the فاء is the فاء of eloquence (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), as though it were said: "If you know that you hastened to answer me, then you are the ones to blame"; لا is the prohibitive lā; تلوموني is an imperfect verb made jussive by the prohibitive لا; the واو is the fāʿil, the نون is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the ياء is the mafʿūl bihi; لوموا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; أنفسكم is the mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ما أنا بمصرخكم وما أنتم بمصرخي﴾: ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negative particle, operating like ليس; ﴿أنا﴾ is the noun of ما; ﴿بمصرخكم﴾: the باء is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition, and ﴿مصرخكم﴾ is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative by position and genitive in form by the باء; ﴿وما أنتم بمصرخي﴾ is conjoined to its counterpart.
﴿إني كفرت بما أشركتمون من قبل﴾: إن is an abrogating particle, the ياء is its noun, and the clause كفرت is its khabar; the باء is a preposition, and ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with ﴿أشركتموني﴾ as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the باء; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿كفرت﴾, i.e. "I disbelieve in your associating me [with Allah]"; it is also said that it is a relative noun; the ياء is the object of ﴿أشركتموني﴾; ﴿من قبل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أشركتموني﴾.
﴿إن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم﴾: إن is an abrogating particle, and الظالمين is its noun; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, advanced khabar; عذاب is the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); أليم is an adjective; the nominal clause is the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿وأدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها﴾: the واو is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; أدخل is a past verb in the passive (built on the form whose agent is not named); الذين is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; عملوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿عملوا﴾ is conjoined to آمنوا; الصالحات is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); جنات is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause ﴿تجري من تحتها الأنهار﴾ is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿جنات﴾.
﴿بإذن ربهم تحيتهم فيها سلام﴾: ﴿بإذن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أدخل﴾; ﴿ربهم﴾ is the muḍāf ilayhi; تحيتهم is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿فيها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); سلام is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿تحيتهم﴾.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿ألم تر كيف ضرب الله مثلا﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, inversion (of tense) and jussive; ﴿تر﴾ is an imperfect verb made jussive by ﴿لم﴾, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت"; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of ضرب; ﴿ضرب الله مثلًا﴾ is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿كلمة طيبة كشجرة طيبة﴾: كلمة is a badal (substitute) from ﴿مثلًا﴾, or a second mafʿūl bihi through ضرب implicitly carrying the meaning of جعل (make); ﴿كشجرة﴾: the كاف is a noun meaning مثل (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is like a good tree"; شجرة: muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿طيبة﴾ is an adjective (ṣifa) of شجرة.
﴿أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء﴾: ﴿أصلها﴾ is the mubtadaʾ and ثابت its khabar, and the clause is a second adjective of شجرة; ﴿فرعها في السماء﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أصلها ثابت﴾.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿تؤتي أكلها كل حين بإذن ربها﴾: the clause is a third adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿شجرة﴾; تؤتي is an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هي"; أكلها is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿كل حين﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تؤتي﴾; ﴿بإذن ربها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿تؤتي﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "clothed with the permission of its Lord".
﴿ويضرب الله الأمثال للناس لعلهم يتذكرون﴾: the واو is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; يضرب الله الأمثال is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿للناس﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يضرب﴾; لعل is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the هاء is its noun, and the clause ﴿يتذكرون﴾ is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:26-26.t: ﴿ومثل كلمة خبيثة كشجرة خبيثة اجتثت من فوق الأرض ما لها من قرار﴾: the واو is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿مثل﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿كلمة﴾ is the muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿خبيثة﴾ is an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿كشجرة﴾: the كاف is a noun meaning مِثل (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; شجرة: muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿خبيثة﴾ is an adjective; the clause ﴿اجتثت من فوق الأرض﴾ is a second adjective of شجرة; ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿لها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, advanced khabar; ﴿مِن﴾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; ﴿قرار﴾ is the delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative by position and genitive in form by ﴿مِن﴾; the clause ﴿ما لها من قرار﴾ is a third adjective of شجرة.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; يثبت is an imperfect verb, ﴿الله﴾ is the fāʿil (agent), and الذين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; ﴿بالقول﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يثبت﴾; الثابت is a naʿt (adjective) of القول; ﴿في الحياة الدنيا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ويضل الله الظالمين ويفعل الله ما يشاء﴾: ﴿ويضل الله الظالمين﴾ is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿ويفعل الله ما يشاء﴾ is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause يشاء is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمت الله كفرا﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of wonder (istifhām taʿajjubī); لم is a particle of negation, inversion (of tense) and jussive; ﴿إلى الذين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تر﴾; the clause بدلوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; نعمة الله is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and ﴿كفرًا﴾ the second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وأحلوا قومهم دار البوار﴾: أحلوا is conjoined to بدلوا; قومهم is the first mafʿūl bihi, and دار البوار the second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿جهنم يصلونها﴾: جهنم is a badal (substitute) from, or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to, ﴿دار البوار﴾, and the clause ﴿يصلونها﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; or ﴿جهنم﴾ is accusative by an omitted verb indicated by what follows it, i.e. "they will burn in Hell", and the clause ﴿يصلونها﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from His words ﴿قومهم﴾ in the preceding ayah, or explicative of an implied verb that makes جهنم accusative, and so has no grammatical position, the implied form being: "they will burn in Hell, they will burn in it".
﴿وبئس القرار﴾: the واو is for the ḥāl; بئس is a rigid (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; القرار is the fāʿil (agent), nominative; the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "هي" (it).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿الذين يستحبون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة﴾: الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of الكافرين, or a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the coming clause ﴿أولئك في ضلال بعيد﴾, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who prefer"; the clause ﴿يستحبون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; الحياة is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and الدنيا an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿على الآخرة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يستحبون﴾.
﴿ويصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا﴾: the واو is a conjunction; يصدون is conjoined to يستحبون; ﴿عن سبيل الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يصدون﴾; يبغونها is conjoined to يصدون; يبغون is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿ها﴾ is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "يبغون لها" (they seek for it); عوجًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the هاء in ﴿يبغونها﴾.
﴿أولئك في ضلال بعيد﴾: the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ; ﴿في ضلال﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar; بعيد is an adjective of ضلال.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿وجعلوا لله أندادا ليضلوا عن سبيله﴾: the واو is a conjunction; جعلوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted that is accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of جعلوا, and أندادًا is the first mafʿūl bihi; or ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿ليضلوا﴾: the lām is the lām of consequence (ʿāqiba), or of outcome (ṣayrūra); it is also said to be the lām of reason (taʿlīl); يضلوا is accusative by an implied أن after the lām of consequence or the lām of reason; the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from أن and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جعلوا; the واو is the fāʿil; ﴿عن سبيله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يضلوا﴾.
﴿قل تمتعوا﴾: ﴿قل﴾ is an imperative verb; the clause ﴿تمتعوا﴾ is the speech reported by the verb "say" (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿تمتعوا﴾ is an imperative verb and its fāʿil.
﴿فإن مصيركم إلى النار﴾: the فاء is for giving a reason (taʿlīl); إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); مصيركم is its noun; ﴿إلى النار﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وما أرسلنا من رسول إلا بلسان قومه ليبين لهم﴾: the واو is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; أرسلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); من is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant); رسول is genitive in form, accusative by position as the object; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿بلسان قومه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "clothed with the tongue of his people", so it is an exception from the most general of states; ﴿ليبين﴾: the lām is for giving a reason (taʿlīl), and ﴿يبين﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of reason; the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from أن and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أرسلنا; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يبين﴾.
﴿فيضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء﴾: the فاء is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; يضل is an imperfect verb, nominative because of resumption; ﴿يضل الله﴾ is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; ﴿مَن﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿يشاء﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿ويهدي من يشاء﴾ is conjoined to ﴿يضل الله من يشاء﴾.
﴿وهو العزيز الحكيم﴾: ﴿هو﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); العزيز is the first khabar (predicate) and الحكيم the second khabar.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; أرسلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); موسى is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿بآياتنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanied by Our signs and strengthened by them".
﴿أن أخرج قومك من الظلمات إلى النور﴾: أن is explicative (tafsīriyya) or maṣdariyya; the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from ﴿أن أخرج﴾ is accusative by removal of the preposition, the implied form being "بأن أخرج قومك" (that you bring your people out), and the preposition and its genitive noun, made up of the باء and the interpreted maṣdar, are attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾. ﴿قومك﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿أخرج﴾; ﴿من الظلمات إلى النور﴾: the prepositions and their genitive nouns are attached to ﴿أخرج﴾. The clause ﴿أخرج﴾ is explicative, or the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿أن﴾, and on both construals it has no grammatical position.
﴿وذكرهم بأيام الله﴾: the واو is a conjunction; ﴿ذكرهم﴾ is an imperative verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿بأيام الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿ذكرهم﴾.
﴿إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿في ذلك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted, advanced khabar (predicate); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; آيات is the delayed noun of إن; ﴿لكل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa); صبار is the muḍāf ilayhi, and ﴿شكور﴾ is an adjective of ﴿صبار﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿وإذ قال موسى لقومه اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم﴾: the واو is resumptive; ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember), i.e. "and remember the time when Mūsā said to his people"; the clause ﴿قال موسى﴾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿لقومه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قال﴾; اذكروا is an imperative verb, and the واو is the fāʿil (agent); نعمة الله is the mafʿūl bihi; ﴿عليكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نعمة﴾ if it is taken as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "remember His bestowing upon you", or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿نعمة الله﴾ if it is taken as a noun, i.e. "remember His favour, being upon you".
﴿إذ أنجاكم من آل فرعون﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) of ﴿نعمة الله﴾, attached to it on the construal of ﴿نعمة﴾ as a maṣdar; or it is a noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from ﴿نعمة الله﴾; the clause ﴿أنجاكم﴾ is in the position of genitive by annexation; ﴿من آل فرعون﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أنجاكم﴾.
﴿يسومونكم سوء العذاب ويذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم﴾: three ḥāls from آل فرعون, or from the pronoun of those addressed.
﴿وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم﴾: the واو is a conjunction; ﴿في ذلكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, advanced khabar (predicate); بلاء is the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿من ربكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of بلاء; عظيم is a second adjective.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿وإذ تأذن ربكم لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم﴾: the واو is a conjunction; ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative by conjunction to ﴿نعمة الله﴾, the implied form being: "remember Allah's favour upon you, and remember when your Lord proclaimed"; or ﴿إذ﴾ is conjoined to the earlier ﴿إذ﴾ in the words of the Exalted ﴿إذ أنجاكم﴾; the clause ﴿تأذن﴾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; ربكم is the fāʿil (agent) of تأذن; the clause ﴿لئن شكرتم﴾ is the speech reported by an omitted verb of saying; or تأذن is treated like قال, since it is a kind of saying, so there is no need to imply a verb of saying; the lām paves the way for the oath (mūṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); إن is conditional; شكرتم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿لأزيدنكم﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and the clause لأزيدنكم has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to the oath; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
﴿ولئن كفرتم﴾: a clause conjoined to its counterpart; the answer to the oath is omitted, but it is implicitly indicated by His words ﴿إن عذابي لشديد﴾, i.e. "لأعذبنكم" (I will surely punish you).
﴿إن عذابي لشديد﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), عذابي is its noun, and شديد its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وقال موسى إن تكفروا أنتم ومن في الأرض جميعا فإن الله لغني حميد﴾: ﴿وقال موسى﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause إن تكفروا is the speech reported by the verb "said" (maqūl al-qawl); إن is conditional; تكفروا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the واو is the fāʿil; أنتم is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the واو; ﴿مَن﴾ is conjoined to the واو; ﴿في الأرض﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; جميعًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the فاء is linking; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the Name of Majesty is its noun, the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and غني حميد are two khabars (predicates) of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين من قبلكم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, inversion (of tense) and jussive; يأت is an imperfect verb made jussive by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the كاف is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); نبأ is the fāʿil (agent), and الذين is the muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿من قبلكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause).
﴿قوم نوح وعاد وثمود﴾: قوم: a badal (substitute) from ﴿الذين﴾. نوح: muḍāf ilayhi. عاد and ثمود: conjoined.
﴿والذين من بعدهم﴾: the واو is a conjunction. الذين: conjoined to ﴿قوم﴾, in the position of genitive, or conjoined to ﴿الذين من قبلكم﴾, or a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause ﴿لا يعلمهم إلا الله﴾. A preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila [Translator's note: this refers to ﴿من بعدهم﴾].
﴿لا يعلمهم إلا الله﴾: لا is negative. يعلمهم: an imperfect verb and an advanced mafʿūl bihi. إلا: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). The Name of Majesty: the delayed fāʿil. The clause ﴿لا يعلمهم إلا الله﴾: resumptive, with no grammatical position; or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿الذين﴾, or from the pronoun latent in the ṣila ﴿من بعدهم﴾; or the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of ﴿الذين﴾; it is also said that the clause is parenthetical between ﴿والذين من بعدهم﴾ and the clause ﴿جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات﴾, which occurs as a ḥāl.
﴿جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position, or a second khabar of الذين; رسلهم is the fāʿil; ﴿بالبينات﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿جاءتهم﴾.
﴿فردوا أيديهم في أفواههم وقالوا إنا كفرنا بما أرسلتم به﴾: the فاء is a conjunction; ردوا is a verb and its fāʿil; أيديهم is the mafʿūl bihi; ﴿في أفواههم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿ردوا﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿وقالوا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ردوا﴾; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause كفرنا is the khabar; ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿كفرنا﴾; the clause أرسلتم is the ṣila; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أرسلتم﴾.
﴿وإنا لفي شك مما تدعوننا إليه مريب﴾: the واو is a conjunction; ﴿إنا﴾ is conjoined to the preceding ﴿إنا﴾; إن is an abrogating particle, and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿في شك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; ﴿مما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿شك﴾, or an adjective (ṣifa) of it; the clause تدعوننا is the ṣila; ﴿إليه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿تدعوننا﴾; مريب is an adjective of شك.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: الر كِتابٌ أَنْزَلْناهُ إِلَيْكَ: that is, "This is a Book which We have sent down to you"; (أنزلناه إليك) is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), as a naʿt (adjective) of (كتاب). لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ: the lām of kay (lām of purpose), and the implied sense is "that he may bring the people out". بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ: (الإذن) "leave/permission" is used figuratively in the sense of "command". إِلى صِراطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: وَما كانَ لَنا أَنْ نَأْتِيَكُمْ: [أَنْ نَأْتِيَكُمْ] is in the position of a nominative as the noun of (كان).

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: وَلَنَصْبِرَنَّ عَلى ما آذَيْتُمُونا: the intransitive form is أذي يأذى أذى.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: ذلِكَ لِمَنْ خافَ مَقامِي وَخافَ وَعِيدِ: whoever reads it with imāla (inclination of the vowel) intends to indicate that it is from (خفت).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: وَخابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ: it is permissible to put (عنيد) in the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of (كلّ).

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: يَتَجَرَّعُهُ: that is, the angels force him to it so that he is tormented by it. وَلا يَكادُ يُسِيغُهُ: that is, [he can hardly make it] go down his throat. وَيَأْتِيهِ الْمَوْتُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكانٍ: that is, there comes to him that from which one dies, from every place of his body. وَمِنْ وَرائِهِ عَذابٌ غَلِيظٌ: it was said: beyond that with which he is tormented there is another, harsh torment.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ: the implied structure according to Sībawayh and al-Akhfash is "and among what is related to you…". Al-Kisāʾī said: [it means] "the likeness of the deeds of those who disbelieved is like ashes". Others said: مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا is a mubtadaʾ (subject); أَعْمالُهُمْ is a badal (substitute) from it, the implied sense being "the likeness of their deeds"; and it is permissible for it to be a second mubtadaʾ, as is related: صفة فلان أنّه أحمر ("So-and-so's description: he is red"). Al-Farrāʾ said: if a reader had read أعمالهم in the genitive it would be permissible, and he recited: [rajaz] 248-
ما للكمال مشيها وئيدا
(What is with the camels, their gait so slow?) «[Translator's note: the source prints «ما للكمال»; the well-known verse reads «ما للجمال» (the camels), which the gloss follows.]»
فِي يَوْمٍ عاصِفٍ: by way of relation (nasab) according to the Basrans, meaning "having storm" (ذي عاصف). Al-Farrāʾ allowed it to mean "on a day whose wind is stormy" (في يوم عاصف الريح), and he also allowed (عاصف) to belong to the wind specifically and then be made to follow (يوم) [in case]. He said: the grammarians have related: هذا جحر ضبّ خرب ("this is a ruined lizard's hole", with (خرب) in the genitive). Abū Jaʿfar said: this is something upon which the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ought not to be construed. Sībawayh mentioned that this is an error on the part of the Arabs, and he took as evidence that when they use the dual they say هذان جحرا ضبّ خربان, because it has become clear through the dual and the singular. A parallel to this error is the saying of al-Nābigha: [kāmil] 249-
أمن آل ميّة رائح أو مغتدي ... عجلان ذا زاد وغير مزوّد
زعم البوارح أنّ رحلتنا غد ... وبذاك خبّرنا الغراب الأسود
(Is it from Mayya's family, departing at evening or setting out at morning, in haste, with provisions or unprovisioned? The ill-omened birds claimed that our journey is tomorrow, and of that the black crow informed us.)
So the like of this is not permissible in speech, nor for any poet we know; how then could it be permissible in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic? Then al-Farrāʾ recited a verse: [basīṭ] 250-
يا صاح بلّغ ذوي الزّوجات كلّهم ... أن ليس وصل إذا انحلّت عرى الذّنب
(O companion, inform all those who have wives that there is no union once the ties of the tail come undone.)
and he claimed that Abū al-Jarrāḥ recited it to him with «كلّهم» in the genitive. This is something not to be relied on, because the accusative does not spoil the poetry. Whoever reads «في يوم عاصف» without tanwīn [i.e. as a construct] puts the adjective in place of the thing described, i.e. "on the day of a stormy wind".

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: اللَّهِ: [in the genitive] as a badal (substitute); and the nominative is as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or, if you wish, with an implied (muqaddar) mubtadaʾ; and likewise وَوَيْلٌ لِلْكافِرِينَ.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ جَمِيعاً: that is, from their graves; and جَمِيعاً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). تَبَعاً means "having following" (ذي تبع), and it is permissible for it to be the plural of (تابع). ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: the implied structure is "alike to us are our impatience and our patience".

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
إِلَّا أَنْ دَعَوْتُكُمْ: in the position of an accusative, an exception (istithnāʾ) not of the same kind as the first. وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُصْرِخِيَّ: with fatḥa on the yāʾ, because the yāʾ of the first person has two usages: fatḥa and sukūn, when no quiescent letter precedes it; but when a quiescent letter precedes it, then fatḥa and nothing else. And whoever gives it kasra is obliged to read هِيَ عَصايَ [Ṭāhā: 18] with kasra on the yāʾ. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read بِمُصْرِخِيَّ إِنِّي with kasra on the yāʾ. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: I have not heard this from any of the Arabs nor from the grammarians. And al-Farrāʾ said:
Perhaps the one who read it this way thought that the bāʾ puts the whole word in the genitive. Abū Jaʿfar said: so this has become, by consensus, impermissible, even though al-Farrāʾ contradicted this and recited: [rajaz] 251-
قال لها هل لك يا تافيّ ... قالت له ما أنت بالمرضيّ
(He said to her: "Would you, O you…?" She said to him: "You are not one to be accepted.")
And the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ought not to be construed on anomalies. The meaning of بِما أَشْرَكْتُمُونِ is "from before", since he had been an associator (of partners with Allah) before them; and it was said: from before the matter.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ allowed "ومثلَ كلمة خبيثة" [in the accusative] by conjunction (nasaq), and they related that in the reading of Ubayy it is: وضرب مثل كلمة خبيثة. «[Translator's note: the source has a stray closing bracket after this quotation.]»

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: وَأَحَلُّوا قَوْمَهُمْ دارَ الْبَوارِ: two objects.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: جَهَنَّمَ is accusative as a badal (substitute) from (دار). It is not declined fully (a diptote) because it is feminine and definite, derived from their saying ركيّة جهنّام ("a deep well") when it is deep-bottomed.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: (عوجا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: it is accusative (manṣūb) as a second object, this being one of the verbs that take two objects, one of them through a preposition; the implied sense is "and they seek crookedness for it" (ويبغون بها عوجا).

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنْداداً لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ: accusative by the lām of kay (lām of purpose), and some call it the lām of outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba).
The meaning is that since their affair ended up at this, they were like someone who had done that in order that this might be.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t:
قُلْ لِعِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ: concerning يُقِيمُوا the grammarians have several views. Al-Farrāʾ said:
its interpretation is a command. Abū Isḥāq said something like this; he said the meaning is "let them establish the prayer" (ليقيموا الصلاة), then the lām was dropped because the command had already preceded. He said: and it is permissible for it to be indeclinable (mabnī), because the lām was dropped and it was made indeclinable since it carries the meaning of a command. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd related to us from al-Māzinī, who said:
The implied structure is: "Say to those who believe: establish the prayer, [and] they will establish it". This is a good view, because when the believers are commanded something they accept it, so it is the apodosis (jawāb) of the command. وَيُنْفِقُوا is conjoined to it. مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلا خِلالٌ: «لا» is made to have the meaning of (ليس); or, if you wish, you put what follows it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). It is permissible to put the first in the nominative and the second in the accusative without tanwīn and with tanwīn; and it is permissible to put the first in the accusative without tanwīn and the second in the nominative with tanwīn, or in the accusative with tanwīn. Al-Akhfash said: (خلال) is the plural of (خلّة). And Abū ʿUbayd said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like (القتال), and he recited: [ṭawīl] 252-
ولست بمقليّ الخلال ولا قال
(And I am not one whose friendship is hated, nor one who hates.)

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: دائِبَيْنِ: as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. constant in what leads to the welfare of people.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
وَآتاكُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ ما سَأَلْتُمُوهُ: there are several views about its meaning. The view of al-Farrāʾ is "of everything you asked for", as you say: "I gave him his request" even if he did not ask anything, i.e. what, had he not asked, he would have asked for. «[Translator's note: the Arabic «أي ما لم يسأل لسأله» is elliptical; rendered by sense.]» Al-Akhfash said:
"And He gave you of everything you asked Him something" — [like] أُوتِيَتْ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ [al-Naml: 23], i.e. of everything in her time, something. He said: and it may be by way of multiplicity [i.e. hyperbole]; and Sībawayh related: ما بقي منهم مخبّر ("not one of them remained to give news"), and that is well known in the speech of the Arabs. And there is a fourth view about it, namely that people, in the diversity of their conditions, asked for things, and so they were addressed accordingly.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَذَا الْبَلَدَ آمِناً: two objects. وَاجْنُبْنِي: and by way of intensification one says جنّبني, and one also says أجنبني. أَنْ نَعْبُدَ is in the position of an accusative, and the meaning is "from worshipping the idols".

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: فَمَنْ تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي: that is, of the people of my religion and of my companions. وَمَنْ عَصانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ: that is, to him if he repents.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: رَبَّنا إِنِّي أَسْكَنْتُ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوادٍ: the object is omitted because «من» indicates it; and likewise رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلاةِ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
وَما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا بِلِسانِ قَوْمِهِ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ: accusative by the lām of kay (lām of purpose). فَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشاءُ is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), and according to most grammarians it is not permissible to conjoin it to what precedes; its parallel is لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِي الْأَرْحامِ ما نَشاءُ [al-Ḥajj: 5]. And the grammarians recited: [rajaz] 245-
يريد أن يعربه فيعجمه
(He wants to make it clear Arabic, but instead he makes it foreign/obscure.)
Abū Isḥāq said: the accusative is permissible in فَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشاءُ, taking it to be like لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَناً [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8], i.e. their affair came to this.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ غافِلًا: two objects.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: Abū Isḥāq said: مُهْطِعِينَ مُقْنِعِي رُؤُسِهِمْ are accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning is "for a day on which their eyes stare, hastening (مهطعين)", i.e. rushing. لا يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ: [طَرْفُهُمْ is] nominative by (يرتد). وَأَفْئِدَتُهُمْ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); هَواءٌ is its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
وَأَنْذِرِ النَّاسَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ الْعَذابُ فَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا: it is not the answer to the command; rather it is conjoined to (يأتيهم) or resumptive (mustaʾnaf). This has confused some grammarians, to the point that one said: the answer to a command is not put in the accusative with the fāʾ; and this contradicts what al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, and Sībawayh said. The grammarians recited: [rajaz] 253-
يا ناق سيري عنقا فسيحا ... إلى سليمان فنستريحا
(O she-camel, go at a broad, long-striding pace to Sulaymān, so that we may rest.)
The accusative is ruled out in the verse only because the meaning is not that. أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوا أَقْسَمْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ زَوالٍ: that is, of moving away from the respite you are in to retribution and requital.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t:
وَإِنْ كانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ الْجِبالُ: «إن» means «ما» (not); this is related from al-Ḥasan thus, and that like it is فَإِنْ كُنْتَ فِي شَكٍّ مِمَّا أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ [Yūnus: 94], and likewise قُلْ إِنْ كانَ لِلرَّحْمنِ وَلَدٌ فَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْعابِدِينَ [al-Zukhruf: 81]; but other than what he said has been said about these two verses, and that is in their places. Mujāhid read وإن كاد مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال with fatḥa on the lām and the verb in the nominative, and al-Kisāʾī read it so. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, according to what is related from him, preferred the view of Qatāda on it. He said: this is because of their disbelief, like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: تَكادُ السَّماواتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ [Maryam: 90]. Abū Jaʿfar said:
Abū Isḥāq held that this came according to the speech of the Arabs, for they say: "Even if you reached such-and-such, you would not attain anything", though one does not reach it; and likewise with «إن». And Sībawayh recited: [ṭawīl] 254-
لئن كنت في جبّ ثمانين قامة ... ورقّيت أسباب السّماء بسلّم
(Even if you were in a well eighty fathoms deep, or were raised up to the ropes of heaven by a ladder…)
And it is related from ʿUmar, ʿAlī and ʿAbd Allāh, may Allah be pleased with them, that they read وإن كاد مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال, with the dāl and the verb in the nominative. The meaning of this is clear, but it is an interpretation and not a reading.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t:
فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ: this is a figurative usage (majāz), as one says: معطي درهم زيدا ("giver of a dirham to Zayd"). And Sībawayh recited: [ṭawīl] 255-
ترى الثّور فيها مدخل الظّلّ رأسه ... وسائره باد إلى الشّمس أجمع
(You see the wild bull in it putting its head into the shade, while the rest of it is entirely exposed to the sun.)

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ: [الْأَرْضُ is] the noun of the verb whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent); غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ is its khabar (predicate). «[Translator's note: so in the source; غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ is ordinarily parsed as the second object of the passive verb.]» Concerning its meaning there are two views: one is that it will be changed into an earth other than this one, and there are hadiths about this; the other view is that its changing is the removal of its mountains and its being made a level, bare plain, and the changing of the sky is its splitting apart, the scattering of its stars and the folding up of its sun, as one says: "I changed my ring", i.e. I altered it from what it was.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t:
مُقَرَّنِينَ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). مُقَرَّنِينَ: their hands and feet bound to their necks with chains and fetters. (القرن) with fatḥa on the rāʾ is the rope with which two things are tied together. Jarīr said:
[basīṭ] 256-
وابن اللّبون إذا ما لزّ في قرن
(And the two-year-old camel, when it is tied in a rope [with a stronger one]…)

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
It is permissible for «أن» to be in the position of an accusative, i.e. "with: bring your people out" (بأن أخرج قومك). This is the view of Sībawayh, as one says: أمرته أن قم ("I commanded him: stand"), meaning "I commanded him to stand" (أن يقوم), and then it is construed according to the sense, as the poet said: [kāmil] 246-
وأنا الذي قتلت بكرا بالقنا
(And I am the one who killed Bakr with the spears.)
And it is permissible for «أن» to have no grammatical position, as in أرسلت إليه أن قم ("I sent to him: stand"), meaning "that is, stand" (أي قم); and its parallel is His saying, glorified is He: وَانْطَلَقَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ امْشُوا [Ṣād: 6].

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: هذا بَلاغٌ لِلنَّاسِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. this exhortation has reached them, if they take heed. وَلِيُنْذَرُوا بِهِ: the lām of kay (lām of purpose), and the verb [it depends on] is omitted because the hearer knows it. وَلِيَعْلَمُوا أَنَّما هُوَ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ وَلِيَذَّكَّرَ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ: conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذابِ وَيُذَبِّحُونَ — and in another place without the wāw. When it is with the wāw, then according to al-Farrāʾ it means "they torment you and they slaughter you", so that the slaughtering is something other than the first torment; and according to others it is permissible for it to be part of the first. When it is without the wāw, it is an explanation of the first and a badal (substitute) from it, as Sībawayh recited: [ṭawīl] 247-
متى تأتنا تلمم بنا في ديارنا ... تجد حطبا جزلا ونارا تأجّجا
(Whenever you come to us, alighting with us in our abodes, you will find thick firewood and a blazing fire.)

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ: (إنّ) is given kasra because what comes after the fāʾ in a conditional requital is a fresh start (mustaʾnaf), and the lām is for emphasis (tawkīd).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَبَؤُا الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعادٍ وَثَمُودَ: as a badal (substitute). (ثمود) is not put in the genitive with tanwīn because it is made a name for the tribe, and it is permissible to put it in the genitive [with tanwīn], making it a name for the clan (al-ḥayy). وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ is in the position of a genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf). لا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: [اللَّهُ is] nominative by the verb. جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ.
And if you wish, you may drop the ḍamma from the sīn [i.e. رُسْلُهُمْ] because of its heaviness. فَرَدُّوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِي أَفْواهِهِمْ: when you use the singular you say (فم), but the original is (فوه), so it is pluralized according to its original form, like (حوض) and (أحواض).

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿الۤر كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ لِتُخْرِجَ ٱلنَّاسَ مِنَ ٱلظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾.
The darknesses are unbelief and the light is Islam, by way of likeness, because unbelief is like darkness and Islam is like light.
The bāʾ in His saying ﴿بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying ﴿لِتُخْرِجَ ٱلنَّاسَ﴾, and the meaning of His saying ﴿بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ is that no one is guided except by Allah's permission.
And it is possible that the meaning is: by your teaching them.
Then He explained the light, saying: ﴿إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذٰلِكَ لِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامِي وَخَافَ وَعِيدِ﴾.
That is, that is for whoever fears his standing before Him; and the maṣdar (verbal noun) may be annexed to the agent and to the object, because it is attached to both.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَٱسْتَفْتَحُواْ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: And they sought help (victory).
And in the ḥadīth: "The Prophet ﷺ used to seek victory (yastaftiḥ) in battle through the poor ones of the Emigrants."
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَخَابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: al-jabbār among the people of language is the one who considers that no one has any right over him.
Mujāhid said: al-ʿanīd is the obstinate one who turns away from the truth.
Qatāda said: al-ʿanīd is the one who refused to say: There is no god but Allah.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿مِّن وَرَآئِهِ جَهَنَّمُ﴾.
That is, in front of him; it is not one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād), but it is from تَوَارَى, i.e. "to be hidden."
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَيُسْقَىٰ مِن مَّآءٍ صَدِيدٍ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, what has mixed with his flesh and blood.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Meaning pus and festering fluid.
Mujāhid said: It is pus and festering fluid.
Others said: It is possible that this is by way of likeness, i.e. he is given to drink what is like pus and festering fluid.
And it is possible that it is: he is given pus and festering fluid to drink.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلاَ يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ﴾.
That is, he swallows it.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَيَأْتِيهِ ٱلْمَوْتُ مِن كُلِّ مَكَانٍ﴾.
That is, from every place of his body.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا هُوَ بِمَيِّتٍ وَمِن وَرَآئِهِ عَذَابٌ غَلِيظٌ﴾.
That is, before him is the torment of Hell.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated to me, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said regarding the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, ﴿وَمِن وَرَآئِهِ عَذَابٌ غَلِيظٌ﴾: the stopping of the breaths.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ كَرَمَادٍ ٱشْتَدَّتْ بِهِ ٱلرِّيحُ فِي يَوْمٍ عَاصِفٍ﴾.
That is, nothing was accepted from them.
And «عاصفٌ» follows in sequence (as an adjective of «يوم»), i.e. the wind on it is violent.
And it is possible that the implied form is "violent of wind" (ʿāṣif al-rīḥ).

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ لَمَّا قُضِيَ ٱلأَمْرُ﴾.
That is, when it has been finished, and the people of Paradise have entered Paradise and the people of the Fire the Fire. ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمْ وَعْدَ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾ — i.e. He promised Paradise to whoever obeyed Him and the Fire to whoever disobeyed Him. ﴿وَوَعَدتُّكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُكُمْ﴾ — i.e. I promised you the opposite of that. ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِيَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِّن سُلْطَانٍ﴾ — i.e. any proof that I could make clear. ﴿إِلاَّ أَن دَعَوْتُكُمْ فَٱسْتَجَبْتُمْ لِي﴾ — i.e. except that I led you astray and you followed me.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿مَّآ أَنَاْ بِمُصْرِخِكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: That is, your rescuer.
And it is narrated that he will be addressed with this in the Fire.
And the meaning of ﴿إِنِّي كَفَرْتُ بِمَآ أَشْرَكْتُمُونِ مِن قَبْلُ﴾ is: I disbelieve in your having associated me (with Allah).

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً كَشَجَرةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Fāryābī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Khālid narrated to us, saying: ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to us from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet ﷺ said one day to his Companions: "Tell me of a tree that resembles the Muslim, whose leaves do not fall, and which gives its fruit at all times by its Lord's permission!" He said: It occurred to me that it was "the date palm." He said: The people kept silent, and the Prophet said: It is the date palm. So I said to my father: It had occurred to me that it was the date palm.
He said: What prevented you from having said it to the Messenger of Allah? Your having said it would be dearer to me than such-and-such. I said: You were among the people, and Abū Bakr, and the two of you said nothing, so I disliked to speak."
And al-Aʿmash narrated from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: It is the date palm.
Likewise al-Aʿmash narrated it from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
And Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً﴾ — he said: There is no god but Allah. ﴿كَشَجَرةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ﴾ — he said: the believer. ﴿أَصْلُهَا ثَابِتٌ﴾ — "There is no god but Allah" is firm in the heart of the believer.
﴿وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ﴾ — he said: shirk (associating partners with Allah). ﴿كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ﴾ — he said: the polytheist. ﴿اجْتُثَّتْ مِنْ فَوْقِ الأرْضِ مَا لَهَا مِنْ قَرَارٍ﴾ — i.e. the polytheist has no root on which he acts.
And Shuʿayb ibn al-Ḥabḥāb narrated from Anas ibn Mālik: ﴿كَشَجَرةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ﴾ — he said: the date palm; and he said: the bad tree is the colocynth.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تُؤْتِيۤ أُكُلَهَا كُلَّ حِينٍ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهَا﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ and Ibn Jurayj narrated from Mujāhid, who said: every year. [Translator's note: the Arabic has «ابن نجيح», presumably for Ibn Abī Najīḥ.]
And ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib and Ṭāriq ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: every six months.
And Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī narrated from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-ḥīn is of two kinds: a ḥīn whose extent is known and a ḥīn whose extent is not known. As for the one whose extent is known, it is His saying: ﴿تُؤْتِيۤ أُكُلَهَا كُلَّ حِينٍ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهَا﴾.
ʿIkrima said: It is six months.
And al-Aʿmash narrated from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-ḥīn may be morning and evening. [Translator's note: the Arabic reads «الأعمش في أبي ظبيان», evidently for «عن».]
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said regarding His saying ﴿تُؤْتِيۤ أُكُلَهَا كُلَّ حِينٍ﴾: by night and by day, in winter and summer; and likewise the believer — his deeds are of benefit at all times.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another and not contradictory, because al-ḥīn according to all the people of language — except those who deviate among them — means "time," applying to a short and a long period. Al-Aṣmaʿī recited the verse of al-Nābigha:
تَنَاذَرَهَا الرَّاقُونَ مِنْ سُوءِ سَمِّهَا * تُطَلِّقُهُ حِيناً وحِيناً تُرَاجعُ
(The snake-charmers warned one another against her because of her evil venom; it lets him go for a time, and for a time it comes back.)
This shows you that al-ḥīn means "time."
However, what best fits the verse is that al-ḥīn is the year, because the ripening of the fruit is every year, and likewise its budding.
And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Allah's mercy be upon him, that he said: The least ḥīn is a year.
And Sufyān narrated from al-Ḥakam and Ḥammād that they both said: al-ḥīn is a year.
And the meaning of ﴿اجْتُثَّتْ﴾ is: its whole body (juththa) was cut off entirely.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَيَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجاً﴾.
They seek other than the straight course.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلاَّ بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِ﴾.
That is, in the language of his people.
﴿لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ﴾ means: to make them understand, so that the proof is established against them.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ بِآيَاتِنَآ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, with the clear signs, meaning His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى تِسْعَ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾.
* And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَذَكِّرْهُمْ بِأَيَّامِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: That is, of the blessings of Allah.
Others said: of His destroying those before them, and His taking vengeance on them for their unbelief.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ ٱذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ أَنجَاكُمْ مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوۤءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ وَيُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ﴾.
And in another place: ﴿يُذَبِّحُونَ﴾ without a wāw.
The meaning of the wāw entails that some torment other than the slaughtering had befallen them; and when it is without the wāw, it is merely an explanation of the first.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ﴾.
That is, they do not kill them; it is from life (al-ḥayāh), i.e. they let them live.
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "Kill the old men of the polytheists and spare (istaḥyū) their youths (sharkhahum)."
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَفِي ذٰلِكُمْ بَلاۤءٌ مِّن رَّبَّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ﴾.
It was said: the meaning is: in His rescuing you from them there is a great blessing, and al-balāʾ [here is blessing.
And it was said: in what they inflicted on you there is a balāʾ, i.e. an affliction.]
And it was said: al-balāʾ here is testing.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِن شَكَرْتُمْ لأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ﴾.
تأذَّن (taʾadhdhana) means "He made known," from their saying آذَنَهُ فأذِنَ بالأمر ("he informed him, so he came to know of the matter"); this is as one says تَوَعَّدتُه and أوْعَدتُه with one meaning.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ لاَ يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn — and Isrāʾīl narrated it from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh — regarding His saying ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ لاَ يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ﴾, that he said: "The genealogists have lied."
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "Between ʿAdnān and Ismāʿīl there are thirty forefathers who are not known."
And it is narrated from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "We have not found anyone who knows what lies between ʿAdnān and Ismāʿīl."
* And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿جَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ فَرَدُّوۤاْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِيۤ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾.
There are several views on its meaning:
(a) Mujāhid said: They threw back the messengers' words at them and gave them the lie.
(b) Qatāda said: They threw back at the messengers what they had brought.
So this is by way of likeness, and it is the position of Abū ʿUbayda;
i.e. they abandoned what the messengers brought them, so they were like one who puts it back to his mouth and keeps silent, saying nothing.
And it was said: ﴿فَرَدُّوۤاْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِيۤ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ means they rejected what, had they accepted it, would have been blessings (ayādī). ﴿فِيۤ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ means with their mouths, i.e. with their tongues.
(c) And it was said: they rejected the blessings of the messengers — because the sending of them is a blessing upon them — by speech and by giving the lie.
(d) There is a fourth view on the verse, and it is the most fitting of them and the most eminent in chain of transmission:
Abū ʿUbayd said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū l-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, regarding His saying ﴿فَرَدُّوۤاْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِيۤ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ — he said: They bit on them in rage.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The proof of the correctness of this view is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإذَا خَلَوْا عَضُّوا عَلَيْكُمُ الأَنَامِلَ مِنَ الغَيْظِ﴾.
The poet said:
لَوْ أنَّ سَلْمَى أبْصَرَتْ تَخَدُّدِي * وَدِقَّةً فِي عَظْمِ سَاقِي وَيَدِي
وَبُعْدَ أهْلِي وَجَفَاءَ عُوَّدِي * عَضَّتْ مِنَ الوَجْدِ بأطْرَافِ اليَدِ
(Had Salmā seen my wasting away and the thinness of the bones of my leg and arm, the distance of my family and the coldness of my visitors, she would have bitten her fingertips out of grief.)

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُثَبِّتُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ بِٱلْقَوْلِ ٱلثَّابِتِ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَفِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Ṭāwūs, from his father, regarding ﴿يُثَبِّتُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ بِٱلْقَوْلِ ٱلثَّابِتِ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾ — he said: There is no god but Allah. ﴿وَفِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾ — at the questioning in the grave. [Translator's note: so in the source; the chain is usually "Maʿmar from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father".]
Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib and Abū Hurayra said: This is at the questioning, when he comes to be in the grave.
And Shuʿba narrated from ʿAlqama ibn Marthad, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbayda, from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, from the Prophet ﷺ, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿يُثَبِّتُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ بِٱلْقَوْلِ ٱلثَّابِتِ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَفِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾ — the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In the grave, when he is questioned." [Translator's note: the Arabic has «سعيد بن عبيدة»; the narrator is usually named Saʿd ibn ʿUbayda.]
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: It has reached me that this community will be tried in their graves, and Allah will make firm those who believe.
And it is narrated that he will be asked: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet? Whoever Allah makes firm says: "Allah is my Lord, Islam is my religion, and Muḥammad is my prophet."
So this is making firm in the Hereafter.
And the making firm in this world is that he is enabled to (give) it only because it was his belief in this world.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ بَدَّلُواْ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ كُفْراً وَأَحَلُّواْ قَوْمَهُمْ دَارَ ٱلْبَوَارِ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: They are the unbelievers of Quraysh.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, said: They are the leaders of the polytheists on the day of Badr; ﴿أَحَلُّواْ قَوْمَهُمْ﴾, i.e. those who followed them, ﴿دَارَ ٱلْبَوَارِ﴾, which is Hell, their abode in the Hereafter.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-bawār in the language is destruction.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿مِّن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لاَّ بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلاَ خِلاَلٌ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: al-bayʿ (selling) here is ransom.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The root meaning of al-bayʿ in the language is that you hand over and take something in exchange for it; and what Abū ʿUbayda said is very good. It is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿واتَّقُوا يَوْماً لاَ تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئاً﴾, and like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلاَ يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا عدلٌ﴾, i.e. a value (equivalent).
Al-khilāl, al-mukhālla and al-khulla mean friendship.
The poet said:
صَرَفْتُ الهَوَى عَنْهُنَّ مِنْ خشْيَةِ الرَّدَى * وَلَسْتُ بمَقْليِّ الخِلاَلِ وَلاَ قَالِي
(I turned my passion away from them for fear of ruin, yet I am neither one whose friendship is hated nor one who hates.)

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآتَاكُم مِّن كُلِّ مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, of everything for which you turned to Him in desire.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view; it holds that they were given some of what they did not ask for. That is well known in the language: one says, "Go to so-and-so, for he will give you everything you ask," even if he gives him other than what he asked.
There is another view on the verse: that when He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said ﴿وَآتَاكُم مِّن كُلِّ مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ﴾, He did not negate anything other than this.
Moreover, al-Ḍaḥḥāk read ﴿وَآتَاكُمْ مِنْ كُلٍّ مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ﴾ (with tanwīn on «كلٍّ»), and this reading is also narrated from al-Ḥasan.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda interpreted it as negation (i.e. "of everything, what you did not ask Him").
And al-Ḥasan said: That is, of all that you asked Him;
meaning: and He gave you of all the things that you asked.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Ḥasan's view is more fitting, and the other is possible but far-fetched; its far-fetchedness is that with a wāw it would be a better conjunction, meaning "and what you did (not) ask Him." Still, it is possible, though far-fetched.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ هَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدَ آمِناً وَٱجْنُبْنِي وَبَنِيَّ أَن نَّعْبُدَ ٱلأَصْنَامَ﴾.
Al-Jaḥdarī and ʿĪsā read ﴿وَأَجْنِبْنِي﴾ with a disjunctive alif (hamzat al-qaṭʿ), and its meaning is: make me to one side.
Likewise the meaning of «اجْنُبْنِي» and «جَنِّبْنِي»: its meaning is "keep me firm upon affirming Your oneness," as the Exalted said: ﴿وَاجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمِينَ لَكَ﴾, when the two of them were already Muslims.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيراً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾.
And they (the idols) have no reason, so the meaning is: many people went astray because of them.
This is common in the language; one says: "This house has captivated me," i.e. I found it beautiful and was captivated because of it, so it is as though it captivated me.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِيۤ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾.
Mujāhid read: «تَهْوَى إليهم».
The meaning of «تَهْوِي» is "be drawn (yearning)," and «تَهْوَى» is "love."
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Samāʿa narrated to us, saying: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā ibn Qirṭās narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyab ibn Rāfiʿ informed me, saying: Ibn ʿAbbās said: When Ibrāhīm ﷺ said ﴿رَبِّ إنِّي أسْكَنْتُ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوَادٍ غَيْرِ ذِي زَرْعٍ﴾ up to His saying ﴿فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِيۤ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ — had Ibrāhīm ﷺ said "make the hearts of the people (afʾidat al-nās) yearn towards them," the Turks and the Daylam would have crowded you out of it.
And it was read before ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn — the judge in Egypt — from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād, who said: Shuʿba narrated to us from al-Ḥakam, who said: I asked ʿAṭāʾ, Ṭāwūs and ʿIkrima about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾, and they said: the pilgrimage (ḥajj).

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ ٱلصَّلاَةِ وَمِن ذُرِّيَتِي﴾.
The meaning is: and make among my offspring those who establish the prayer.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
Then He said: ﴿رَبَّنَا ٱغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلْحِسَابُ﴾.
It was said: He made this prayer only at first; then when it became clear to him that he (his father) was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him.
And it was said: by "his parents" he means Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read «اغفِرْ لي ولوالِدِي», meaning his father.
Al-Nakhaʿī and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read «اغفر لِي وَلِوَلَدَيَّ», meaning his two sons.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ مُقْنِعِي رُءُوسِهِمْ لاَ يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ﴾.
His saying: ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid and Abū l-Ḍuḥā said: That is, staring fixedly.
Qatāda said: That is, hastening.
What is known in the language is that one says أهْطَعَ when he hastens.
Abū ʿUbayda said: Both senses may be together, meaning hastening while staring fixedly.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿مُقْنِعِي رُءُوسِهِمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, raising them.
Qatāda said: al-muqniʿ is the one who raises his head, his gaze fixed, not blinking.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the view of the people of language, except that Abū l-ʿAbbās (al-Mubarrad) said: One says أقْنَعَ when he raises his head, and أقنع when he lowers his head in abasement and submission. He said: Both views have been given on the verse.
He said: And it is possible that he raises his head staring fixedly, then lowers it in submission and abasement.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is well known in the language is that the one who raises his head is called muqniʿ.
And it is narrated that they will keep raising their heads and looking at what comes from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. The people of language recited:
يُبَاكِرْنَ العِضَاهَ بِمُقْنِعَاتٍ * نَوَاجِذُهُنَّ كَالحِدَإِ الوَقِيعِ
(They come early to the thorn-trees with raised heads, their molars like sharpened axe-heads.)
He is describing camels, and that they raise their heads, (their teeth) like axes.
And from it the miqnaʿa (head-veil) is so called, because of its being raised.
And from it: قَنِعَ الرجلُ when he is content, and قَنَعَ when he begs, i.e. does something one should be ashamed of. [Translator's note: «ما يُتقنَّعُ منه», literally "what one covers one's head (out of shame) from".]
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ وَأَفْئِدَتُهُمْ هَوَآءٌ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from Murra: ﴿وَأَفْئِدَتُهُمْ هَوَآءٌ﴾ — he said: torn open, retaining nothing, meaning from fear.
And Ḥajjāj narrated from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ﴿هَوَآءٌ﴾ — there is nothing of good in them, as a house with nothing in it is called hawāʾ.
And it was said: He described them with cowardice and terror, i.e. their hearts are hollow.
The root meaning of al-hawāʾ in the language is the hollow, empty thing; from it is the saying of Zuhayr:
كَأَنَّ الرَّحْلَ مِنْهَا فَوْقَ صَعْلٍ * منَ الظِّلْمَانِ جُؤْجُؤُهُ هَوَاءُ
(As though the saddle on her were upon a small-headed male ostrich whose breast is hollow.)
i.e. there is no marrow or anything in it. And Ḥassān said:
أَلاَ أَبْلِغْ أبَا سُفْيَانَ عَنِّي * فَأَنْتَ مُجَوَّفٌ نَخِبٌ هَوَاءٌ
(Convey from me to Abū Sufyān: you are hollow, heartless, empty.)

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنذِرِ ٱلنَّاسَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ﴾.
That is, make them afraid.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوۤاْ أَقْسَمْتُمْ مِّن قَبْلُ مَا لَكُمْ مِّن زَوَالٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, you swore that you would not die. (Addressed) to Quraysh.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَدْ مَكَرُواْ مَكْرَهُمْ وَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ مَكْرُهُمْ وَإِن كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ ٱلْجِبَالُ﴾.
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Allah's mercy be upon him, read ﴿وَإنْ كَادَ﴾ with a dāl.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Allah's good pleasure be upon him, read ﴿وَإن كَانَ مكرُهم لَتَزُولُ مِنه الجِبَالُ﴾ with fatḥa on the lām and the verb in the nominative (marfūʿ)… and «كاد» with a dāl — this is what is known of his reading.
What is well known of the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās is «وإنْ كادَ» with a dāl.
Mujāhid read: ﴿وَإنْ كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ منهُ الجبالُ﴾, and it is the reading of al-Kisāʾī and Mujāhid; and «إن» [means «لو» ("if"), i.e. and even if their plotting were such that the mountains would be moved by it, they would not attain this, and they will never be able to (overcome) Islam, since Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, has willed] to make it prevail over all religion.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is well known in the speech of the Arabs, as one says: "Even if you reached the ropes of heaven" — when he does not reach them; this is like that.
And it is narrated in the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, may Allah have mercy on him: ﴿ولولا كلمةُ اللهِ لَزَالَ مكرهم الجبال﴾.
Qatāda said, on «وإن كان مكرُهم لتزولَ منه الجبالُ»: when they ascribed a son to Allah, and He, Glorified is He, has said: ﴿تكادُ السَّمواتُ يتفطَّرنَ منهُ﴾.
And whoever read ﴿وإنْ كان مكرُهم لِتزُولُ منه الجبالُ﴾ held that the meaning is: their plotting was not such that the Qurʾān would be removed by it, in view of its weakness, while (the Qurʾān) is as firmly fixed as the mountains. [Translator's note: the vowelling «لِتزُولُ» is as printed; the reading meant here is evidently «لِتَزُولَ» with kasra on the lām, with «إن» as negation.]
Al-Ḥasan said: Their plotting was flimsier and weaker than that the mountains should be moved by it — and he read with this reading.
Another view has been given on the meaning of the nominative reading: it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that when Nimrod starved the vultures and hung meat for them on spears, and rose up high, it was said to him: Where do you intend to go, O wicked one? Come down. He said: That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَإِن كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ ٱلْجِبَالُ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: «مكرُهم» here is their shirk, and it is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿تَكَادُ السَّمَوَاتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ وتَنْشَقُّ الأرْضُ وَتَخِرُّ الجِبَالُ هَدًّا﴾.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ ٱلأَرْضُ غَيْرَ ٱلأَرْضِ وَٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ وَبَرَزُواْ للَّهِ ٱلْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: It will be replaced with a white earth like silver, on which no forbidden blood has been shed and in which no sin has been committed.
Jābir said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar "Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī" about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ ٱلأَرْضُ غَيْرَ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾. He said: It will be replaced with a loaf of bread, from which creation will eat on the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَاهُم جَسَداً لاَ يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعَامَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan ibn Faraj narrated to us in Gaza, saying: Yūsuf ibn ʿAdī narrated to us, saying: ʿAlī ibn Mushir narrated to us from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ ٱلأَرْضُ غَيْرَ ٱلأَرْضِ وَٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ﴾: Where will the people be on that day, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "On the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ)."
Al-Ḥasan said: The earth will be changed, as someone says: "Our hands have changed." [Translator's note: «لقد تبدلت يدينا» is as written; the point is a change of state, not of substance.] He said: Its sun, its moon, its stars, its rivers and its mountains will go — that is the changing.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَرَى ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُّقَرَّنِينَ فِي ٱلأَصْفَادِ﴾.
Qatāda said: In iron collars and fetters.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَرَابِيلُهُم مِّن قَطِرَانٍ وَتَغْشَىٰ وُجُوهَهُمْ ٱلنَّارُ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: It is the tar (qaṭirān) used on camels.
And it is narrated from a group of the Successors that they said: It is copper.
What is known in the language is that copper is called qiṭr: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَا لَهُ عَيْنَ القِطْرِ﴾. [Translator's note: so quoted here; the muṣḥaf wording, quoted correctly below, is ﴿وَأَسَلْنَا لَهُ عَيْنَ القِطْرِ﴾ (Sabaʾ 34:12).]
Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿIkrima read: «سَرَابِيلُهُمْ من قِطْرٍ آنٍ» ("their garments of molten copper, extremely hot"), and they both explained it as copper.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the correct (view), and from it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَأَسَلْنَا لَهُ عَيْنَ القِطْرِ﴾. And al-sarābīl are shirts.
ʿIkrima said: And «آنٍ» means its heat has reached its utmost. And it is said that the hamza is a substitute for the ḥāʾ.
If it is said: Perhaps the ḥāʾ is the substitute for the hamza, it is answered: That is more fitting, because it is taken from al-ḥīn (time).

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(الر) disconnected letters (ḥurūf muqaṭṭaʿa) with no grammatical position [Note: See the first verse of Sūrat al-Baqara.], (كتاب) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هذا ("this").
