(قل) like the preceding «1» , (لعبادي) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قل) , and the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied on the letter before the yāʾ.. and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (الذين) a relative in the position of a genitive, naʿt of عباد (آمنوا) like بدّلوا «2» .. and the object of قلّ is omitted, implied "establish the prayer" (يقيموا) an imperfect verb, jussive as the answer to the request of the implied verb أقيموا, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and (الواو) is the agent (الصلاة) direct object, accusative (الواو) a conjunction (ينفقوا) like يقيموا and conjoined to it (من) a preposition (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of a genitive, attached to (ينفقوا) , and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "that We have provided them with" (رزقناهم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (نا) is the agent, and (هم) the direct object (سرّا) a verbal noun in the place of a ḥāl, accusative [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the verbal noun because it is its kind, i.e. "spending in secret".] , (علانية) conjoined to (سرّا) with the wāw, accusative (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يقيموا) or (ينفقوا) , (أن) a maṣdar particle (يأتي) an imperfect verb, accusative (يوم) agent, nominative (لا) negative (بيع) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: or the noun of (لا) operating like ليس, and the khabar of لا is the preposition and its genitive noun "فيه".] , (في) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to the khabar (الواو) a conjunction (لا) redundant, to reinforce the negation (خلال) conjoined to بيع, nominative like it.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتي ... ) is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين) .
And the clause: «يقيموا ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of an implied condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ, i.e. "if they are commanded to establish the prayer, they will establish it".
And the clause: «ينفقوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يقيموا.
And the clause: «رزقناهم ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (ما) .
And the clause: «يأتي يوم ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-like (أن) .
And the clause: «لا بيع فيه ... » is in the position of a nominative, naʿt of يوم.

* Morphology:
(خلال) , a samāʿī (heard-from-the-Arabs) verbal noun of the quadriliteral خالّه, i.e. "he befriended him"; its pattern is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ, and it is singular.. or it is the plural of خلة with kasra on the khāʾ, meaning befriending and brotherhood.

* Rhetoric:
- Omission of the content of the saying:
Regarding the saying of the Exalted قُلْ لِعِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا.. etc., most of the parsers agreed that the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) is omitted, indicated by its answer, i.e. "Say to them: Establish the prayer and spend". The skilled rejected this parsing, saying: "There is something to consider in this parsing, because the answer would then be a report; for if he said this saying to them, they would comply with its requirement and establish the prayer and spend; yet they were told, and many of them did not comply, and the report of Allah is too exalted for contradiction. This subtlety is what led many of the parsers to turn away from this parsing, despite its leaping to mind at first glance. Its correctness is possible by taking the general as the majority rather than as all-inclusive. It is strengthened by two fine points: one is that this construction occurs only for one described with true faith, whose faith is lauded at the time of the command, like this verse and others, such as the saying of the Exalted قُلْ لِعِبادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ and وقُلْ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصارِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُوا فُرُوجَهُمْ. The second is its repeated occurrence for those described as servants of Allah, honoured by their being annexed to the name of Allah the Exalted. They have said that the word العباد occurs in the Mighty Book only as praise of the believers, especially when the Exalted is annexed to it with the annexation of honour. The sum is that the one commanded in this verse is one who is on the point of compliance and in the sphere of hastening to obedience, so the report of their compliance is true and sound, either in general if that is intended, or for the majority."

* Rhetoric:
1- Rational figurative usage (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī): in the attribution of misguiding to the idols in His saying أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ, i.e. they were a cause of misguidance. The attribution of misguiding to them is figurative because they are inanimate and nothing of that is conceivable from them; the one who misguides in reality is Allah the Exalted. It may also be a free metonymy (majāz mursal) whose relation is causation, because they are a cause of misguidance.
2- Antithesis (ṭibāq): in several forms, such as the saying of the Exalted رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ ما نُخْفِي وَما نُعْلِنُ وما يَخْفى عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي السَّماءِ.

* Benefits:
1- «ربّ» is a vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the first person.
The vocative, by i'rab, is of two kinds:
1- Indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative. This is the singular proper name and the specific indefinite noun.
2- Declinable, accusative. This is the non-specific indefinite noun, the annexed noun, and the noun resembling the annexed. Thus the kinds of vocative are five: singular proper name, specific indefinite, non-specific indefinite, annexed, and resembling the annexed; and the muḍāf ilayhi, which is the yāʾ, has been omitted.
A parallel to it has already been treated, so return to it in its proper places.

(ربّ) its i'rab has been given earlier «1» , (اجعلني) like اجنبي «2» , (مقيم) second direct object, accusative (الصّلاة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) a conjunction (من ذرّيّتي) its i'rab has been given earlier [Note: In verse (37) of this surah.] .
attached to an implied adjective conjoined to the first-person pronoun in (اجعلني) , i.e. "make me one who establishes the prayer, and some of my offspring" [Note: Abū Ḥayyān said in al-Baḥr: "And (من) is partitive, because he knew that among his offspring would be one who is a disbeliever, or one who neglects its establishment even if a believer."
(5, 6) In verse (37) of this surah.] , (ربّنا) its i'rab has been given earlier «5» , (الواو) a conjunction (تقبّل) an imperative verb of supplication, and the agent is "you" (دعاء) direct object, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ, omitted for lightness - or for agreement with the verse endings - and the omitted (الياء) is a pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.

* Morphology:
(مقيم) , an active participle of the quadriliteral أقام, its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.. It contains a weakening change by making quiescent and a weakening change by substitution; its origin is مقوم - with sukūn on the qāf and kasra on the wāw - then the (واو) was made quiescent and the vowel moved to the qāf - the change by making quiescent - and when the letter before the quiescent (واو) was given a kasra, it was turned into yāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
- Metaphor (istiʿāra): in the saying of the Exalted يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْحِسابُ, i.e. it is established and comes to pass. The use of "standing" in what is mentioned is either a free metonymy (majāz mursal) or a metaphor, and among that is "the war stood". It is also allowed that the reckoning be likened to a standing man by implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), with standing affirmed for it by imaginative attribution (takhyīl), or that what is meant is "the people of the reckoning stand", the muḍāf being omitted, or what belongs to its people is attributed to the reckoning figuratively.

* Benefits:
The building of the Kaʿba: Ibrāhīm confided to his son Ismāʿīl an awesome secret and a wondrous command; he said to him: "O my son, Allah has commanded me to build a house here.."
and he pointed to the place of the Kaʿba, and the two began raising the foundations of the House, asking Allah and saying: رَبَّنا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ، رَبَّنا وَاجْعَلْنا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِنا أُمَّةً مُسْلِمَةً لَكَ وَأَرِنا مَناسِكَنا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ.
Ismāʿīl was preparing the tools and bringing the stones while Ibrāhīm raised the building. Then Ibrāhīm said: "O my son, find me a stone to place under my feet, that I may be able to complete what I began and oversee what I have built." Ismāʿīl came upon the Black Stone and presented it to his father, who stood on it building, while Ismāʿīl handed him the stones and moved around the structure until the building of the House was completed, which became a resort for the people. [Translator's note: the source prints «حيث أقام عليه بيني» ("where he stood on it, building me"), which seems to be a slip for «يبني».] And Allah answered Ibrāhīm's prayer: فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ وَارْزُقْهُمْ مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ, Sūrat Ibrāhīm, verse 38.

safi-cedvel:42-43.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing (تحسبنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a jussive, and the agent is "you", and (النون) is for emphasis (الله) the divine name, first direct object, accusative (غافلا) second direct object, accusative (عن) a preposition (ما) a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, the clause after it being the ṣila, and the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "the wrongdoers do".] (يعمل) an imperfect verb, nominative (الظالمون) agent, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw (إنّما) a restrictive particle (kāffa) and the restricted (يؤخّرهم) like يعمل ... and (هم) a pronoun, direct object, and the agent is "he" (ليوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤخّر) , (تشخص..
الأبصار) like يعمل الظالمون (في) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (تشخص) .
Clause: «لا تحسبنّ ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يعمل الظّالمون ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-like (ما) and the interpreted maṣdar (ما يعمل ... ) is in the position of a genitive by the preposition, attached to (غافلا) and the clause: «يؤخّرهم ... » has no grammatical position, a clarifying resumption.
And the clause: «تشخص فيه الأبصار ... » is in the position of a genitive, naʿt of يوم.
(مهطعين) a ḥāl, accusative, from الأبصار because it indicates their owners, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ [Note: or a direct object of an omitted verb, implied "you see them", the seeing then being of the heart; or a ḥāl from the pronoun in (تراهم) , the seeing then being visual.] , (مقنعي) a second ḥāl, accusative, like معطهين [Translator's note: the source prints «معطهين» for مهطعين.] (رؤوسهم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (لا) a particle of negation (يرتدّ) like يعمل (إلى) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached - (يرتدّ) , [Translator's note: the source breaks off at «متعلق-» before «(يرتدّ)».] (طرفهم) agent, nominative, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (أفئده) mubtadaʾ, nominative and (هم) like the last (هواء) khabar, nominative.
And the clause: «لا يرتدّ إليهم طرفهم ... » is in the position of an accusative, ḥāl from the pronoun in مقنعي [Note: or it is a badal of مقنعي.] .
And the clause: «أفئدتهم هواء ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause لا يرتدّ ... [Note: or it is a ḥāl without conjunction, its operator being what operates in the preceding ḥāl, or it is resumptive with no position.] .

* Morphology:
(مهطعين) , plural of مهطع, an active participle from أهطع in the sense of "hurried". Its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(مقنعي) , plural of مقنع, its nūn dropped because of annexation, an active participle like مهطع, its pattern is مفعل.
(طرف) , originally a verbal noun, then applied to the faculty of sight; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(هواء) , originally a rigid noun, used here as an adjective meaning empty or void; for this reason the sense of the tāʾ that indicates plurality is implied in it and it remained singular; its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ.. The final hamza is changed from yāʾ because it is pluralised as أهوية; when the yāʾ came final after a quiescent alif it was turned into hamza.

* Benefits:
1- عَمَّا يَعْمَلُ الظَّالِمُونَ: When the preposition «عن» enters the relative «ما», it is written with the alif, as in this verse. When it enters an interrogative noun, the alif is dropped and it is written with the mīm only, as in the saying of the Exalted: عَمَّ يَتَساءَلُونَ؟ ..
2- (مهطعين) : a ḥāl, and the ḥāl is an indefinite accusative noun that explains the state of the agent or the direct object, or both together at the occurrence of the action.
An example of a ḥāl explaining the state of the agent is: (سأزحف ثائرا متمردا) ("I shall advance, rebelling, defiant"), and of the object: (ركب عليّ السيارة مسرعة) ("ʿAlī rode the car, speeding").
Kinds of ḥāl: a- The singular ḥāl: that which is neither a clause nor a quasi-clause, and agrees with its ṣāḥib in gender (masculine and feminine) and in number (singular, dual and plural), such as: (واجه الصّعاب قويا) ("he faced the difficulties, strong"), (واجها الصّعاب قويين) ("the two faced the difficulties, strong"), (واجهوا الصّعاب أقوياء) ("they faced the difficulties, strong").
b- The quasi-clause ḥāl, which comes as an attached element (adverb or preposition and its genitive noun), such as: (الصيف على الجبال أجمل منه على الشاطئ) ("Summer on the mountains is more beautiful than on the shore").
c- The ḥāl as a clause (nominal or verbal), such as: رأيت زيدا وهو خارج ("I saw Zayd while he was going out"), and رأيت زيدا يخرج ("I saw Zayd going out").
It is required of a clause occurring as a ḥāl that it contain a link tying it to the ṣāḥib al-ḥāl, and this link may be:
(1) the wāw alone, such as: (لن نفعل والعدوّ متربص) ("We shall not do it while the enemy lies in wait").
(2) or the pronoun alone, such as: (جئت وقد هبط الظلام) ("I came when darkness had fallen").
(3) or the pronoun and the wāw together, such as: لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكارى.

safi-cedvel:44-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (أنذر) an imperative verb, and the agent is "you" (الناس) direct object, accusative (يوم) second direct object, accusative, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "warn them of its terrors" (يأتيهم) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ, and (هم) a pronoun, direct object, (العذاب) agent, nominative (الفاء) a conjunction (يقول) like يأتي (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of a nominative, agent (ظلموا) a past verb and its agent (ربّنا) its i'rab has been given earlier [Note: In verse (37) of this surah.] , (أخّرنا) , like انذر.. and (نا) a pronoun, direct object (إلى أجل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أخّرنا) , (قريب) naʿt of أجل, genitive (نجب) an imperfect verb, jussive, the answer to the request, and the agent is "we" (دعوتك) direct object, accusative.. and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (نتّبع الرسل) like نجب دعوتك, and the end of the verb was given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescents (الهمزة) for interrogation (الواو) a conjunction (لم) a particle of negation and jussive (تكونوا) a defective imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the noun of تكون (أقسمتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (تم) is a pronoun, agent (ما) negative (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to a preposed khabar (من) a redundant preposition (زوال) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postposed mubtadaʾ.
Clause: «أنذر الناس ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يأتيهم العذاب ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «يقول الذين ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause يأتيهم العذاب.
And the clause: «ظلموا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين) .
And the clause: «النّداء وجوابها ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «أخّرنا ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
And the clause: «نجب ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of an implied condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «نتّبع ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نجب..
And the clause: «لم تكونوا ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of an implied saying..
And the clause: «القول المقدّرة معطوفة على جملة يقول الذين ظلموا. [Translator's note: the source text of this clause is incomplete as printed, lacking the closing guillemet and the opening «وجملة» of the implied clause; it reads "the implied saying clause is conjoined to the clause يقول الذين ظلموا".]
And the clause: «أقسمتم ... » is in the position of an accusative, khabar of تكونوا.
And the clause: «ما لكم من زوال ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the oath.
(الواو) a conjunction (سكنتم) like أقسمتم (في مساكن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (سكنتم) , (الّذين) a relative, muḍāf ilayhi (ظلموا) like the first (أنفسهم) direct object, accusative.. and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) resumptive (تبيّن) a past verb and the agent is omitted, understood from the context of the speech, i.e. "their state became clear" (كيف) an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the position of an accusative, ḥāl, its operator being (فعلنا) which is a verb and agent (الباء) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (فعلنا) , (الواو) resumptive (ضربنا) like فعلنا (لكم) like the first, attached to (ضربنا) , (الأمثال) direct object, accusative.
And the clause: «سكنتم ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause أقسمتم [Note: it may be a ḥāl with an implied قد.] .
And the clause: «ظلموا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين) .
And the clause: «تبيّن لكم (الحال) ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «فعلنا ... » has no grammatical position, a clarifying resumption.
And the clause: «ضربنا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(زوال) a verbal noun of the triliteral زال, its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ; there are other verbal nouns, among them زول with fatḥa and sukūn, and زوالان on the pattern فعلان with two fatḥas.

safi-cedvel:46-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (قد) a particle of certainty (مكروا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and (الواو) is the agent (مكرهم) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative [Note: Abū Ḥayyān said: "What is preserved is that مكر is not made transitive to a direct object by itself; the Exalted said: وإذ يمكر بك الذين كفروا, and 'Zayd is مكور' is not preserved; rather one says 'ممكور به'." End.] . (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (عند) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted preposed khabar (الله) the divine name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (مكرهم) a postposed mubtadaʾ, nominative, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the recompense for their plotting" or "the knowledge of their plotting".. and (هم) like the first (الواو) resumptive (إن) negative [Note: or lightened from (إنّ) , i.e. "they plotted to remove what is equal to the mountains in firmness, but they were unable to do so". It is conditional in the opinion of Ibn Hishām.] , (كان) a defective past verb - an abrogator [Note: or it is complete, i.e. "their plot did not exist so that the laws and prophethoods, which are like the mountains in their firmness, would pass away by it."] - (مكرهم) the noun of kāna, nominative, and (هم) like the first (اللام) the lām of cause [Note: Ibn Hishām rejected that the lām be the lām of denial (juḥūd), and said in brief: "There is something to consider in this statement, because the particle of negation is other than (ما) or (لم), and the agents of (كان) and (تزول) differ.. The apparent is that it is the lām of purpose (lām kay) and (إن) is conditional, i.e.: with Allah is the recompense of their plotting, and it is a greater plot than theirs, even if their plot, by its intensity, was prepared for the removal of great matters likened in their greatness to mountains." End; the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "so with Allah is the recompense of their plotting".] , (تزول) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām (من) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (تزول) and من is causal (الجبال) agent, nominative.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تزول) is in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted khabar of كان [Note: or attached to the complete (كان) .] .
Clause: «قد مكروا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «عند الله مكرهم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «كان مكرهم..» has no grammatical position, resumptive. [Note: The meaning stated: their plot was not prepared to remove mountains; and it is an illustration of the affair of the Messenger ﷺ.]
And the clause: «تزول منه الجبال ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle-like (أن) .
(الفاء) a conjunction linking the effect to the cause [Note: or a connecting particle for an implied conditional apodosis.] , (لا تحسبنّ الله مخلف) like ولا تحسبنّ الله غافلا [Note: In verse (42) of this surah.] , (وعده) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (رسله) first direct object of the active participle مخلف, which is annexed to its second object وعد [Note: If (مخلف) is made transitive to one, then (رسل) is the object of the verbal noun وعد.] and (الهاء) like the last (إنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative (الله) the divine name, the noun of inna (عزيز) khabar of inna, nominative (ذو) a second khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw (انتقام) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
And the clause: «لا تحسبنّ ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied clause, i.e. "be alert, so do not think".. or conjoined to the preceding resumptive clause قد مكروا ... [Note: or it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if the state of the wrongdoers is such in plotting, then do not think that Allah ...] .
And the clause: «إنّ الله عزيز ... » has no grammatical position, causal.
(يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to انتقام [Note: or attached to مخلف وعده رسله.. and inna and what follows is parenthetical. Or it is a direct object of an omitted verb, implied "remember".] , (تبدّل) a passive imperfect verb, nominative (الأرض) deputy agent, nominative (غير) direct object, accusative [Note: and it is originally an adjective of an omitted noun, i.e. "an earth other than the earth".] , (الأرض) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) a conjunction (السموات) conjoined to the deputy agent, nominative (الواو) resumptive (برزوا) like مكروا (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (برزوا) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for the recompense of Allah" (الواحد) naʿt of the divine name, genitive (القهّار) a second naʿt, genitive.
And the clause: «تبدّل الأرض ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «برزوا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: al-Jamal allows it to be conjoined to the clause تبدّل, making the past in the sense of the imperfect, i.e. "and the Day they come forth to Allah ..."] , or a ḥāl with an implied قد.

* Morphology:
(مخلف) , an active participle of the quadriliteral أخلف, its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
- Explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): in the saying of the Exalted وَإِنْ كانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ الْجِبالُ, where by His saying لتزول منه الجبال their plot is likened to mountains for its enormity and intensity, their absorption in it and their reaching the utmost of it; and His law, His signs and the lofty teachings and clear proofs He sent down upon His Prophet are likened to mountains in their firmness and their being established in the souls of the believers.

* Benefits:
1- مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ:
مخلف is the second direct object of the verb «تحسبنّ» and it is annexed. Had it been read detached from annexation, with tanwīn, «مخلفا وعده», it would operate as an active participle, and وعده would become the direct object of the active participle. There is a continuation of this discussion, which we shall give its due later on.
(2) يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ.
The commentators and thinkers took various positions on the substitution; the most important are two:
The first is that the substitution is from one state to another with the original remaining as it is.
The second is that the substitution is the removal of a thing and its replacement by another.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ}: it may be nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «ألر», if we say that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the clause after it a naʿt (adjective); it may be the khabar of a latent mubtadaʾ, i.e. "This is a Book"; and it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being the clause after it — beginning with an indefinite noun being permissible because it is qualified by implication, its implied form being: "a Book — and what a Book!", meaning a mighty one among the heavenly Books.

His words: «لِتُخْرِجَ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أَنْزَلْنا». It has been read «ليَخْرج الناسُ», with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the rāʾ, from «خَرَجَ يَخْرُج», with «الناس» nominative as the fāʿil (agent).

His words: «بإذنِ» may be attached to the act of bringing out, i.e. by His facilitating and easing it; and it may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of «تُخْرِجَ», i.e. "being permitted".

His words: {إلى صِرَاطِ}: there are two views. First: it is a badal (substitute) from His words {إِلَى النور}, with repetition of the governing word; the separation by the prepositional phrase does no harm, because it is among the dependents of the governor of the substituted-for element. Second: it is attached to an omitted element as the answer to an implied question, as though it were said: "To which light?" — "To the path."

semin-durr:2-2.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {الله الذي}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read the word of majesty in the nominative, and the rest — and al-Aṣmaʿī transmitted it from [Nāfiʿ] — in the genitive.

The nominative is on two views. First: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the relative noun after it, or is omitted, its implied form being: "Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, is the Mighty, the Praiseworthy", omitted because what preceded indicates it. Second: it is the khabar of a latent mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is Allah", and that is by way of praise.

The genitive is as a badal (substitute) according to Abū al-Baqāʾ, al-Ḥawfī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya, and as ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) according to al-Zamakhsharī, who said: "because it has come to be treated like proper names, owing to its predominant use for the One rightly worshipped, like «النجم» for the Pleiades." The Shaykh said: "This reasoning is only complete if its origin is «الإله» and then what was mentioned at the beginning of this topic was done to it." Master Ibn ʿUṣfūr said: "An attribute is not put before the qualified noun except where it is heard, and that is rare. The Arabs have two ways in it. One: the attribute is put first as it is; the grammarians have two analyses of this: one, that it is parsed as a fronted attribute; the other, that the qualified noun is made a badal from its attribute. The second of the two ways: that the attribute is put in construct with the qualified noun. On this basis {العزيز الحميد} may be parsed as a fronted attribute. Among instances of the attribute being put first is the poet's saying:
286 - 5- والمُؤْمِنِ العائذاتِ الطيرِ يَمْسَحُها ... رُكْبانُ مكةَ بين الغِيل والسَّنَدِ
(By the One who grants safety to the birds that take refuge [in the sanctuary], whom the riders of Mecca stroke between al-Ghīl and al-Sanad.)
and another's saying:
286 - 6- وبالطويل العُمْرِ عُمْراً حَيْدَراً ...
(And by the long life, a life [that is] …)
meaning: the birds that take refuge, and by the long life." I say: this is where the qualified noun is not indefinite; when it is indefinite we have another treatment: that the attribute is made accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

His words: {وَوَيْلٌ}: beginning with it is permissible because it is an imprecation, like «سلامٌ عليكم». «للكافرين» is its khabar, and {مِنْ عَذَابٍ} is attached to «الويل». The Shaykh disallowed this, because it entails separating the maṣdar (verbal noun) from its dependent. A discussion of this has been given to you: namely, that this is forbidden only where the maṣdar is resolvable into a maṣdar particle and a verb. For that reason they allowed {بِمَا صَبَرْتُمْ} [al-Raʿd: 24] to be attached to «سلام» and raised no objection to it; that was given in the preceding sura, and there is no difference between the two places.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the connection of His words {مِنْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ} with «الويل»? I say: because the meaning is 'they wail on account of a severe punishment'." The Shaykh said: "Its apparent sense indicates supplying a governor to which {مِنْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ} is attached." It may also be attached to an omitted element as an attribute of the mubtadaʾ; this is free of the objection above, and the separation by the khabar does no harm.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {الذين يَسْتَحِبُّونَ}: it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is «أولئك» and what follows it; it may be the khabar of a latent mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who"; it may be accusative by an implied verb of praise (in both cases); and it may be genitive as a badal (substitute), ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) or naʿt (adjective) — this was said by al-Zamakhsharī, Abū al-Baqāʾ, al-Ḥawfī and others. The Shaykh rejected it because it involves separation by an extraneous element, namely His words {مِنْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ}. He said: "Its parallel, if it is an attribute, is that you say: 'The house belongs to Zayd, the beautiful, the Qurashī' — and this is not permissible, because you have separated Zayd from his attribute by something extraneous to both, namely the attribute of the house, and that is not permissible. The eloquent construction is to say: 'The beautiful house belongs to Zayd the Qurashī', or: 'The house belongs to Zayd the Qurashī, the beautiful one.'"

«يَسْتَحِبُّون»: the form istafʿala here has the sense of afʿala, like «استجاب» in the sense of «أجاب»; or it is in its proper meaning and is made to imply the sense of "preferring", which is why it is made transitive with «على».

Al-Ḥasan read «ويُصِدُّون», from «أَصَدَّ»; «أَصَدَّ» is transferred from the intransitive «صَدَّ», and the object is omitted, i.e. others or themselves.

And {وَيَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجاً}: its like has been discussed before.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِلاَّ بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِ}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "except speaking in the language of his people". The generality read «بلسان» on the pattern of «كِتاب», i.e. "in the language of his people". Abū al-Jawzāʾ, Abū al-Sammāl and Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī read «بِلِسْنِ», with kasra on the lām and sukūn on the sīn. There are two views about it. First: the two have one meaning, like «الرِّيش» and «الرِّياش». Second: «اللسان» is applied both to the well-known organ and to language, whereas «اللِّسْن» is specific to language; Ibn ʿAṭiyya and the author of al-Lawāmiḥ mentioned this.

Abū Rajāʾ, Abū al-Mutawakkil and al-Jaḥdarī read «بِلُسُن», with ḍamma on the lām and the sīn; it is the plural of «لِسان», like «كِتاب» and «كُتُب». It has also been read with sukūn on the sīn only, which is a lightening of the preceding reading, as in «رُسْل» for «رُسُل» and «كُتْب» for «كُتُب».

The hāʾ in «قومه» apparently refers back to the «رسول» mentioned. From al-Ḍaḥḥāk: that it refers to Muḥammad ﷺ; they judged him mistaken in that, since the meaning would become that the Torah and others were sent down in the language of the Arabs so that the Prophet ﷺ might explain the Torah to them.

His words: {فَيُضِلُّ}: a resumption of a statement; it may not be made accusative by conjunction to what precedes, because the conjoined is like what it is conjoined to in meaning, and the messengers were sent to make clear, not to lead astray. Al-Zajjāj said: "Were it read in the accusative, on the basis that the lām is the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba), it would be permissible."

semin-durr:5-5.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَنْ أَخْرِجْ}: «أنْ» may be maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), i.e. "with: bring out". The bāʾ in «بآياتنا» is for the ḥāl (circumstantial), and this [implied bāʾ] is for transitivity. It may also be explicative (mufassira) of the sending. It has been said that it is rather redundant (zāʾida), and that is an error.

His words: {وَذَكِّرْهُمْ}: it may be conjoined to «أَخْرِجْ», and so be part of the explanation; or it may not be conjoined, and so be resumptive. «أيام الله» is an expression for His favours, as in the saying:
286 - 7- وأيامٍ لنا غُرٍّ طِوالٍ ... عَصَيْنا المَلْكَ فيها أن نَدِينا
(And many bright, long days of ours, in which we defied the king, refusing to submit.)
or for His retributions, as in the saying:
286 - 8- وأيامُنا مشهورةٌ في عَدُوِّنا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And our days are famous among our enemies …)
Its rationale: the Arabs use figurative speech, attributing the event figuratively to the time and putting it in construct with it, as in their sayings: "a fasting day", "a night standing in prayer", and "the plotting of the night".

semin-durr:6-6.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِذْ أَنجَاكُمْ}: three views are possible. First: it is accusative by «نِعْمَةَ». Second: by «عليكم». What clarifies this is what al-Zamakhsharī said: "«إذ أنجاكم» is an adverb of «النعمة» in the sense of bestowing, i.e. His bestowing upon you at that time. If you say: may it be accusative by «عليكم»? I say: it is one of two cases: either [«عليكم»] is a complement (ṣila) of «النعمة» in the sense of bestowing, or not a complement, if by «النعمة» you mean the gift. If it is a complement, it does not govern it; and if it is not a complement, in the sense 'Remember Allah's favour, resting upon you', it governs it. The difference between the two views becomes clear in that when you say {نِعْمَةَ الله عَلَيْكُمْ}, if you make it a complement it is not a complete utterance until you say 'abundant' or the like; otherwise it is a complete utterance." Third: it is a badal (substitute) from «نعمة», i.e. "Remember the time of your being rescued", and it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl).

His words: {وَيُذَبِّحُونَ}: another ḥāl (circumstantial) from {آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ}. In al-Baqara it is without the wāw, because there it was meant as an explanation; so the «سَوْم» (infliction) here is other than the «سَوْم» there.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ}: it may be conjoined to {إِذْ أَنجَاكُمْ}, or it may be accusative by «اذكروا» as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not an adverb. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be conjoined to «نعمة», so that it is part of Moses' speech, the implied form being: "And when Moses said: Remember Allah's favour, and remember when He proclaimed." The parallel of this has been given in al-Aʿrāf. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يَذْبَحون» without doubling.
[Translator's note: the word «يَذْبَحون» belongs to the previous verse (Ibrāhīm: 6, {وَيُذَبِّحُونَ}); the source records the reading here.]

semin-durr:9-9.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {قَوْمِ نُوحٍ}: a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf [bayān] (explicative apposition).

His words: {والذين مِن بَعْدِهِمْ}: it may be conjoined to the first relative noun, or to the element substituted for; or it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is {لاَ يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلاَّ الله}, with «جاءَتْهُم» another khabar. On the preceding views, «لا يعلمهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الذين», or from the pronoun in {مِن بَعْدِهِمْ}, since that occurs as a ṣila (relative clause). This is what Abū al-Baqāʾ meant by saying "a ḥāl from the pronoun in {مِن بَعْدِهِمْ}"; he does not mean the genitive pronoun, because his doctrine is to forbid a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi, even though some allowed it in certain cases. He and al-Zamakhsharī also allowed it to be resumptive.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The clause consisting of His words {لاَ يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلاَّ الله} is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ)." The Shaykh refuted him on the ground that a parenthesis occurs only between two parts one of which requires the other. Likewise, when al-Zamakhsharī parsed «والذين» as a mubtadaʾ and «لا يَعْلمهم» as its khabar, he said: "The clause made of the mubtadaʾ and khabar is parenthetical," and the Shaykh objected to him likewise with what preceded. It can be answered in both places that al-Zamakhsharī may hold that «جاءَتْهم» is a ḥāl from what precedes, so the parenthesis falls between the ḥāl and the one it describes — and this is a sound statement.

His words: {فردوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ في أَفْوَاهِهِمْ}: the pronouns may all be for the disbelievers, i.e. the disbelievers put their hands back into their mouths out of rage, with «في» in its proper sense of location; or they put their hands over their mouths laughing and mocking, so «في» means «على»; or they pointed with their hands to their tongues and what they had uttered of their saying "We have disbelieved", so it means «إلى». The nominative pronoun may be for the disbelievers and the other two for the messengers, on the basis that "hands" means favours, i.e. they returned the messengers' favours — namely their counsels — into the messengers' mouths, since when they belied them it is as though they sent them back whence they came, by way of a figure. [This meaning may also be intended with "hands" meaning the limbs.] The first two may be for the disbelievers and the last for the messengers, i.e. the disbelievers put their hands to the messengers' mouths, i.e. "Close your mouths!", signalling them to be silent; or they placed them on their mouths, thereby preventing them from speaking.

It has been said that «في» here means the bāʾ. Al-Farrāʾ said: "We have found among the Arabs those who put «في» in place of the bāʾ. One says: 'He admitted you into (bi-) the Garden' and 'in (fī) the Garden'." And he cited:
286 - 9- وأرغَبُ فيها عن لَقيطٍ ورَهْطِهِ ... ولكنَّني عن سِنْبِسٍ لستُ أرغبُ
(Through her I hold myself above Laqīṭ and his clan, but from Sinbis I do not turn away.)
i.e. "I hold myself above … by her". Abū ʿUbayda said: "This is a figurative expression; the Arabs say 'He put his hand back into his mouth' when he refrains from answering"; al-Akhfash said this too. Al-Qutaybī said: "We have not heard anyone say 'He put his hand back into his mouth' meaning he abandoned what he was commanded." This was rejected, for whoever has memorised [a usage] is a proof against whoever has not.

Ṭalḥa read «تَدْعُونَّا», assimilating the nūn of the nominative into the nūn of the pronoun, just as it is assimilated into the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya).

semin-durr:10-10.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَفِي الله شَكٌّ}: two views are possible for «شَكٌّ». The more apparent: it is a fāʿil (agent) governed by the preposition before it, which is permissible because it leans on the interrogative. Second: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the prepositional phrase. The first is preferable; indeed it ought to be the only option, because the second entails separating the attribute from the qualified noun by something extraneous, namely the mubtadaʾ — unlike the first, where the separating element is not extraneous, since it is a fāʿil, and the fāʿil is like part of what makes it nominative. What shows this is their allowing «ما رأيت رجلاً أحسنَ في عينه الكحلُ منه في عين زيد» ("I have not seen a man in whose eye kohl is more beautiful than it is in Zayd's eye"), with «أحسنَ» accusative as an attribute and «الكحلُ» nominative as the fāʿil of the afʿal form; the separation by it between afʿal and «مِنْ» does no harm because it is like part of what makes it nominative. They did not allow «أحسن» to be nominative as a fronted khabar with «الكحلُ» a delayed mubtadaʾ, lest afʿal be separated from «مِنْ» by something extraneous. The point of citing this question: they made the mubtadaʾ extraneous, unlike the fāʿil. This question has a place other than this.

The generality read «فاطرِ» in the genitive. There are two views in it: naʿt (adjective) and badal (substitute) — Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. There is a reservation about it, for substitution with derived words is rare; had he made it ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) it would have been easier. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The hamza of disapproval was put on the adverbial phrase because the discourse is not about the doubt but about what is doubted, and that it does not admit doubt because of the manifestness of the proofs and their testimony to it."

His words: «لِيَغْفِرَ»: the lām is attached to the calling, i.e. for the sake of your Lord's forgiveness, as in the saying:
287 - 0- دَعَوْتُ لِما نابني مِسْوَرا ... فَلَبَّى فَلَبَّى يَدَيْ مِسْوَرِ
(I called Miswar for what had befallen me, and he answered — so blessed be Miswar's hands, again and again.)
The lām may also be the one that makes transitive, as when you say "I called you to Zayd", and His words {إِذْ تُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى [الإيمان]} [Ghāfir: 10]. The implied form: "He calls you to the forgiveness of your sins."

His words: {أَن تَصُدُّونَا}: the generality read the nūn without doubling. Ṭalḥa read it doubled, just as he doubled «تَدْعُونَّا». There are two explanations of it. First: what was given for its parallel, that «أَنْ» is the lightened one (mukhaffafa), not the one that makes accusative, its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the absence of a separator between it and the verbal clause is anomalous. Second: it is the one that makes accusative but was left without effect, by analogy with the maṣdar-forming «ما», like the reading «أَنْ يُتِمُّ» with «يُتِمُّ» nominative. The discussion of this has been given.

And «مِنْ» in {مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمْ}: it has been said to be redundant (zāʾida); it has been said to be partitive; and it has been said to mean substitution, i.e. in place of the punishment of your sins, as in His words {أَرَضِيتُمْ بالحياة الدنيا مِنَ الآخرة} [al-Tawba: 38].

His words: «تُرِيْدون» may be a second attribute of «بَشَرٌ», construed according to its meaning, because it is equivalent to «القوم» and «الرَّهْط», as in His words {أَبَشَرٌ يَهْدُونَنَا} [al-Taghābun: 6]; or it may be resumptive.

semin-durr:11-11.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمَا كَانَ لَنَآ أَن نَّأْتِيَكُمْ}: the khabar (predicate) of «كان» may be «لنا» and {أَن نَّأْتِيَكُمْ} its noun, i.e. "It was not for us to bring you an authority", with {إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِ الله} a ḥāl (circumstantial). Or the khabar may be {إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِ الله}, with «لنا» for clarification (tabyīn).

semin-durr:12-12.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمَا لَنَآ أَلاَّ}: like His words {وَمَا لَنَآ أَلاَّ نُقَاتِلَ} [al-Baqara: 246], which has been discussed. «لَنَصْبِرَنَّ» is the answer to an oath. His words «ما آذَيْتُمونا»: «ما» may be maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), which is the preferable view, since there is no need for a linking pronoun claimed to be omitted contrary to rule. Second: it is a nominal relative noun, with the referent pronoun omitted gradually, since the original is «آذيْتُمونا به»; then the bāʾ was dropped, so the verb reached it by itself [and then it was omitted].
[Translator's note: the bracketed final clause is added for clarity; the source ends at "reached it by itself".]

Al-Ḥasan read the lām of command in «فَلْيَتَوَكَّلْ» with kasra, and that is the original.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
And {لَنُخْرِجَنَّكُمْ}: the answer to an implied oath, like His words «ولَنَصْبِرَنَّ».

His words: {أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ}: there are three views about «أوْ». First: it is in its proper sense of one of two things. Second: it means «حتى» ("until"). Third: it means «إلا» ("unless"), as in their saying «لأَلْزَمَنَّكَ أو تَقْضِيَني حقي» ("I will stick to you unless you pay me my due"). The last two views are rejected, since neither the construction with «حتى» nor that with «إلا» is valid with His words «لَتَعُودُونَّ», unlike the preceding example.

«العَوْد» here may be in its proper sense, i.e. "you shall surely return", with {فِي مِلَّتِنَا} attached to it; or it may mean "becoming", in which case the prepositional phrase is in the position of the accusative as its khabar (predicate); al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. [He said:] "If you say: it is as though they had been in their religion so that they would return to it — I say: Allah forbid! Rather «العَوْد» means 'becoming', and this is very common in the speech of the Arabs, so widespread that you scarcely hear them use «صار», but rather «عاد»: 'I no longer (mā ʿudtu) see him', 'he came not to speak to me', 'so-and-so no longer has wealth'. Or they addressed with it every messenger and those who believed in him, and in the address gave the group precedence over the individual." His words "Or they addressed …" to the end are the first view with the interpretation mentioned, and it is a good interpretation.

His words: {لَنُهْلِكَنَّ}: the answer to a latent oath. That oath and its answer admit two views. First: it is on the implication of a verb of saying, i.e. "He said: We shall surely destroy". Second: He treated revelation (al-īḥāʾ) like saying, because it is a kind of it.

Abū Ḥaywa read «لَيُهْلِكَنَّ» and «لَيُسْكِنَنَّكم» with the yāʾ of the third person, to match His words «ربُّهم».

semin-durr:14-14.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {ذلك}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), pointing to the bequeathing of the land; «لِمَنْ خاف» is the khabar (predicate). «مَقامي» admits three views. First: it is inserted (muqḥam, i.e. pleonastic), and that is far-fetched, since nouns are not inserted. Second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in construct with its agent.

Al-Farrāʾ said: "«مَقامي» is a maṣdar [in construct] with its agent, i.e. My standing over him with guarding." Third: it is a noun of place. Al-Zajjāj said: "the place of his standing before the reckoning", like His words {وَلِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ} [al-Raḥmān: 46].

His words: «وَعِيْد»: Warsh from Nāfiʿ kept the yāʾ here and in two places in Qāf — {كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ الرسل فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ} [verse 14] and {فَذَكِّرْ بالقرآن مَن يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ} [verse 45] — in continuous reading, and dropped it in pause; the rest dropped it both in continuous reading and in pause.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {واستفتحوا}: the generality read «استفتحوا» as a past verb. There are several views about its pronoun. First: it refers back to the noble messengers, and «الاستفتاح» means seeking victory: {إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُواْ فَقَدْ جَآءَكُمُ الفتح} [al-Anfāl: 19]; and it has been said: seeking judgment, from «الفُتاحة» (judgment). Second: it refers back to the disbelievers, i.e. the nations of the messengers sought a decision against them, as in His words {فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنَا حِجَارَةً مِّنَ السمآء} [al-Anfāl: 32]. It has been said: it refers to both parties, since each sought victory over the other. It has been said: it refers to Quraysh, because in the years of drought they sought rain and were not given rain; on this view it is resumptive, whereas on the other views it is conjoined to His words {فأوحى إِلَيْهِمْ}.

Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «واسْتَفْتِحوا» in the form of the imperative, a command to the messengers to seek victory; this strengthens its referring back to the messengers in the well-known reading. The implied form: "He said to them: We shall surely destroy …, and said to them: Seek victory."

His words: «وخابَ»: in the reading of the generality it is conjoined to an omitted element, its implied form being: "they were given victory and triumphed, and [every stubborn tyrant] failed." It may also be conjoined to «اسْتَفْتحوا» on the view that its pronoun is for the disbelievers. In the other reading it is conjoined to the omitted verb of saying; it has been stated before that a request may be conjoined to a statement and vice versa.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
And {مِّن وَرَآئِهِ جَهَنَّمُ}: a clause in the position of the genitive as an attribute of «جبارٍ». The attribute may also be the prepositional phrase alone, with «جهنمُ» a fāʿil (agent) governed by it. His words «ويُسْقََى» are an attribute conjoined to the attribute before it — a verbal clause conjoined to a nominal one; if you make the attribute the prepositional phrase alone and attach it to a verb, it is a verbal clause conjoined to a verbal clause. It has been said: it is conjoined to an omitted element, i.e. "he is cast into it and is given to drink".

«وراء» here is in its proper sense ("behind"). It has been said: it means «أمام» ("in front"), so it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād); this is what al-Zamakhsharī meant by saying "before him". He cited:
287 - 1- عَسَى الكربُ الذي أَمْسَيْتُ فيه ... يكون وراءَه فَرَجٌ قريبُ
(Perhaps the distress in which I have come to be will have, beyond it, a near relief.)
This is the view of Abū ʿUbayda, Quṭrub and Ibn Jarīr. Another said on this:
287 - 2- أيَرْجُو بنو مروانَ سَمْعي وطاعتي ... وقومي تميمٌ والفلاةُ ورائِيا
(Do the Banū Marwān hope for my hearing and obedience, while my people are Tamīm and the open desert lies "behind" me?)
i.e. before me. Another said:
287 - 3- أليس ورائي إنْ تراخَتْ مَنِيَّتي ... لُزومُ العَصَا تُحْنى عليها الأَصابعُ
(Is there not "behind" me, if my death is delayed, clinging to the staff, the fingers bent over it?)
Thaʿlab said: "It is a noun for what is hidden from you, whether it is behind you or in front of you."

His words: {مِن مَّآءٍ صَدِيدٍ}: there are three views about «صديد». First: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «ماء», and there are two interpretations of this. One: it is on the omission of the particle of comparison, i.e. "water like pus"; on this view the water they drink is not pus but like it. The other: since pus resembles water, it was called "water" though it is not truly water; on this view they drink the very pus that resembles water — this is the view of Ibn ʿAṭiyya. Al-Ḥawfī and others held that it is an attribute. There is a reservation about this, since it is not derived — except for one who explained it as «صَدِيد» in the sense of «مَصْدود» ("repelled"), taking it from «الصَّدّ», as if, because of its loathsomeness, it is repelled from, i.e. everyone refrains from it.

Second: it is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); al-Zamakhsharī held this. It is not the doctrine of the Basrans that it occurs with indefinite nouns; only the Kufans held that, and al-Fārisī also followed them.

Third: it is a badal (substitute). Al-Fārisī also parsed «زَيتونةٍ» in His words «[يُوقَدُ] مِنْ شجرةٍ مباركةٍ زَيْتُونةٍ» as ʿaṭf bayān.

«الصَّديد» is a fluid that flows from the bodies of the people of the Fire. It has been said: it is the pus that lies between skin and flesh.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {يَتَجَرَّعُهُ}: the clause may be an attribute of «ماءٍ», a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يُسْقَى», or resumptive. «تَجَرَّع» is of the form tafaʿʿala, and it has several possibilities. First: it is the reflexive-compliant (muṭāwiʿ) of «جَرَّعْتُه», like «عَلَّمْتُه فَتَعَلَّمَ» ("I taught him and he learned").

Second: it is for effortful striving, like «تَحَلَّم», i.e. he forces himself to gulp it; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. Third: it indicates gradualness, like «فَهَّمته», i.e. he takes it bit by bit by gulping, just as one understands bit by bit through being made to understand. Fourth: it has the sense of the bare form «جَرَع», like «عَدَوْت الشيءَ» and «تَعَدَّيْتُه».

{وَلاَ يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ}, i.e. he does not come near to swallowing it easily — so how could he actually do so? — like His words «لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاها», which will come, Allah willing.

His words: {وَمِن وَرَآئِهِ عَذَابٌ غَلِيظٌ}: there are two views about the pronoun. The more apparent: it refers back to «كل جبار». Second: it refers back to the punishment mentioned before.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مَّثَلُ الذين كَفَرُواْ}: there are several views. First — the doctrine of Sībawayh — it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "Among what is recited to you is the likeness of those who disbelieved." The clause {أَعْمَالُهُمْ كَرَمَادٍ} is then resumptive, answering an implied question, as though it were said: "What is their likeness?" and it was said: "Such and such." «المَثَل» is a borrowed term for a description in which there is something remarkable, as when you say: "Zayd's description: his honour is guarded and his wealth freely given."

Second: «مَثَل» is a mubtadaʾ, «أعمالُهم» a second mubtadaʾ, «كرمادٍ» the khabar of the second, and the second with its khabar the khabar of the first. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "To me this is the most preferable of the views; it is as though you said: what is established in the mind as a likeness for those who disbelieved is this clause mentioned." Al-Ḥawfī inclined to it. The Shaykh said: "It is not permissible, because the clause that is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ has no link connecting it to the mubtadaʾ, and it is not the mubtadaʾ itself so as to dispense with a link." I say: rather, the clause is the mubtadaʾ itself, for their likeness is itself their works being like ashes, in that none of them avails anything nor leaves any trace; it is the parallel of your saying "My father's constant refrain is: There is no god but Allah."

Third: «مَثَل» is redundant (zāʾida) — said by al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ — i.e. "Those who disbelieved, their works are like ashes"; so «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ, «أعمالُهم» a second mubtadaʾ, and «كرمادٍ» its khabar. But the addition of nouns is disallowed.

Fourth: «مَثَل» is a mubtadaʾ and «أعمالُهم» a badal (substitute) from it, on the implied form "the likeness of their works", with «كرمادٍ» the khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī said this; on this view it is a badal of the whole from the whole, with omission of the muḍāf as mentioned.

Fifth: «مَثَل» is a mubtadaʾ, «أعمالُهم» a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl) from it, and «كرمادٍ» the khabar, as in the saying of al-Zabbāʾ:
287 - 4- ما للجِمال مَشْيِها وئيدا ... أجَنْدَلاً يَحْمِلْن أم حديدا
(What is with the camels — their walking so heavily? Is it rocks they carry, or iron?)

Sixth: «مَثَل» is a mubtadaʾ and «أعمالُهم» its khabar, i.e. "the likeness of their works", the muḍāf being omitted; «كرماد» on this view is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. Abū al-Baqāʾ, when mentioning the badal view, said: "Were it [not] the Qurʾān, it would be permissible to make «أعمالهم» a badal from «الذين», as a badal of inclusion," meaning that it would be read «أعمالِهم» in the genitive — but it has not been read so.
[Translator's note: the source reads «ولو كان القرآن» ("were it the Qurʾān"); the bracketed "[not]" is supplied for the evident sense — perhaps a scribal slip for «ولو كان في غير القرآن» or similar.]

«الرماد» (ashes) is well known: it is what fire has pulverised of bodies. Its plural of multitude is «رُمُد» and of paucity «أرْمِدَة», like «جَماد», «جُمُد» and «أَجْمِدَة»; its plural «أَرْمِدَاء» is anomalous. «الرِّماد» is also a year — a year of drought. «أَرْمَدَ الماءُ» means the water became ash-coloured; «الأَرْمَدُ» is what is ash-coloured; gnats were called «رُمْد» for that reason. One says «رَمادٌ رِمْدِدٌ»: it has become fine dust.

His words: {اشتدت بِهِ الريح}: in the position of the genitive as an attribute of «رماد», and «في يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اشْتَدَّت».

His words: «عاصفٍ»: there are several views. First: it is on the implied form «عاصفٍ ريحُه» ("whose wind is stormy") or «عاصفِ الريح»; then «الريح» was omitted and the attribute was given to the day figuratively, as in their sayings "a rainy day" and "a sleeping night". Al-Harawī said: "It was omitted because it had been mentioned before, as the poet said:
287 - 5- إذا جاء يومٌ مظلِمُ الشمسِ كاسفُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When there comes a day with its sun darkened, eclipsed …)
i.e. eclipsed of sun."

Second: it is by way of relation (nasab), i.e. "possessing storminess", like «لابِن» ("milk-owner") and «تامِر» ("date-owner").

Third: it is made genitive by proximity (al-khafḍ ʿalā al-jiwār), i.e. originally «العاصف» should follow «الريح» in i'rab, one saying «اشتدَّتْ به الريحُ العاصفُ في يوم»; when it came after «اليوم» it was given its i'rab, as in their saying «جُحرُ ضَبّ خَربٍ» ("the ruined hole of a lizard"). There is a reservation about making this a case of genitive by proximity, because one of its conditions is that, if it were made an attribute of what it is cut off from in i'rab, it would be valid, as in the example mentioned; here, if you made it an attribute of «الريح» it would not be valid, because they differ in definiteness and indefiniteness in this particular construction.

Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «يوم» in construct with «عاصِفٍ». This is on the omission of the qualified noun, i.e. "on a day of stormy wind", omitted because the meaning indicating it is understood. It may also be a case of putting the qualified noun in construct with its attribute, according to those who hold that, as in «بَقْلَةُ الحَمْقَاء» ("purslane", lit. "the herb of the foolish one").

One says «ريحٌ عاصِفٌ» and «مُعْصِفٌ»; its origin is from «العَصْف», which is what is broken of the crops. This was said of a strong wind because it «تَعْصِفُ», i.e. breaks what it passes over.

His words: {لاَّ يَقْدِرُونَ}: resumptive; it is weak to make it an attribute of «يوم» with omission of the referent pronoun, i.e. "they have no power in it". «مِمَّا كَسَبُوا» is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شيء», since if it came after it, it would be an attribute. The implied form: "over anything of what they earned".

semin-durr:19-19.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَلَمْ تَرَ}: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read it with sukūn on the rāʾ. There are two views about this. First: he treated continuous reading like pause. Second: the Arabs dropped the final radical of the word even in the absence of a jussive particle, saying «ولو تَرَ ما الصبيانُ»; so when the jussive particle entered they imagined that the rāʾ was the place of the jussive. Its parallel is «لم أُبَلْ», whose origin is «أبالي»; they dropped its final radical in the indicative, and when they made it jussive they disregarded its final radical and imagined the jussive on the lām.

The seeing here is mental (qalbiyya), so «أنَّ» is in the position of the two objects or one of them, according to the disagreement. The two brothers [Translator's note: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read here {خالقَ السماوات والأرض}: «خالق» as an active participle in construct with what follows, and therefore they made what is conjoined to it — «الأرض» — genitive; and in al-Nūr {خَالقُ كُلِّ دَآبَّةٍ} [verse 45], an active participle in construct with what follows. The rest read «خَلَقَ» as a past verb, and therefore made «الأرضَ» and {كُلِّ دَآبَّةٍ} accusative. So the kasra of «السماواتِ» is a genitive in the reading of the two brothers and an accusative in the reading of the others. Were it said that in the reading of the two brothers «الأرضَ» may be accusative on one of two grounds — either by the position, or by the dropping of the tanwīn because of the meeting of two sukūns, so that «السماواتِ» would be accusative in form and position — it would not be impossible; but it has not been read so.

«بالحقِّ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلق», on the basis that the bāʾ is causal; or to an omitted element, on the basis that it is circumstantial — either from the agent, i.e. "rightfully", or from the object, i.e. "bound up with the truth".

semin-durr:21-21.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {تَبَعًا}: it may be the plural of «تابِع», like «خادِم/خَدَم» and «غائِب/غَيَب»; and it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), as in «قومٌ عَدْلٌ», in which case the three well-known interpretations apply.

His words: {مِنْ عَذَابِ الله مِن شَيْءٍ}: there are several views about «مِنْ». First: the first «مِنْ» is explicative (li-l-tabyīn) and the second partitive, the implied form being: "availing us part of the thing that is Allah's punishment" — said by al-Zamakhsharī. The Shaykh said: "This requires that {مِن شَيْءٍ} be placed before {مِنْ عَذَابِ الله}, because he made {مِن شَيْءٍ} the thing explained by 'of punishment', and what the explicative «مِنْ» explains comes before it and does not come after." I say: al-Zamakhsharī's statement is correct in meaning, for {مِنْ عَذَابِ الله}, had it come after «شيء», would be an attribute of it and explicative; when it was put first, its i'rab changed from attribute to ḥāl (circumstantial), while its meaning — namely explanation — remains unchanged.

Second: both are partitive, meaning: "Are you availing us some part of something that is part of Allah's punishment?", i.e. part of Allah's punishment — said by al-Zamakhsharī. The Shaykh said: "This requires it to be a badal (substitute), so it would be a badal of the general from the particular, and this is not said; for the partness of 'thing' is absolute, so it has no part." I say: there is no dispute that one says "part of the part"; it is a current expression. That part which is divided is a whole for its parts and a part of its whole — like the intermediate genus, which is a species for what is above it and a genus for what is below it.

Third: «مِنْ» in {مِن شَيْءٍ} is redundant (zāʾida), and «مِنْ» in {مِنْ عَذَابِ} admits two views. One: it is attached to an omitted element, because originally it is an attribute of «شيء»; when it was put first it became accusative as a ḥāl. The other: it is attached to «مُغْنُوْنَ» itself, on the basis that «من شيء» stands in place of the maṣdar, i.e. "any availing". What Abū al-Baqāʾ said clarifies this: "«مِنْ» is redundant, i.e. 'anything being of Allah's punishment', and it is construed according to the meaning, its implied form being: 'Will you ward off from us anything?' And «شيء» may stand in place of the maṣdar, i.e. 'availing', so that {مِنْ عَذَابِ الله} is attached to «مُغْنُوْن»." Al-Ḥawfī also said: "{مِنْ عَذَابِ الله} is attached to «مُغْنُون», and «مِنْ» in {مِن شَيْءٍ}, for the comprehensiveness of the genus, is redundant for emphasis."

His words: {سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْنَآ} to the end: there are two views. First: it is the speech of the arrogant. Second: it is the speech of the arrogant and the weak together. Each clause came independent, without a conjunction, to indicate that each of the meanings stands by itself and suffices as a statement. The discussion of «سواء» (equality) and the hamza after it has been given at the beginning of al-Baqara.

«الجَزَع» is the inability to bear hardship. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
287 - 6- جَزِعْتُ ولم أَجْزَعْ من البَيْنِ مَجْزِعاً ... وعَزَّيْتَ قلباً بالكواعب مُولَعا
(I grieved — yet I did not grieve at parting as one truly grieves — and you consoled a heart enamoured of full-breasted maidens.)
Al-Rāghib said: "The origin of «الجَزْع» is cutting a rope in its middle; one says «جَزَعْتُه فانْجَزَعَ». Because of the notion of interruption in it, «جَزْعُ الوادي» was said of the place where the valley is crossed; and because of the interruption of colour by its changing, a multicoloured bead was called «جَزْع»; «اللحمُ المُجَزَّع» is meat of two colours; «البُسْرَة المُجَزَّعَة» is an unripe date half of which has ripened; and «الجازِع» is a beam placed in the middle of the house on which the ends of the beams from the two sides are laid — as though it were so named from the notion of its 'grieving' at the burden placed on it, or from its cutting across the middle of the house." «الجَزَع» is more specific than grief, for «الجَزَع» is a grief that turns a person away from what he is engaged in.

«المَحيص» may be a maṣdar or a noun of place. One says «جاض», with the dotted ḍād, and «جَيْضاً» — with it and with the jīm.
[Translator's note: the last sentence appears garbled in the source. The usual statement is that one says «حاصَ … حَيْصاً» and also «جاضَ … جَيْضاً», with the jīm and the dotted ḍād, in the same sense; it is translated as written.]

semin-durr:22-22.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَعْدَ الحق}: it may be a case of the qualified noun put in construct with its attribute, i.e. "the true promise"; or «الحق» may mean the attribute of the Creator, the Exalted, i.e. Allah promised you His promise; or «الحق» may mean the resurrection and requital in general, so that it is a genuine construct.

His words: {إِلاَّ أَن دَعَوْتُكُمْ}: there are two views. The more apparent: it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because his calling is not of the genus of «السلطان», which is the clear proof. Second: it is connected (muttaṣil), because the ability to drive a person to evil is sometimes by coercion and sometimes by strengthening the motive in his heart, and that is by whispering to him, so it is a kind of having power over him.

It has been read «فلا يَلُوْموني» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, by way of a shift of person (iltifāt), as in His words {حتى إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي الفلك وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم} [Yūnus: 22].

His words: {بِمُصْرِخِيَّ}: the generality read the yāʾ with fatḥa, because a yāʾ into which another is assimilated always takes fatḥa, especially when preceded by a second kasra. Ḥamza read it with kasra, and it is the dialect of the Banū Yarbūʿ. People's statements about this reading have been in great turmoil: some are bold against it and accuse its reader of solecism (laḥn); some allow it without weakness; and some allow it with weakness.

Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī said: "I asked Abū ʿAmr about the kasra of the yāʾ, and he allowed it." This account is related from him through many routes, among them the one given, and among them: "I asked Abū ʿAmr and said: The grammarians accuse us of solecism in it. He said: It is permissible too; he only wanted to give the yāʾ a vowel, and you do not care whether you move it downward or upward." And from him: "Whoever wishes may give it fatḥa, and whoever wishes may give it kasra." And among them that he said: "With the genitive (kasra) it is good." And from him [al-Juʿfī]: "Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ came to us and I asked him about the Qurʾān, and I found him knowledgeable in it. I asked him about something [of] the reading of al-Aʿmash, and I sounded him out about {وَمَآ أَنتُمْ بِمُصْرِخِيَّ} with the kasra, and he said: It is permissible. So since he allowed it and al-Aʿmash read it, I adopted it."

Abū Ḥātim censured Abū ʿAmr for approving this reading, but no attention is paid to him, because he [Abū ʿAmr] is one of the eminent authorities of the Qurʾān, language and grammar, and he became acquainted with what [those above al-Sijistānī] did not:
287 - 7- وابنُ اللَّبُونِ إذا ما لُزَّ في قَرَنٍ ... لم يستطعْ صَوْلَةَ البُزْلِ القناعيسِ
(The two-year-old camel, when tied in one rope with the others, cannot match the charge of the mighty full-grown stallions.)
[Translator's note: the bracketed phrase is in brackets in the source; as it stands the sense seems to be that Abū ʿAmr knew what Abū Ḥātim (al-Sijistānī) did not.]

Then the scholars mentioned several explanations of it. One: the kasra is according to the rule for the meeting of two sukūns. That is, the yāʾ of the i'rab [i.e. of the sound plural] is vowelless, and the yāʾ of the speaker is originally vowelless; when they met, it was given kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns. Second: it resembles the hāʾ of the pronoun, in that each of them is a pronoun of a single letter; the hāʾ of the pronoun is extended with a wāw when it has ḍamma and with a yāʾ when it has kasra, and it takes kasra after a kasra and after a vowelless yāʾ. So it is given kasra just as the hāʾ is given kasra in «عليْهِ»; and the Banū Yarbūʿ extend it with a yāʾ, just as Ibn Kathīr extends e.g. «عليهي» with a yāʾ. Ḥamza gave this yāʾ kasra without the extension, since his principle requires its absence. Quṭrub also claimed that it is the dialect of the Banū Yarbūʿ; he said: they add a yāʾ to the yāʾ of the possessive, and cited:
287 - 8- ماضٍ إذا ما هَمَّ بالمُضِيِّ ... قال لها: هل لكِ ياتا فِيَّ
(Resolute when he is set on going, he said to her: "Have you, O you, any [liking] for me?")
Al-Farrāʾ cited it and said: "If that is sound, it is a case of the meeting of two sukūns." Abū ʿAlī said: "Al-Farrāʾ said in his book al-Taṣrīf: al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn claimed that it is correct, and he was trustworthy and discerning."

Among those who attacked it is Abū Isḥāq [Translator's note: al-Zajjāj], who said: "This reading, according to all the grammarians, is poor and contemptible, and has no aspect except a weak one." Abū Jaʿfar [Translator's note: al-Naḥḥās] said: "This has become an assimilation, and it is not permissible that the Book of Allah the Exalted be construed according to the anomalous." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is weak; they adduced as evidence for it an unattributed verse:
287 - 9- قال لها: هل لكِ ياتا فِيَّ ... قالت له: ما أنت بالمَرْضِيِّ
(He said to her: "Have you, O you, any [liking] for me?" She said to him: "You are not one to be pleased with.")
It is as though he supposed the possessive yāʾ vowelless, preceded by a vowelless yāʾ, and moved it with kasra according to the basic rule for the meeting of two sukūns. But it is not sound, because the possessive yāʾ is only ever with fatḥa where it is preceded by an alif, as in «عصايَ» — so what of it when it is preceded by a yāʾ? If you say: the first yāʾ was treated like a sound letter because of the assimilation, so it is as though it were a yāʾ that occurred [vowelless] after a vowelless sound letter, and so it was moved with kasra according to the basic rule — I say: this is a good analogy, but widespread usage, which is like a mass-transmitted report, makes analogies dwindle before it."

The Shaykh said: "As for his statement 'they adduced as evidence for it an unattributed verse', others have mentioned that it is by al-Aghlab al-ʿIjlī; and it is a dialect that remains in the mouths of many people to this day, who say «ما فِيَّ أفعلُ» with kasra on the yāʾ." I say: the one who mentioned the author of this rajaz is Shaykh Abū Shāma; he said: "I myself saw it at the beginning of his dīwān, and the beginning of this rajaz is:
288 - 0- أقبل في ثَوْبٍ مَعافِرِيِّ ... عند اختلاط الليلِ والعَشيِّ
(He came forward in a Maʿāfirī garment, when night mingled with evening.)"

Then the Shaykh said: "As for the explanation he mentioned, it is the explanation of al-Farrāʾ, which al-Zajjāj transmitted from him. As for his saying, in the course of his speech, 'where it is preceded by an alif' (ḥaythu qablahā alif), I do not know «حيث» to be put in construct with a clause headed by an adverb, as in 'Zayd sat where in front of ʿAmr is Bakr'; this construction needs to be attested by hearing." I say: the grammarians' general statement that it is put in construct with clauses suffices for this; there is no need to trace every single instance, given that they state general rules.

Then he said: "As for his statement 'the possessive yāʾ …' to the end: the yāʾ has been transmitted vowelless after an alif, and readers have read so, as in «محياْيْ»." I say: the occurrence of sukūn in this yāʾ does not help him here; it would only help him if it had come with kasra after an alif, for that is the point at issue. The grammarians cited a verse of al-Dhubyānī with kasra and fatḥa, namely:
288 - 1- عليَّ لِعمروٍ نِعْمةٌ بعد نعمةٍ ... لوالدِه ليسَتْ بذاتِ عَقارِبِ
(I owe ʿAmr favour upon favour, for his father's sake — favours not attended by scorpions [of reproach].)
[Translator's note: the source has «بين الذبياني», evidently «بيتَ الذبياني» ("the verse of al-Dhubyānī"); translated accordingly. The kasra/fatḥa concerns «عليَّ».]

Al-Farrāʾ said in his book al-Maʿānī: "Al-Aʿmash and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb both gave the yāʾ of «بمُصْرِخِيِّ» kasra — al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn told me that from al-Aʿmash. Perhaps it is one of the readers' mistakes, for few of them are free from mistakes. Perhaps he thought that the bāʾ in «بمُصْرِخِيَّ» makes the whole word genitive, with the speaker's yāʾ excluded from that."

He said: "Among what we consider them to have made mistakes in is His words {نُوَلِّهْ مَا تولى وَنُصْلِهْ جَهَنَّمَ} with sukūn on the hāʾ." Then he mentioned other things.

Abū ʿUbayd said: "As for the kasra, we consider it an error, because they thought that the bāʾ puts in the genitive everything after it. Among the readers there were those who considered it a solecism; I would not like to go that far with it, but the proper reading in our view is the other one."

Al-Akhfash said: "I have not heard this from any of the Arabs, nor from any of the grammarians." Al-Naḥḥās said: "So this has become a consensus."

I say: there is no consensus, for what people have related — that it is a second dialect of some Arabs — has been given. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī took up the defence of this reading; he said in his Ḥujja: "Its rationale is that the yāʾ is either in the position of the accusative or of the genitive. The yāʾ in the accusative and genitive is like the hāʾ in both, and like the kāf in «أكرمتُك» and «هذا لك». Just as the hāʾ has an addition attached to it in «لهُوْ» and «ضَرَبَهُوْ», and the kāf too has an addition attached in the speech of those who say «أَعْطَيْتُكاه» and «أَعْطَيْتُكِيْه», as Sībawayh related — and these two are sisters of the yāʾ — and the tāʾ has an addition attached in the poet's saying:
288 - 2- رَمَيْتِيْهِ فَأَصْمَيْتِ ... وما أَخْطَأْتِ [في] الرَّمْيَهْ
(You shot him and killed him outright; you did not miss the shot.)
likewise they attached to the yāʾ an addition of lengthening, saying «فِيَّ»; then the yāʾ added to the yāʾ was dropped, just as the addition was dropped from the hāʾ in the speech of the one who said:
288 - 3-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . لَهْ أَرِقانِ
(… [my two eyes] are sleepless for him.)
And Abū al-Ḥasan [Translator's note: al-Akhfash] claimed that it is a dialect."

I say: what Abū ʿAlī meant by the parallel with the verse in his words «لَهْ أَرِقان» is the dropping of the extension; it so happens that in the verse there is also the dropping of the vowel. Had he given as an example «عليهِ» and «فيهِ», it would have been better.

Then al-Fārisī said: "Just as the addition was dropped from the kāf, so that one said «أعطيتكَهُ» and «أَعْطَيْتُكِهِ», likewise the yāʾ attached to the yāʾ was dropped, as it was dropped from its two sisters, and the kasra that preceded the dropped yāʾ was kept, so the yāʾ remained with the kasra it had." He said: "So since the kasra on the yāʾ is in this dialect — even if another is more widespread than it — and analogy supports it as we have mentioned, it is not permissible for anyone to say that reading so is a solecism, since it is sound in attested usage and in analogy, and what is so is not a solecism."

I say: this explanation is an elucidation of the second explanation I mentioned before. As for the first explanation, al-Farrāʾ also elucidated it. Al-Zajjāj said: "Al-Farrāʾ allowed the kasra on a weak basis, because the basic vowel for the meeting of two sukūns is the kasra."

Al-Farrāʾ said: "Do you not see that they say «مُذُ اليومِ» and «مُذِ اليوم»? The ḍamma on the dhāl is the proper form, because it is the original vowel of «منذ», but the kasra is permissible. Likewise the yāʾ of «مُصْرِخيَّ» was given kasra, though originally it has fatḥa."

I say: al-Farrāʾ's likening of the question to «مذ اليوم» is open to reservation, because the first letter [the dhāl] is a sound letter, and it is not preceded by a succession of kasras, unlike what we are dealing with. This is what al-Zamakhsharī meant by his words, which I quoted from him earlier: "so it is as though it occurred after a sound letter."

The transmission from al-Farrāʾ on this question is confused, as you have seen: some relate from him that he held it erroneous at one time and correct at another. Perhaps the matter was so, for scholars are asked and answer with what is present to them at the time of the question, and these differ.

The third explanation: the kasra is by assimilation of vowels (itbāʿ) to what follows it, namely the kasra of the hamza of «إنِّي», like the reading «الحمدِ لله» and their saying «بِعِير», «شِعِير» and «شِهيد», with kasra on their first letters by assimilation to what follows. This is very weak.

The fourth explanation: what licenses this kasra on the yāʾ, though it is heavy, is that when the preceding yāʾ was assimilated into it, it was strengthened by the assimilation and came to resemble the sound letters, so it could bear the kasra; for the kasra is only felt heavy on it when it is light and preceded by a kasra. Do you not see that the vowels of i'rab run on the doubled yāʾ? That is only because it is assimilated to the sound letters.

«المُصْرِخ» is the rescuer. One says «اسْتَصْرَخْتُه فَأَصْرَخَني», i.e. "I called him for help and he helped me". It is as though its hamza is privative, i.e. he removed my cry. «الصَّارخ» is the one who calls for help. The poet said:
288 - 4- ولا تَجْزَعوا إني لكمْ غيرُ مُصْرِخٍ ... وليس لكم عندي غَناءٌ ولا نَصْرُ
(Do not grieve; I am no rescuer for you, and with me there is neither avail nor help for you.)
One says «صَرَخَ يَصْرُخُ صَرْخاً وصُراخاً وصَرْخَة». The poet said:
288 - 5- كنَّا إذا ما أتانا صارخٌ فَزِعٌ ... كان الصُّراخُ له قَرْعَ الظَّنابيبِ
(We were such that whenever a terrified one crying for help came to us, the answer to his cry was the striking of shins [i.e. instant readiness].)
He means: the rescuing [given] was …; he omitted the muḍāf and put the maṣdar of the triliteral in place of the maṣdar of the quadriliteral, as in {والله أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17].

«الصَّريخ» is the people who call for help. The poet said:
288 - 6- قومٌ إذا سَمِعُوا الصَّريخَ رأيتَهُمْ ... ما بين مُلْجِمِ مُهْرِهِ أو سافِِعِ
(A people who, when they hear the cry for help, you see them either bridling their colts or seizing [the forelocks].)
«الصَّريخ» is also the rescuers, so it is one of the words with opposite meanings; it may be an adjective on the pattern faʿīl, like «الخَليط», or originally a maṣdar. He said {فَلاَ صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ} [Yā Sīn: 43]: this may be a maṣdar, or faʿīl in the sense of mufʿil, i.e. "there is no rescuer for them", i.e. helper. «تَصَرَّخ» means to force oneself to cry out.

His words: {بِمَآ أَشْرَكْتُمُونِ}: two views are possible for «ما». First: it means «الذي». Then as to what is meant by this relative noun there are two views. One: it is the idols, its implied form being: "by the idol which you obeyed me in as you obeyed it" — so said Abū al-Baqāʾ.
