The referent pronoun is omitted; Abū al-Baqāʾ supplied it as «بما أشركتموني به», then it was omitted — meaning after the preposition was dropped and the verb reached it directly. But there is no need to supply it as genitive with the bāʾ, because this verb is transitive to one object, as in «شَرَكْتُ زيداً»; when the hamza of transfer entered, it gave it a second object, which is the referent pronoun. You say «أَشْرَكْتُ زيداً عمراً»: I made him a partner of his.

The other: it is the Creator, the Exalted, i.e. "by what you associated me with", i.e. with Allah the Exalted. The discussion of the referent pronoun is as before, except that this involves applying «ما» to one who has knowledge, whereas the well-known use is for non-rational beings.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Like this «ما» is the «ما» in their saying «سبحانَ ما سَخَّرَكُنَّ» ('Glory be to Him who subjected you'). The meaning of their associating Satan with Allah the Exalted is their obeying him in the worship of idols that he made attractive to them." The Shaykh said: "Whoever disallows that makes «سبحان» a proper name for glorification, just as «بَرَّة» was made a proper name for piety, and «ما» maṣdar-forming and temporal" — i.e. it would then be on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "glory be to the Author of your subjection", since glorification befits none but Allah.

The second of the two initial views: it is maṣdar-forming, i.e. "by your associating me".

His words: {مِن قَبْلُ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كَفَرْتُ» on the first view, i.e. "I disbelieved before, when I refused to prostrate to Adam, in the One you associated me with, namely Allah the Exalted"; and to «أشركتموني» on the second, i.e. "I disbelieve today in your associating me before this day", i.e. in the world, as in His words {وَيَوْمَ القيامة يَكْفُرُونَ بِشِرْكِكُمْ} [Fāṭir: 14]. This is al-Zamakhsharī's view. Abū al-Baqāʾ, however, allowed it to be attached to «كفرتُ» and to «أشركتموني» without ordering this according to «ما» being maṣdar-forming or relative; he said: "«ومِنْ قبلُ» is attached to «أشركتموني», i.e. I now disbelieve [in] your having associated me before. It has been said: it is attached to «كفرتُ», i.e. I disbelieved before your associating, so I do not benefit you at all."

Abū ʿAmr read with the yāʾ kept in «أشركتموني» in continuous reading and dropped in pause; the rest dropped it both in continuous reading and in pause.

Here Satan's speech ends. His words {إِنَّ الظالمين} are the speech of Allah the Exalted; and it may be from Satan's speech. «عذاب» may be nominative by the prepositional phrase before it, on the basis that [the phrase] is the khabar (predicate); or as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is the prepositional phrase.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَأُدْخِلَ}: the generality read «أُدْخِلَ» as a past passive verb, the agent being Allah or the angels. Al-Ḥasan and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «وأُدْخِلُ» as an imperfect attributed to the speaker, namely Allah the Exalted. So the position of the relative noun on the first reading is nominative, and on the second accusative.

His words: {بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ}: in the [reading of] the generality it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أُدْخِلَ», i.e. they were admitted by His command and facilitation. It may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. bound up with their Lord's command. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be part of the completion of «خالدين», meaning attached to it, and that is not impossible. As for the reading of the two shaykhs [al-Ḥasan and ʿAmr], al-Zamakhsharī said: "To what is it attached in the other reading, given that your saying 'and I admit, by their Lord's permission' is an incoherent utterance? I say: the proper way in this reading is that it be attached to what follows it, i.e. 'their greeting therein is peace, by their Lord's permission.'" The Shaykh rejected this on the ground that the dependent of a maṣdar (verbal noun) does not precede it.

Others besides al-Zamakhsharī attached it to «أُدْخِلُ», and there is no incoherence in that, because everyone knows that the speaker in "and I admit" is the Lord, the Exalted. Better than both of these is that in this reading it be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, as was established above. «تحيتُهم» is a maṣdar in construct with its object, i.e. Allah or the angels greet them; it may also be in construct with its agent, i.e. they greet one another. The first is supported by {وَالمَلاَئِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن كُلِّ بَابٍ سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُم} [al-Raʿd: 23]. «فيها» is attached to it.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {ضَرَبَ الله مَثَلاً كَلِمَةً}: there are three views. First: «ضَرَبَ» is transitive to one object, meaning "He set forth a likeness and laid it down"; «كلمةً» on this view is accusative by a latent verb, i.e. "He made a good word like a good tree", and this is an explanation of His words {ضَرَبَ الله مَثَلاً}, as when you say: "The emir honoured Zayd: he clothed him in a robe and mounted him on a horse." Al-Zamakhsharī began with this. The Shaykh said: "It involves the strain of supplying an element for which there is no necessity." I say: rather its meaning [requires] it, so one is compelled to supply it in order to preserve this particular nuance of meaning.

Second: «ضَرَب» is transitive to two objects because it means «صَيَّر» ("to make"), but specifically with the word «المَثَل»; this was established at the beginning of this topic. So «كلمةً» is the first object and «مَثَلاً» the second, which is fronted.
[Translator's note: «فيما تقدَّم» at the end of this paragraph is rendered "which is fronted", taking it to refer to «مَثَلاً» standing first; literally "in what precedes".]

Third: it is transitive to one object, namely «مَثَلاً», and «كلمةً» is a badal (substitute) from it, with «كشجرةٍ» the khabar (predicate) of a latent mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is like a good tree". On the two preceding views, «كشجرةٍ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كلمة».

It has been read «كلمةٌ» in the nominative, and there are two views about it. First: it is the khabar of a latent mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it", i.e. the likeness is a good word, with «كشجرةٍ» on this view a naʿt of «كلمة». Second: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and «كشجرةٍ» its khabar.

Anas ibn Mālik read «ثابتٍ أصلُها». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what difference is there between the two readings? I say: the reading of the majority is stronger in meaning, because in Anas's reading the attribute is made to run on «الشجرة»; and when you say 'I passed by a man whose father is standing (abūhu qāʾimun)', it is stronger than 'by a man standing his father (qāʾimin abūhu)', because what is predicated about is the father, not the man."

The clause «أصلُها ثابتٌ» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of «شجرة».

semin-durr:25-25.t:
{تؤتي أُكُلَهَا}: it is also possible that both of them be resumptive. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «تُؤْتي» to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the sense of the clause before it, i.e. "it rises, yielding". The disagreement over «أُكُلَها» among the readers has been given.
[Translator's note: "both of them" presumably refers to the preceding clauses (including «وفرعها في السماء» and «تؤتي أكلها»); the source does not specify.]

semin-durr:26-26.t:
It has been read «ومَثَلَ», with «مثلَ» in the accusative, conjoined to the first «مثلَ». «اجْتُثَّتْ» is an attribute of «شجرة». The meaning of «اجْتُثَّتْ»: its «جُثَّة», i.e. its body, was reached. «الجُثَّة» is the body of a person sitting or lying. One says «اجْتَثَثْتُ الشيءَ», i.e. I uprooted it; it is iftiʿāl from the word «الجُثَّة»; and «جَثَثْتُ الشيءَ»: I pulled it out. Laqīṭ al-Iyādī said:
288 - 7- هو الجَلاءُ الذي يَجْتَثُّ أصلَكُمُ ... فَمَنْ رَأَى مثلَ ذا يوماً ومَنْ سَمِعا
(It is the exile that will uproot your stock — who has ever seen the like of this, or heard of it?)
Al-Rāghib said: "The «جُثَّة» of a thing is its protruding body; «المَجَثَّة» is that with which one uproots; «الجَثِيْثَة» is used for what comes to its bulk after being ground; and «الجَثْجاث» is a plant."

«مِنْ قَرار» may be a fāʿil (agent) governed by the prepositional phrase before it, because it leans on the negation, or a mubtadaʾ (subject). The negated clause is either a naʿt (adjective) of «شجرة» or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of «اجْتُثَّتْ».

semin-durr:27-27.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {بالقول}: there are two views. First: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُثَبِّتُ». Second: it is attached to «آمنوا».

His words: «في الحياةِ» is attached to «يُثَبِّتُ»; it may also be attached to «الثابِت».

semin-durr:28-28.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {بَدَّلُواْ نِعْمَةَ الله كُفْراً}: there are several views.

First: the original is "they exchanged the gratitude for the favour of [Allah] for disbelief", like His words {وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 82], [i.e.] the gratitude for your provision. Gratitude was incumbent on them, and they put disbelief in its place.

Second: they exchanged the favour itself for disbelief, in that when they were ungrateful for it they were stripped of it, and remained deprived of the favour, characterised by disbelief, which they had acquired. Al-Zamakhsharī said both of these. I say: on this view there is no need to omit a muḍāf. It has been stated that «بَدَّلَ» is transitive to two objects, the first without a preposition and the second with the bāʾ, and that the genitive is what is given up and the accusative is what is obtained; and the preposition may be omitted. So what is genitive with the bāʾ here is «نعمة», because it is what is given up. When you know this, you know that the statement of al-Ḥawfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ that «كفراً» is the second object is not good, because it is what the verb reaches by itself, not by a preposition, and whatever is so is the first object.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {جَهَنَّمَ}: there are three views. First: it is a badal (substitute) from «دارَ». Second: it is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it. On these two views the settling [of them in it] takes place in the Hereafter. Third: it is accusative by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), by an implied verb; on this view the settling takes place in this world, because His words {جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَهَا} take place in the Hereafter.

This interpretation is supported by Ibn Abī ʿAbla's reading «جهنمُ» in the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the clause after it as the khabar (predicate). Ibn Abī ʿAbla's reading also admits another view: that it is nominative as the khabar of a latent mubtadaʾ, with «يَصْلَوْنها» a ḥāl (circumstantial) either from «قومَهم», or from «دارَ», or from «جهنمَ». This explanation is preferable, in that nothing precedes that would make the accusative preferable, nor anything that would make it equal; and the mass of readers read the accusative — they would not have abandoned the more eloquent form unless the question had nothing at all to do with ishtighāl. What I have mentioned also favours its being accusative as a badal or explicative over its being accusative by ishtighāl.

«البَوار» is perdition. The poet said:
288 - 8- فلم أرَ مثلَهُم أبطالَ حربٍ ... غداةَ الرَّوْعِ إذ خِيْفَ البوارُ
(I have never seen their like as heroes of war, on the morning of terror when perdition was feared.)
Its origin is from stagnation of goods (kasād), as it is said: "it stagnated until it spoiled"; since stagnation leads to spoiling and perishing, «البَوار» was applied to it. One says «بار يَبُورُ بَواراً وبُوراً», and «رجل حائرٌ بائرٌ» ("a man confused and ruined"). His words {وَكُنتُمْ قَوْماً بُوراً} [al-Fatḥ: 12] may be a maṣdar used as an attribute of the plural, or a plural of «بائر» in meaning. Among instances of «بُور» applied to a single person is the saying:
288 - 9- يا رسولَ المَليكِ إنَّ لساني ... راتِقٌ ما فَتَقْتُ إذ أنا بُوْرُ
(O Messenger of the King! My tongue now mends what I tore when I was perishing.)
i.e. perishing.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِّيُضِلُّواْ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read here {وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ أَندَاداً لِّيَضِلُّواْ} with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and the rest with ḍamma, from «أَضَلَّه». The lām is the preposition lām with «أنْ» implied after it; it is the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba), since their outcome was to that. It may also be causal. It has been said: with fatḥa on the yāʾ it is for consequence only, and with ḍamma it admits both views — as though this speaker imagined that they did not set up rivals for the purpose of going astray. It is not as he claimed, because some of them disbelieved out of obstinacy and took gods in order to go astray themselves.

His words: {فَإِنَّ مَصِيرَكُمْ إِلَى النار}: «إلى النارِ» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», and «المصير» is the maṣdar of the complete (tāmma) «صار», i.e. "your return is to the Fire". Al-Ḥawfī allowed «إلى النار» to be attached to «مصيرَكم». Some rejected this on the ground that if we make it a maṣdar of «صار» in the sense of "moved", with «إلى النار» attached to it, «إنَّ» would remain without a khabar. It cannot be said that its khabar is then omitted, because its omission in such a case is rare; its omission is frequent only when the noun is indefinite and the khabar an adverb or prepositional phrase, as in the saying:
289 - 0- إنَّ مَحَلاًّ وإنْ مُرْتَحَلا ... وإنَّ في السَّفْرِ ما مَضَى مَهَلا
(There is a place of halting and a place of departure, and in the travellers who have gone on there is respite [no return].)

semin-durr:31-31.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {قُل لِّعِبَادِيَ الذين آمَنُواْ يُقِيمُواْ}: there are several views. First: «يُقيموا» is jussive (majzūm) by an omitted lām of command, its implied form being «ليقيموا»; it was omitted and its effect remained, just as a preposition is omitted and its effect remains, as in the saying:
289 - 1- محمدُ تَفْدِ نفسَك كلُ نفسٍ ... إذا ما خِفْتَ مِنْ شيءٍ تَبالا
(O Muḥammad, may every soul ransom your soul, whenever you fear evil consequence from anything.)
He means «لِتَفْدِ». Sībawayh cited it, but restricted it to poetry. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«يُقيموا» and «يُنْفِقوا» may be in the sense of «لِيُقيموا» and «لِيُنْفقوا», and this would be what is said. They said: the omission of the lām is only permissible because the imperative «قُلْ» is a compensation for it; had one said 'يقيموا الصلاة ويُنفقوا' initially, with the lām omitted, it would not be permissible." I say: Ibn Mālik inclined to something close to this, for he made the omission of this lām of several kinds: rare, frequent and intermediate. The frequent: when it is preceded by a verb of saying in the imperative form, as in the noble verse. The rare: when no verb of saying precedes, as in his saying «محمدُ تَفْدِ» — the verse. The intermediate: when one precedes, not in the imperative form, as in the saying:
289 - 2- قُلْتُ لبَوَّابٍ لديهِ دارُها ... تِيْذَنْ فإني حَمْؤُها وجارُها
(I said to a doorkeeper at whose post her house is: "Let [me] in, for I am her in-law and her neighbour.")

Second: «يُقيموا» is jussive as the answer to «قُلْ»; al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad inclined to this. People rejected this from them on the ground that it does not follow from His saying to them "Establish …" that they will do it — how many have fallen short of this command! This was answered: what is meant by "servants" is the believers — which is why He attributed them to Himself as an honour — and the believers, whenever He commands them, comply.

Third: it is jussive as the answer to the omitted statement, its implied form being: "Say to My servants: Establish and spend — they will establish and spend." Abū al-Baqāʾ said — and he attributed it to al-Mubarrad: "So a group mentioned it and did not address its invalidity. It is invalid in two respects. First: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) differs from the protasis either in the verb or in the agent or in both; when it is like it in verb and agent it is an error, as in your saying 'Stand, you will stand'; and the implied form according to what is mentioned in this view is 'If they establish, they will establish'. The second respect: the implied imperative is for direct address, whereas «يُقيموا» is in the form of the third person, and that is an error if the agent is one and the same." I say: the first invalidation is reasonable; the second is nothing, because one may say "Say to My servant: Obey me — he will obey you", even though it is in the third person after direct address, by way of narrating the situation.

Fourth: the implied form is "If you say to them 'Establish', they will establish"; this is narrated from Sībawayh according to what Ibn ʿAṭiyya related. I say: this is the second view.

Fifth: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«يُقيموا» may be the answer to the command whose meaning His word «قُلْ» gives us; that is, you take His words «قُلْ» in this verse in the sense of 'Convey and deliver the Law — they will establish.'"

Sixth: al-Farrāʾ said: "The imperative has an implied condition with it; you say: 'Obey Allah — He will admit you to the Garden.'"
The difference between this and what precedes: in what precedes the imperative itself is made to imply the sense of the condition, while in this the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) is supplied after the imperative verb without implication.

Seventh: al-Fārisī said: "It is an imperfect turned from the imperative to the statement form, and its meaning is 'Establish'." This is rejected, because it ought then to keep its nūn, which indicates its i'rab. This was answered: it was made indeclinable (mabnī) because it occurs in the place of an indeclinable, just as the one addressed is made indeclinable in e.g. «يا زيدُ» because it occurs in the place of the pronoun; or [it could be] said that its nūn was dropped for lightness, as it was dropped in his saying ﷺ: «لا تَدْخُلوا الجنَّة حتى تؤمنوا، ولا تؤمنوا حتى تحابُّوا» ("You will not enter the Garden until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another").
[Translator's note: the final conditional «ولو قيل …» is left without an apodosis in the source; rendered "or [it could be] said".]

There are three views about the dependent of «قُلْ». First: the implied imperative, i.e. "Say to them: Establish — they will establish." Second: it is «يُقيموا» itself, according to what Ibn ʿAṭiyya said. Third: it is the clause from His words {الله الذي خَلَقَ} to the end — said by Ibn ʿAṭiyya. This involves breaking up the arrangement and making the clause «يُقيموا الصلاة» to the end detached from what precedes and follows it; or it would be an answer separating the verb of saying from its dependent — but the establishing of prayer and the spending do not follow from saying that, except by a very far-fetched interpretation.

His words: «سِرَّاً وعلانِيَةً»: there are three views about their accusative. First: they are two ḥāls (circumstantials) from what precedes, and the three interpretations of «زيد عَدْل» apply to them: i.e. possessors of secrecy and openness; or doing it secretly and openly; or they are made secrecy and openness themselves, for intensification. Second: they are accusative as adverbs, i.e. at times of secrecy and of openness. Third: they are accusative as maṣdars (absolute objects), i.e. spending secretly and spending openly.

His words: «مِنْ قبل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُقيموا» and «يُنْفِقوا», i.e. they do that before this day.

The disagreement of the readers over {لاَّ بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلاَ خِلاَلٌ} has been given. «الخِلال» is mutual friendship (al-mukhālla), i.e. companionship. One says «خالَلْتُه خِلالاً ومُخَالَّةً». Ṭarafa said:
289 - 3- كلُّ خليلٍ كنتُ خالَلْتُه ... لا تَرَكَ اللهُ له واضِحَهْ
(Every friend whom I befriended — may Allah not leave him a single front tooth!)
Imruʾ al-Qays said:
289 - 4- صَرَفْتُ الهَوَى عنهنَّ مِنْ خشيةِ الرَّدى ... ولستُ بمَقْلِيِّ الخِلالِ ولا قالِ
(I turned my passion away from them for fear of ruin, yet I am not one whose friendship is hated, nor one who hates.)
Al-Akhfash said: "«خِلال» is a plural of «خُلَّة», like «بُرْمَة» and «بِرام»."

semin-durr:32-32.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِنَ السمآء}: it may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أَنْزَل», with «مِنْ» for the beginning of the extent; or to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما», because it is originally an attribute. Likewise «مِن الثمرات», on the two views.

Al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed «مِنْ» to be for explaining the genus, i.e. "a provision which is the fruits". It is objected against them that the explicative «مِنْ» only comes after a vague term. It may be answered for them that they meant that in terms of meaning, not i'rab. The discussion of this was given in al-Baqara.

«بأَمْرِهِ» may be attached to «تَجْرِي», i.e. by reason of it; or to an omitted element, on the basis that it is circumstantial, i.e. bound up with it.

semin-durr:33-33.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {دَآئِبَينَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the sun and the moon. The derivation of «الدَّأْب» has been given.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِّن كُلِّ مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ}: the generality read «كُلّ» in construct with «ما». There are two views about «مِنْ». First: it is redundant (zāʾida) in the second object, i.e. "all that you asked Him"; this only works on al-Akhfash's view. Second: it is partitive, i.e. He gave you part of all that you asked Him, out of regard for you and your interests; on this view the object is omitted, its implied form being "and He gave you something of all that you asked Him" — and this is Sībawayh's opinion.

«ما» may be a nominal relative noun, or a particle (i.e. maṣdar-forming), or an indefinite noun qualified [by the following clause]; [in the maṣdar case] the maṣdar stands in place of the object, i.e. "what you asked for". If it is maṣdar-forming, the pronoun in «سَأَلْتموه» refers back to Allah the Exalted. If it is a relative or qualified noun, [the pronoun] refers back to it, and it is not permissible that it refer back to Allah the Exalted with the referent pronoun of the relative or qualified noun omitted; because it would have to be supplied either as attached — «سألتموهوه» — or detached — «سألتموه إياه» — and in neither is omission permissible, for the reason I gave you at the beginning of al-Baqara on His words {وَممَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ}.

Ibn ʿAbbās, Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid, Qatāda, Sallām, Yaʿqūb, and Nāfiʿ in one transmission, read {مِّن كُلٍّ} with tanwīn. On this reading there are two views about «ما». First: it is negating; al-Zamakhsharī began with this and said: "«وما سأَلْتُموه» is a negation, and its position is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He gave you of all that without your asking for it." I say: the second object would then be the prepositional phrase «مِنْ كُلٍّ», as in His words {وَأُوتِيَتْ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ} [al-Naml: 23].

Second: it is a relative noun meaning «الذي», and it is the second object of «آتاكم». This second explanation is preferable, because in the first there is an apparent contradiction with the reading of the generality. The Shaykh said: "When al-Zamakhsharī sensed the apparent contradiction between this reading and that, he said: '«ما» may be relative, on the sense: He gave you of all that what you needed, without which neither your conditions nor your livelihoods would be set right — so it is as though you sought it or asked for it with the tongue of your state.' So he interpreted «سَأَلْتموه» in the sense of what you needed."

His word: «نعمةَ» has the sense of what is bestowed. This [verse] was closed with {إِنَّ الإنسان لَظَلُومٌ}, and its counterpart in al-Naḥl with {إِنَّ الله لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ} [al-Naḥl: 18], because in this one there preceded His words {أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الذين بَدَّلُواْ نِعْمَةَ الله كُفْراً} [Ibrāhīm: 28], and after it {وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ أَندَاداً} [Ibrāhīm: 30]; so His words {إِنَّ الإنسان} came as a testimony to the foulness of whoever does that, and it was fitting to close it with that. In the one in al-Naḥl He mentioned several details and was emphatic in it, and mentioned His words {أَفَمَن يَخْلُقُ كَمَن لاَّ يَخْلُقُ} [al-Naḥl: 17], i.e. is He who brought into being these favours mentioned before like one who has no power over any of them? So He also mentioned that among His bounties is His being characterised by these two attributes.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {هذا البلد آمِناً}: the two objects of «الجَعْل» in the sense of transforming (taṣyīr); its precise treatment was given in al-Baqara. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what difference is there between His words {اجعل هذا بَلَداً آمِناً} [al-Baqara: 126] and His words {هذا البلد آمِناً}? I say: in the first he asked that He make it one of the lands whose people are safe and do not fear; in the second, that He bring it out of a state of fear in which it was to its opposite, safety — as though he said: it is a fearful land, so make it safe."

His words: {واجنبني}: one says «جَنَبَه شرَّاً» and «أَجْنَبَه إياه», triliteral and quadriliteral — this is the dialect of Najd — and «جَنَّبه إياه» with doubling, which is the dialect of the Ḥijāz; it means keeping away, and its origin is from «الجانب» (the side). Al-Rāghib said: "His words {واجنبني وَبَنِيَّ} are from «جَنَبْتُه عن كذا», i.e. I kept him far from it. It has been said: from «جَنَبْتُ الفَرَسَ» (I led the horse by my side), as though [he asked] that He lead him away from the side of polytheism by His kindnesses and hidden means."

And {أَن نَّعْبُدَ} is on the omission of the preposition, i.e. «عن أن». Al-Jaḥdarī and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read «وأَجْنِبْني» with a disjunctive hamza, from «أَجْنَبَ».

semin-durr:36-36.t:
The pronoun in «إنَّهُنَّ» and «أَضْلَلْنَ» refers back to the idols, because they are a broken plural of a non-rational. His word «مني», i.e. of my followers.

His words: {وَمَنْ عَصَانِي}: a condition; the position of «مَنْ» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is {فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ}, and the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. "for him".

semin-durr:37-37.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِن ذُرِّيَّتِي}: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) may be omitted, with this prepositional phrase its attribute, i.e. "I have settled some offspring from my offspring". «مِنْ» may also be redundant (zāʾida) according to al-Akhfash.

His words: «بوادٍ», i.e. in a valley, as in «هو بمكة» ("he is in Mecca").

His words: {عِندَ بَيْتِكَ}: it may be an attribute of «وادٍ». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be a badal (substitute) from it", meaning a badal of part from whole, since the valley is more general than the vicinity of the House. There is a reservation about this, in that «عند» is not freely inflected (lā yataṣarraf).

His words: «ليُقِيموا»: this lām may be the lām of command, or the lām of cause. In the latter case there are two views about what it is attached to. One: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أَسْكنْتُ», which is apparent, the vocative being parenthetical. The other: it is attached to «اجْنُبْني», i.e. "keep them away from idols so that they may establish", and this is far-fetched.

His words: {أَفْئِدَةً مِّنَ الناس}: the generality read «أفْئِدة», plural of «فُؤاد», like «غُراب/أَغْربة». Hishām from Ibn ʿĀmir read it with a yāʾ after the hamza. It has been said: this is lengthening (ishbāʿ), as in the saying:
289 - 5-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يُحِبَّك عَظْمٌ في الترابِ تَرِيْبُ
(… a bone lying in the dust will love you.)
i.e. «تَرِب»; and as in the saying:
289 - 6- أعوذُ باللهِ مِنَ العَقْرابِ ... الشائلاتِ عُقدَ الأَذْنابِ
(I seek refuge in Allah from the scorpions that raise the knots of their tails.)
A group attacked this reading and said: lengthening is one of the licences of poetry, so how can it be put in the most eloquent speech? Some claimed that Hishām only read it with the hamza lightened to an in-between sound (bayna bayna), and the transmitter thought it was the addition of a yāʾ after the hamza; he said: "just as it was imagined of Abū ʿAmr's slurring (ikhtilās) in «بارئكم» and «يَأْمُركم» that he gave sukūn." This is nothing, for the transmitters are too eminent for this.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «إفادة» on the pattern of «رِفادة». There are two views on it. First: it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «أفاد», like «أقام إقامةً», i.e. possessors of benefit — the people from whom benefit is had. Second: its origin is «وِفادة» (a delegation's coming), the wāw being replaced by a hamza, as in «إشاح» and «إعاء».

Umm al-Haytham read «أَفْوِدَة» with a wāw with kasra. There are two views on it. First: it is the plural of the lightened «فُوَاد»: a hamza with fatḥa preceded by ḍamma is regularly changed into a wāw, as in «جُوَن»; this was done in the singular «فُؤاد», and it was kept as it was in the plural. Second: the author of al-Lawāmiḥ said: "It is the plural of «وَفْد»." I say: then the form should have been «أَوْفِدة», with the wāw first — unless it is said that he pluralised «وَفْد» as «أَوْفِدَة» and then transposed it, so its measure is «أَعْفِلَة», like their saying «آرام» for «أرْآم» and its class; except that the plural of faʿl on afʿila is rare, as in «نَجْد/أَنْجدة» and «وَهْي/أَوْهِيَة». Umm al-Haytham is a woman from whom something of the language has been transmitted.

It has been read «آفِدَة» on the pattern of «ضارِبة». It admits two views. First: it is transposed from «أَفئدة», with the hamza put before the fāʾ, then the hamza changed into an alif, so its measure is «أَعْفِلة», like «آرام» for «أرْآم».
Second: it is an active participle of «أَفِد يَأْفَدُ», i.e. to draw near, the meaning being "an approaching group", or "approaching groups".

It has been read «أَفِدَة» without the long vowel [Translator's note: the source writes «آفِدَة» here too, but says "with shortening (bi-l-qaṣr)"], and there are two views on this too. First: it is an active-participle adjective on the pattern faʿil, like «فَرِحَ فهو فَرِح». [Second]: it is lightened from «أَفْئِدة» by transferring the vowel of the hamza to the vowelless letter before it and dropping the hamza.

And «من الناس»: there are two views about «مِنْ». First: it is for the beginning of the extent. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«مِنْ» may be for the beginning of the extent, as when you say 'The heart from me is sick', meaning 'my heart'; as though it were said 'hearts of people'. I only made the muḍāf indefinite in this illustration because «أَفْئدة» is indefinite — since in the verse it is indefinite — so that it comprises some of the hearts." The Shaykh said: "Its being for the extent is not apparent, because we have no verb in which there is a beginning with an extent at which it ends, since it is not valid to make the beginning of the hearts from the people."
Second: it is partitive. In the exegesis: had he not said «من الناس», all people would have made the pilgrimage.

His words: «تَهْوي»: this is the second object of «الجَعْل». The generality read «تَهْوِي» with kasra on the ʿayn, meaning: they hasten and fly with longing to them. The poet said:
289 - 7- وإذا رَمَيْتَ به الفِجاجَ رَأَيْتَه ... يَهْوي مخارمَها هُوِيَّ الأجْدَلِ
(When you launch him into the mountain passes, you see him swooping through their defiles as the falcon swoops.)
Its original is to be made transitive with the lām, as in the saying:
289 - 8- حتى إذا ما هَوَتْ كفُّ الغلامِ لها ... طارَتْ وفي كَفِّه مِنْ ريشِها بِتَكُ
(Until, when the boy's hand swooped at her, she flew off, leaving in his hand plucked tufts of her feathers.)
It was only made transitive with «إلى» because it was made to imply the sense of «تميل» ("to incline"), as in the saying:
289 - 9- تَهْوي إلى مكَّةَ تَبْغي الهدى ... ما مُؤْمِنُ الجِنِّ كأَنْجاسِها
(She hastens to Mecca seeking guidance; the believer among the jinn is not like their unclean ones.)
The Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad and Mujāhid read it with fatḥa on the wāw [«تَهْوَى»]. There are two views on it. First: «إلى» is redundant, i.e. "they love them". Second: it was made to imply the sense of "yearn and incline". The maṣdar of the first [form] is «هُوِيّ», as in the saying:
290 - 0-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يَهْوي مخارِمَها هُوِيَّ الأجْدَل
(… swooping through their defiles as the falcon swoops.)
and that of the second is «هَوَى». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Their meanings are close, except that «هَوِيَ» — meaning with fatḥa on the wāw [in the imperfect] — is transitive by itself, and it was only made transitive with «إلى» by construal on «تميل»."

Maslama ibn ʿAbd Allāh read «تُهْوَى», with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the wāw, passive, from «أهوى», transferred from the intransitive «هَوِيَ», i.e. they are made to hasten to them.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {عَلَى الكبر}: there are two views. First: «على» is in its proper sense of figurative superiority. Second: it means «مع» ("with, despite"), as in the saying:
290 - 1- إنِّي على ما تَرَيْنَ من كِبَري ... أعلمُ مِنْ تُؤْكَلُ الكَتِفَ
(Despite the old age you see in me, I know from where the shoulder is eaten [i.e. I know how to handle affairs].)
Al-Zamakhsharī said this. The position of this prepositional phrase is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the yāʾ in «هَبْ لي».
[Translator's note: the source has «من الباء»; the pronoun in «لي» is the yāʾ, which is evidently meant.]

His words: {لَسَمِيعُ الدعآء}: there are several views. First: faʿīl is an intensive form in construct with its object, the construct arising from an accusative; this is evidence for Sībawayh that faʿīl operates like the active participle, even though he differed from the majority of Basrans and Kufans in this.

Second: the construct does not arise from an accusative; it is only like your saying «هذا ضاربُ زيدٍ أمس» ("this is the one who struck Zayd yesterday"). Third: «سميع» is in construct with its nominative [subject], Allah's prayer being made "hearing" figuratively, what is meant being Allah's hearing — al-Zamakhsharī said this.

The Shaykh said: "It is far-fetched, because it entails its being a ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle) while the adjective is transitive; this only works on the view of al-Fārisī, who allows the ṣifa mushabbaha to be from a transitive verb on condition that ambiguity is avoided, as in «زيد ظالمُ العبيد» ('Zayd whose slaves are unjust') when it is known that he has unjust slaves. Here, however, ambiguity is present, since the apparent sense is that it is the intensive form in construct with the object, not the agent."
I say: ambiguity here too is absent, because the meaning is on figurative attribution as established, so ambiguity is ruled out.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمِن ذُرِّيَتِي}: conjoined to the first object of «اجعلني», i.e. "and make some of my offspring establishers of prayer". This prepositional phrase is in reality an attribute of that omitted [object], i.e. "and some from my offspring".

His words: {وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَآءِ}: Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and Warsh read it with the yāʾ kept in continuous reading and dropped in pause; al-Bazzī kept it in both states; and the rest dropped it both in continuous reading and in pause. Some have transmitted its being kept in pause as well.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَلِوَالِدَيَّ}: the generality read «والِدَيَّ» with an alif after the wāw and a doubled yāʾ. Ibn Jubayr read likewise, except that he gave the yāʾ sukūn, meaning his father alone, as in His words {واغفر لأبي} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 86].

Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, Muḥammad and Zayd the sons of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and Ibn Yaʿmar read «ولولدي» without an alif, the dual of «وَلَد», meaning by the two Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq. Al-Jaḥdarī rejected it on the ground that in the codex of Ubayy it is «ولأبويَّ», which explains the reading of the generality.

It is related from Ibn Yaʿmar that he read «ولِوُلْدي» with ḍamma on the wāw and sukūn on the yāʾ. There are two interpretations of it. One: it is the plural of «وَلَد», like «أُسْد» from «أَسَد». The other: it is a dialectal variant of «الوَلَد», like «الحُزْن/الحَزَن», «العَدَم/العُدْم» and «البُخْل/البَخَل»; on this is the poet's saying:
290 - 2- فليتَ زياداً كان في بَطْنِ أمِّه ... وليت زياداً كان وُلْدَ حمارِ
(Would that Ziyād had stayed in his mother's belly; would that Ziyād had been the offspring of a donkey.)
It has been read so in Maryam, al-Zukhruf and Nūḥ among the Seven, as will come, Allah the Exalted willing. «يومَ» is accusative by «اغفر».
[Translator's note: in the second interpretation the source has «وأنْ يكونَ» without an explicit "second"; and «وسكون الياء» presumably refers to the lām (i.e. «وُلْدي»); translated as written.]

semin-durr:42-42.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِيَوْمٍ}, i.e. for the sake of a day; so the lām is causal. It has been said: it means «إلى», i.e. for the limit. The generality read «يُؤَخِّرُهم» with the yāʾ, because the noble name of Allah preceded. Al-Ḥasan, al-Sulamī, al-Aʿraj and many others — and it is related from Abū ʿAmr — read «نُؤَخِّرُهم» with the nūn of majesty. «تَشْخَصُ» is an attribute of «يوم». The meaning of «شُخُوص البصر» is the sharpness of the gaze and its not resting in its place. One says «شَخَص سَهْمُهُ وبَصَرُه» (his arrow / his gaze rose) and «أشخصَهما صاحبُهما» (their owner raised them); «شَخَصَ بصرُه»: his eyelid did not blink. One says «شَخَص مِنْ بلدِه», i.e. he went far away. «الشَّخْص» is the dark form of a person seen from afar.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مُهْطِعِينَ مُقْنِعِي رُءُوسِهِمْ}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the omitted muḍāf, since the implied form is "the owners of the eyes", because one says «شَخَصَ زيدٌ بصرَه»; or the eyes indicate their owners, so the ḥāl came from what is indicated. Abū al-Baqāʾ said both of these. It has been said: «مُهْطِعين» is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "He sees them hastening". «مُقْنِعي» may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُهْطِعين», so that it is an overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl. The construct of «مُقْنعي» is not a genuine one, which is why it occurs as a ḥāl.

«الإِهطاع»: it has been said to be hastening in walking. The poet said:
290 - 3- إذا دعانا فأَهْطَعْنا لدَعْوَته ... داعٍ سميعٌ فَلَفُّونا وساقُوْنا
(When a caller, one who is heard, called us and we hastened to his call, they gathered us up and drove us on.)
And another said:
290 - 4- وبمُهْطِعٍ سُرُحٍ كأن عِنَانَه ... في [رأس] جَذْعٍ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And on a swift, hastening [horse], as though its rein were on [the top of] a palm trunk …)
Abū ʿUbayda said: "It may be hastening and keeping the gaze fixed." Al-Rāghib said: "«هَطَع الرجلُ ببصره» is when he directs it downward, and «بعيرٌ مُهْطِعٌ» is a camel that lowers its neck." Al-Akhfash said: "It is turning attentively to listening," and he cited:
290 - 5- بِدِجْلَةَ دارُهُمْ ولقد أراهُمْ ... بِدِجْلِةَ مُهْطِعِيْن إلى السَّماعِ
(Their abode is by the Tigris, and I indeed see them by the Tigris, intent upon listening.)
The meaning: turning their heads toward hearing the caller. Thaʿlab said: "«أَهْطَعَ الرجلُ» is when he looks in humiliation and submission, not withdrawing his gaze." This agrees with the statement of Abū ʿUbayd [Translator's note: earlier the source names Abū ʿUbayda]; «أَهْطَعَ» and «هَطَعَ», quadriliteral and triliteral, have both been heard.

«الإِقناع» is raising the head and keeping the gaze fixed without turning to anything else — said by al-Qutabī and Ibn ʿArafa. From it is the saying of the poet describing camels that graze on the tops of trees and so raise their heads:
290 - 6- يُباكِرْن العِضَاهَ بمُقْنَعاتٍ ... نواجِذُهُنَّ كالِحَدأ الوَقيع
(They come early to the thorn-trees with raised [heads], their molars like sharpened axe-heads.)
One also says «أَقْنَعَ رأسَه», i.e. he lowered and bowed it, so it is one of the words with opposite meanings. «القَناعَة» is being content with little; the meaning of «قَنِع بكذا» is that his head is raised above asking. «فَمٌ مُقَنَّع» is a mouth whose teeth are bent inward; and «رجلٌ مُقَنَّعٌ» with doubling. One says «قَنِعَ يَقْنَعُ قَناعةً وقَنَعاً» when he is content, and «قَنَعَ قُنُوعاً» when he begs; so the difference falls in the maṣdar.

Al-Rāghib said: "Some said: the origin of this word is from «القِناع», which is what covers the head. «القانِع» is one who does [not] press in asking and is content with what comes to him, as in the saying:
290 - 7- لَمالُ المَرْءِ يُصْلِحُهُ فَيُغْني ... مَفاقِرَه أعفُّ مِنَ القُنُوعِ
(A man's wealth, which he tends so that it relieves his needs, is more chaste than begging.)
And «رجل مَقْنَعٌ» is one with whom one is satisfied. The poet said:
290 - 8-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... شُهودِيْ على لَيْلَى عُدُولٌ مَقانِعُ
(… my witnesses concerning Laylā are upright, acceptable.)"

«الرُّؤوس» is the plural of «رَأْس», which is feminine [Translator's note: so in the source («مؤنث»); «رأس» is normally treated as masculine]. Its plural of paucity is «أَرْؤُس» and of multitude «رُؤوس». «الأَرْأَس» is one with a large head; it is used to denote a great man, like «الوجه»; «الرئيس» is derived from that; «رِئاس السيف» is its hilt; and «شاةٌ رَأْساء» is a ewe whose head is black.

His words: {لاَ يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ}: also in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُقْنِعِي». It may be a badal (substitute) from «مُقْنِعي» — so said Abū al-Baqāʾ, meaning that it takes its place. It may also be resumptive.

«الطَّرْف» is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and was applied to the agent, as in their saying "There is not among them an eye that blinks"; [perhaps] here it is the eye. The poet said:
290 - 9- وأَغُضُّ طَرْفي ما بَدَتْ لي جارَتي ... حتى يُواري جارَتي مَأْواها
(I lower my gaze whenever my neighbour-woman appears to me, until her dwelling conceals her.)
«الطَّرْف» is also the eyelid; one says "he did not close his «طَرْف» — i.e. his eyelid — upon the other"; and «الطَّرْف» is also the moving of the eyelid.

His words: {وَأَفْئِدَتُهُمْ هَوَآءٌ}: it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl, the governor being either «يَرْتَدُّ» or the governing elements before it. «هواء» is singular though it is the khabar (predicate) of a plural, because it means "empty, torn open"; had that not been intended, He would have said «أَهْوِيَة», so that the khabar agrees with its mubtadaʾ (subject).

«الهواء» is what is empty of bodies, and it is used to denote cowardice; one says «جَوْفُه هواءٌ», i.e. empty. Zuhayr said:
291 - 0- كأن الرَّحْلَ منها فوق صَعْلٍ ... من الظَّلْمَانِ جُؤْجُؤُه هَواءُ
(As though the saddle on her were upon a small-headed male ostrich, whose breast is hollow.)
And Ḥassān ibn Thābit, may Allah be pleased with him, said:
291 - 1-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وأنت مُجَوَّفٌ نَخِبٌ هواءُ
(… while you are hollow, heartless, empty.)
«النَّخِب» is one whose «نُخْبة», i.e. best part, has been taken.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ}: the second object of «أَنْذِرْ», that is: "frighten them with the punishment of a day." Thus Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it, but there is something to consider in it, since it comes down to your saying "warn of the punishment of the day on which the punishment comes to them," so there is no need for that. Nor is it permissible for it to be an adverbial (ẓarf) of it, because there is no warning on that day, whether it is said that it is the Day of Resurrection, or a day of their destruction, or the day the angels meet them. His saying «نُجِبْ» is the answer to the imperative.
His saying: {أَوَلَمْ تكونوا}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "On the intention of an implied saying, and there are two aspects to it: that they say that out of arrogance and insolence, or that they say it in the tongue of their condition, since they built strongly and hoped far."
And «مالكم» is the answer to the oath. It came in the form of address only because of His saying «أَقْسَمْتُمْ»; had it come in the form of those who swear, it would have been said: "ما لنا." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] implied that saying as being from the words of Allah the Exalted or of the angels, that is: "So it will be said to them: أو لم تكونوا." In my view this is more apparent than the first, I mean the saying proceeding from others, not from them.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَسَكَنتُمْ فِي مساكن}: the original usage of «سَكَن» is to be transitive by means of «في», as in this verse, and at times it is transitive by itself. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Sukná is from sukūn, which is lingering (labth), and the original of its transitivity is with «في», as in your saying: «قَرَّ في الدارِ» (he stayed in the house), «أقامَ فيها» (he resided in it), and «غَنِيَ فيها» (he dwelt in it). But when it was transferred to a specific sukūn, it was treated freely, so it was said «سَكَنَ الدارَ» just as it was said «تبوَّأَها» and «أَوْطَنها»; and it is possible that it is from sukūn in the sense of calm, that is: they settled in it and were at ease."
His saying: «وتَبَيَّنَ»: its agent (fāʿil) is a latent pronoun, indicated by the context, [that is]: their condition, their affair and their destruction. And «كيف» is accusative (manṣūb) by «فَعَلْنا»; the interrogative clause is not governed by «تَبَيَّن», because it is one of the verbs that are not suspended (lā tuʿallaq). Nor is it permissible for «كيف» to be the agent, because it is either conditional or interrogative, and neither of the two is governed by what precedes it, and the agent does not come first according to us.
Some of the Kufans said: "The clause «كيف فَعَلْنا» is itself the agent," and they permit a clause to be an agent; this was mentioned shortly before, in His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِّن بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُاْ الآيات لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ} [Yūsuf: 35].
The majority read «تَبَيَّن» as a past verb. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and al-Sulamī, in one report from him, read: «ونُبَيِّنَ» with ḍamma on the first nūn and the second, an imperfect of «بَيَّن»; it is the predicate of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: «ونحنُ نبيِّن». And al-Sulamī read, according to what al-Mahdawī reported, likewise, except that he made the nūn sākin for the jussive, as a conjunction (nasaq) on «تكونوا», so it falls within the scope of the implied saying.
[Translator's note: "ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb" renders the source's «عمر لن الخطاب», which is evidently a typographical corruption of «عمر بن الخطاب».]

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَعِندَ الله مَكْرُهُمْ}: it is possible that this maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its agent, like the first, meaning: that their scheming which they schemed, its recompense is with Allah the Exalted; or to the object, meaning: that with Allah is their scheming, which He schemes against them, that is: He punishes them. Al-Zamakhsharī stated both. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is not sound unless «مَكَرَ» is transitive by itself, as he said, since he implied «يمكرهم به»; but what is preserved is that «مَكَر» is not transitive to a direct object by itself. The Exalted said: {وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الذين كَفَرُواْ} [al-Anfāl: 30], and you say «زيدٌ ممكورٌ به», and «زيدٌ ممكورٌ» is not preserved without the cause."
His saying «لِتَزُولَ»: the majority read it with kasra on the lām, and al-Kisāʾī read it with fatḥa. As for the first reading, it has three aspects. The first: that «إنْ» is negative and the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), because it comes after a negated kawn. In «كان» there are then two views. The first: that it is complete (tāmma), and the meaning is belittling their scheming: that it was not such that the laws, which are like mountains in their steadfastness and strength, would pass away through it. What supports its being negative is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: «وما كان مَكْرُهم». The second view: that it is incomplete (nāqiṣa), and regarding its predicate there are the two well-known views between the Basrans and the Kufans: is it omitted, with the lām attached to it, which is the position of the Basrans, or is it this lām and what it governs in the genitive, which is the position of the Kufans; this was settled at the end of Āl ʿImrān.
The second aspect: that it is the lightened form of the heavy («إنْ» for «إنَّ»). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Even if their scheming was great and extreme in its severity, so that the passing away of the mountains from it was given as a parable of its severity, that is: even if their scheming was prepared for that." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible, in my view, that the meaning of this reading is magnifying their scheming, that is: even if it is severe, it is only done so that great matters would go away by it." The implication of these two statements is that it is the lightened form, because it is an affirmation.
The third: that it is conditional, and its answer is omitted, that is: "even if their scheming was prepared to remove the like of the firm mountains, which are the miracles and the signs, then Allah will requite them with a scheme greater than it." The last two aspects have been preferred over the first, which is that it is negative, because the latter conflicts with the reading of al-Kisāʾī, since his reading announces affirmation, while the reading of others announces negation.
Some of them answered that by saying that the situation in the reading of al-Kisāʾī is an allusion to great matters other than Islam and its miracles, as their scheming had the capacity to remove them, whereas in the reading of the community it is an allusion to what the Prophet ﷺ brought of the true religion, so there is no conflict, as they did not converge on one meaning in negation and affirmation.
As for the reading of al-Kisāʾī, in «إنْ» there are two aspects: the position of the Basrans, that it is the lightened form and the lām is the distinguishing lām (fāriqa); and the position of the Kufans, that it is negative and the lām is in the sense of «إلا». Both positions have been verified earlier.
ʿUmar, ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Salama and a group read «وإن كاد مكرهم لَتزول», like the reading of al-Kisāʾī, except that they put a dāl in place of the nūn of «كان», a verb of approximation (fiʿl muqāraba); its analysis is as before, but the passing away does not occur.
And «لَتَزُوْل» was read with fatḥa on both lāms. Its analysis, despite its difficulty, is that it came on the dialect of those who put fatḥa on the lām of «kay».

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ}: the majority annex «مُخْلِف» to «وعدِه», and there are two aspects to it. The more apparent: that «مُخْلف» is transitive to two objects like its verb, so he put the second object first, and the active participle was annexed to it for lightness, as in «هذا كاسِيْ جُبَّةٍ زيداً» ("this one clothes Zayd with a cloak"). Al-Farrāʾ and Quṭrub said: "Since it is transitive to both of them, no heed is paid to putting one first or last." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said «مُخْلِفَ رسلِه وعدَه», and why did He put the second object before the first? I say: He put the promise first to make known that He never breaks the promise; then He said «رسله» to announce that if He does not break His promise to anyone, and breaking promises is not His way, how could He break it to His messengers?"
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is close to their saying:
291 - 2- يا سارقَ الليلةِ أهلَ الدارِ (O thief of the night, of the people of the house)
and some of them recited, as a parallel to the noble verse, the saying of the poet:
291 - 3- ترى الثورَ فيها مُدخِلَ الظلِ رأسَهُ ... وسائرُه بادٍ إلى الشمسِ أجمعُ (You see the bull in it putting its head in the shade, while the rest of it is exposed to the sun, all of it)
and ḥusbān here is: the negated matter, as in his saying:
291 - 4- فلا تَحسَبَنْ أني أَضِلُّ مَنِيَّتي ... فكلُّ امرِئٍ كأسَ الحِمام يذوقُ (Do not think that I miss my fate, for every man will taste the cup of death)
The second: that it is transitive to one, which is «وعدِه», while «رُسُلَه» is accusative by the maṣdar, for it resolves into a maṣdar particle and a verb, its implied form being: «مُخْلِفُ ما وعدَ رُسُلَه», where «ما» is maṣdar-forming, not in the sense of «alladhī»."
[Translator's note: the passage from "Abū l-Baqāʾ said" onward is garbled in the source: the quotation marks are not closed, the verse numbering (291-2 to 291-4) is interleaved with the text, and the line "ثانٍ" at the start of the second aspect ("الثاني") is run on with the end of verse 291-4. I have translated what is written, keeping the verse numbers; the second verse's gloss and the attribution of the wording after the verses are as they appear in the source.]
A group read {مُخْلِفَ وَعْدَ رُسُلَهُ} with accusative on «وعدَه» and genitive on «رسله», separating the two annexed terms by the object. It is like the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir {قَتْلُ أَوْلاَدَهمْ شُرَكَآئِهِمْ}; al-Zamakhsharī said, boldly: "And this is as weak as the one who read {قَتْلُ أَوْلاَدَهمْ شُرَكَآئِهِمْ}."

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ}: several aspects are permissible in it. The first: that it is accusative (manṣūb) by «انتقام», that is: His vengeance takes place on that day. The second: that it is accusative by «اذكْر» (remember). The third: that it is accusative by what is distilled from the meaning of {عَزِيزٌ ذُو انتقام}. The fourth: that it is a badal (substitute) of {يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ} [Ibrāhīm: 44]. The fifth: that it is accusative by «مُخْلِف». The sixth: that it is accusative by «وَعْدِه», with «إنَّ» and what follows it being a parenthetical clause. Abū l-Baqāʾ ruled out these last two, saying: "because what precedes «inna» does not govern what follows it." That is not a barrier, because, as was said, it is a parenthetical clause, so no heed is paid to it as a separator.
His saying «والسماواتُ»: its implied form is: «وتُبَدَّل السماواتُ غيرَ السماواتِ» (and the heavens will be changed into other than the heavens). Regarding the changing there are two views: is it connected with the essence or with the attribute? Ibn ʿAbbās inclined to the second, and he recited:
291 - 5- فما الناسُ بالناسِ الذين عَهِدْتُهُمْ ... ولا الدارُ التي كنتُ تَعْلَمُ (The people are not the people whom I knew, nor is the abode the one you used to know)
And «نُبَدِّل» was read with nūn, with «الأرضَ» accusative and «السماواتِ» conjoined (nasaq) to it.
His saying: «وبَرَزوا»: there are two aspects to it. One: that it is a resumptive clause, that is: «ويَبْرُزُون» (and they will come forth); so Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it, meaning that it is a past verb intended for the future. The better view is that it is like {ونادى أَصْحَابُ النار} [al-Aʿrāf: 50], {ونادى أَصْحَابُ الجنة} [al-Aʿrāf: 44], {رُّبَمَا يَوَدُّ الذين كَفَرُواْ} [al-Ḥijr: 2], {أتى أَمْرُ الله} [al-Naḥl: 1], because of the certainty of that.
The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الأرض», with «قد» intended with it; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it. The pronoun in «بَرَزوا» would then refer to creation, which the context indicates, and the link between the ḥāl and its owner is the wāw.
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «وبُرِّزوا» with ḍamma on the bāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ, doubled, to indicate intensification in the verb and its object.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مُّقَرَّنِينَ}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), if the verb is one of sight, and it may be a second object, if the verb is one of knowledge. And {فِي الأصفاد} is attached to it. It was also said: to an omitted element, as a ḥāl or an adjective of «مُقَرَّنين». The muqarran is the one gathered in the qaran, which is the rope with which one is tied. He [the poet] said:
291 - 6- وابنُ اللَّبونِ إذا ما لُزَّ في قَرَنٍ ... لم يَسْتَطِعْ صَوْلَةَ البُزْلِ القَناعِيٍسِ (The young camel, when it is bound in a rope, cannot withstand the charge of the strong, mighty camels)
And another said:
291 - 7- والخيرُ والشرُّ مَلْزُوْزان في قَرَنْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (Good and evil are bound together in a rope ...)
In the exegesis: every disbeliever is bound together with his devil in a chain.
And al-aṣfād: the plural of ṣafad, which is the shackle and the fetter. It is said: «صَفَده يَصْفِدُه صَفْداً» (he fettered him); the noun is al-ṣafad, and «صَفَّده», doubled, is for intensification. He [the poet] said:
298 - 1- فآبُوا بالنهَّائِبِ والسَّبايا ... وأُبْنا بالمُلوكِ مُصفَّدينا (They returned with the plunder and the captives, and we returned with the kings fettered)
[Translator's note: the verse number appears in the source as 298 - 1, though the sequence of the surrounding numbers (291 - 7, 291 - 9) suggests 291 - 8; I have kept the number as written.]
And al-ṣifād is like al-ṣafad, and «أَصْفَده» means: he gave him. So they distinguished between faʿala and afʿala. It was also said: rather, both are used for fettering and for giving.
Al-Nābigha said:
291 - 9- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
فلم أُعَرِّض -أبيتَ اللَّعْنَ- بالصَّفَد (so I did not allude — may you refuse curses — to the giving)
that is: to the giving. Giving was called ṣafad because it binds the one to whom it is given; and from it comes "I am shackled by your favours and a captive of your bounty."

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سَرَابِيلُهُم مِّن قَطِرَانٍ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar (subject and predicate) in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial): either from «المجرمين», or from «مُقَرَّنين», or from its pronoun. It may also be resumptive, and this is the apparent view.
Al-sarābīl: garments. «سَرْبَلْتُه» means: you clothed him with the sirbāl. He [the poet] said:
292 - 0- أَوْدَى بنَعْلَيَّ وسِرْباليَهْ (It destroyed my two sandals and my two garments)
and it is applied to what fortifies in war, such as armour and the like. The Exalted said: {وَسَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُم بَأْسَكُمْ} [al-Naḥl: 81].
Al-qaṭirān: what is extracted from a tree, then boiled and smeared on mangy camels so that their mange goes away by its sharpness; and it is the best of things for kindling with. There are dialects in it: qaṭirān with fatḥa on the qāf and kasra on the ṭāʾ, which is the reading of the majority. Qaṭrān on the pattern of sakrān, with which ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib read. Abū l-Najm said:
292 - 1- لَبَّسَه القَطْرانَ والمُسُوحَا ... (He clothed him in tar and in coarse haircloth)
And qiṭrān with kasra on the qāf and sukūn on the ṭāʾ, on the pattern of sirḥān; it was not read so, as far as I know.
A large group, among them ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Hurayra and al-Ḥasan, read «بَقَطِرٍ آنٍ» with fatḥa on the qāf, kasra on the ṭāʾ and tanwīn on the rāʾ, and «آنٍ» on the pattern of ʿānin, making them two words. Al-qaṭir is copper, and al-ānī is an active participle of «أَنَى يَأْني», that is: it reached the utmost in heat, as in His saying: {وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ} [al-Raḥmān: 44]. And from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: "It is not the tar, but rather the copper that takes on its colour."
And «وتَغَشَّى» was read with doubled shīn, that is «وتَتَغشَّى», with one of the two tāʾs omitted.
It was also read with «وجوهُهم» nominative and «النار» accusative, by way of figurative speech, making the faces' coming to the Fire a covering.
As for the clause «وتَغْشى», Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "also a ḥāl," meaning that it is conjoined to the ḥāl, and he does not mean that it is a ḥāl with the wāw being a wāw of the ḥāl, because it is an affirmative imperfect.

semin-durr:51-51.t: His saying, the Exalted: {لِيَجْزِيَ}: in this verse there are two aspects. The better of them: that it is attached to «بَرَزُوا», and on this view His saying «وَتَرَى» is a parenthetical clause between the attached element and that to which it is attached. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element, that is: "We did that to the criminals so that He might recompense every soul"; because when He punishes the criminal, He rewards the obedient.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {هذا} is a pointer to what precedes, from His saying {فَلاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ} [Ibrāhīm: 47] up to here, or to the whole Qurʾān, which is treated as though present.
His saying: «وَلِيُنْذَروا»: there are several aspects in it. The first: that it is attached to an omitted element, that is: «وليُنْذِرُوا به أَنْزَلْنا عليك» (We sent it down to you so that they may be warned by it).
The second: that it is conjoined to an omitted element, and that omitted element is attached to «بلاغ», its implied form being: «ليُنْصَحوا ولِيُنْذَروا» (so that they may be advised and warned). The third: that the wāw is redundant (zāʾida) and «لِيُنْذَروا» is attached to «بلاغ»; this is the opinion of al-Akhfash, reported by al-Māwardī. The fourth: that it is construed according to the meaning, that is: «ليُبَلَّغُوا ولِيُنْذَرُوا» (so that it be conveyed to them and they be warned). The fifth: that the lām is the lām of command. Some of them said: it is good were it not for His saying «ولِيَذَّكَّر», which is only accusative. I say: there is no objection in that, for His saying «ولِيَذَّكَّرَ» is not conjoined to what precedes it, but is attached to an implied verb, that is: «ولِيَذَّكَّر أَنْزَلْناه وأَوْحيناه» (We sent it down and revealed it so that he may take heed). The sixth: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). The implied form: «هذا بلاغٌ وهو ليذَّكَّر»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it. The seventh: that it is the conjunction of a singular to a singular, that is: "this is a delivery of the message and a warning"; al-Mubarrad said it, and it is an explanation of meaning, not of i'rab.
The eighth: that it is conjoined to His saying {لِتُخْرِجَ الناس} [Ibrāhīm: 1] at the beginning of the sūra. This is very strange. The ninth: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The meaning: this is a delivery of the message to the people and for the warning, so it is attached to «بلاغ» or to an omitted element if you make «الناس» an adjective; and it may be attached to an omitted element, its implied form being: «ولِيُنْذَروا به أُنْزِل وتُلِي» (it was sent down and recited so that they may be warned by it)." I say: the implication leads to the construction remaining: "this is a delivery of the message for the warning," and the warning cannot be a purpose of that.
The majority read «لِيُنْذَرُوا» as a passive. Mujāhid and Ḥumayd ibn Qays read «ولِتُنْذِرُوا» with a ḍamma-vowelled tāʾ and kasra on the dhāl, as though the delivery is for everyone and the warning is for those addressed.
Yaḥyā ibn ʿUmāra al-Dhāriʿ, from his father, and Aḥmad ibn Yazīd ibn Usayd al-Sulamī read «ولِيُنْذَرُوا» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the dhāl, from «نَذَر بالشيء», that is: he knew of it and so prepared for it. They said: no maṣdar is known for it, so it is like «ʿasā» and other verbs that have no verbal nouns.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الشَّيْطَانُ لَمَّا قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمْ وَعْدَ الْحَقِّ وَوَعَدْتُكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُكُمْ وَمَا كَانَ لِي عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ إِلَّا أَنْ دَعَوْتُكُمْ فَاسْتَجَبْتُمْ لِي فَلَا تَلُومُونِي وَلُومُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ مَا أَنَا بِمُصْرِخِكُمْ وَمَا أَنْتُمْ بِمُصْرِخِيَّ إِنِّي كَفَرْتُ بِمَا أَشْرَكْتُمُونِي مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (٢٢)).
The Exalted's saying (إِلَّا أَنْ دَعَوْتُكُمْ): a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because his calling was not a sulṭān, i.e. a proof.
(بِمُصْرِخِيَّ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ. It is the plural of مُصْرِخٍ; the first yāʾ is the yāʾ of the plural and the second is the pronoun of the first person. It was given fatḥa so that the kasra and the yāʾ would not come together after two kasras.
It is also read with kasra on it, and that is weak because of the heaviness we mentioned. There are two views on it:
The first: it was given kasra according to the original form.
The second: he intended by it مُصْرِخِيِّ, and this is a minor dialect (lughayya), whose speakers say فِي and رَمَيْتِيهِ, so that a yāʾ follows the kasra by way of lengthening (ishbāʿ); except that in the verse the final yāʾ was dropped, the kasra before it sufficing.
(بِمَا أَشْرَكْتُمُونِ): concerning «مَا» there are two views. The first: it means الَّذِي (that which); on this view the implied wording is بِالَّذِي أَشْرَكْتُمُونِي بِهِ, i.e. "in the idol, in which you obeyed me as you obeyed it", and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) was dropped. The second: it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. "in your associating me with Allah, Mighty and Majestic".
And (مِنْ قَبْلُ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَشْرَكْتُمُونِي, i.e. "I now disbelieve in that with which you associated me before".
It is also said that it is attached to كَفَرْتُ, i.e. "I disbelieved before your associating (me), so I will not benefit you at all".

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأُدْخِلَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ تَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيهَا سَلَامٌ (٢٣)).
The Exalted's saying (وَأُدْخِلَ): it is read in the form of the past verb, and it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to بَرَزُوا, or to فَقَالَ الضُّعَفَاءُ. It is also read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with ḍamma on the lām, as an imperfect verb, the fāʿil (agent) being Allah.
(بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ): it may belong to the completion of (أُدْخِلَ), or it may belong to the completion of «خَالِدِينَ».
(تَحِيَّتُهُمْ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) may be annexed to its agent, i.e. they greet one another with this word; or it may be annexed to its object, i.e. Allah, or the angels, greet them.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ أَصْلُهَا ثَابِتٌ وَفَرْعُهَا فِي السَّمَاءِ (٢٤)).
The Exalted's saying (كَلِمَةً): a badal (substitute) for «مَثَلًا». (كَشَجَرَةٍ): a naʿt (adjective) for it. It is also read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, «كَلِمَةٌ» in the nominative, with كَشَجَرَةٍ as its khabar (predicate).
And (تُؤْتِي أُكُلَهَا): a naʿt for the tree; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the meaning of the second clause, i.e. "it rises, yielding its fruit".

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ اجْتُثَّتْ مِنْ فَوْقِ الْأَرْضِ مَا لَهَا مِنْ قَرَارٍ (٢٦)).
The Exalted's saying (مَا لَهَا مِنْ قَرَارٍ): the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) for شَجَرَةٍ. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «اجْتُثَّتْ».

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ وَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ الظَّالِمِينَ وَيَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ مَا يَشَاءُ (٢٧)).
The Exalted's saying (فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يُثَبِّتُ. It may also be attached to الثَّابِتِ.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ بَدَّلُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ كُفْرًا وَأَحَلُّوا قَوْمَهُمْ دَارَ الْبَوَارِ (٢٨)).
The Exalted's saying (كُفْرًا): the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of بَدَّلَ.
And (جَهَنَّمَ): a badal (substitute) for دَارِ الْبَوَارِ. It may also be accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, i.e. "they will roast in جَهَنَّمَ", or "they will enter جَهَنَّمَ".
And (يَصْلَوْنَهَا) is an explanation (tafsīr) of it; on this view يَصْلَوْنَهَا has no grammatical position. On the first view, its position may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from جَهَنَّمَ, or from الدَّار, or from قَوْمَهُمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ لِعِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلَانِيَةً مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لَا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلَا خِلَالٌ (٣١))
The Exalted's saying (يُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ): there are three views on it. The first: it is the answer (jawāb) of «قُلْ», and there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "say to them 'perform the prayer', and they will perform it", i.e. "if you say to them, they will perform it". Al-Akhfash said this.
A group rejected it, saying: because the Messenger's saying (this) to them does not necessitate that they perform (it). In my view this does not invalidate his position, because he did not mean by "the servants" the disbelievers but the believers; and when the Messenger says to them "perform the prayer", they perform it. This is shown by His saying «لِعِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا».
The second position is reported from al-Mubarrad: that the implied wording is "say to them 'perform', they will perform"; so the explicit يُقِيمُوا is the answer to the omitted أَقِيمُوا. A number (of scholars) reported it without addressing its invalidity; and it is invalid for two reasons:
The first: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) differs from the condition, either in the verb or in the agent or in both. When it is the same as it in both the verb and the agent, that is an error, as in your saying قُمْ تَقُمْ ("stand, you will stand"); and the implied wording according to what is mentioned in this view is: "if they perform, they will perform". The second reason: the implied imperative is for direct address (second person), while يُقِيمُوا is in the form of the third person (absence), and that is an error when the agent is one and the same. The third position: it is jussive (majzūm) by an omitted lām, its implied form being لِيُقِيمُوا ("let them perform"), so it is a resumptive (new) command; and the dropping of the lām is permitted because «قُلْ» indicates the command.
And (يُنْفِقُوا) is like يُقِيمُوا.
(سِرًّا وَعَلَانِيَةً): two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الْفُلْكَ لِتَجْرِيَ فِي الْبَحْرِ بِأَمْرِهِ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الْأَنْهَارَ (٣٣)).
[Translator's note: the source entry is numbered for verse 32 but quotes part of verse 32 with the verse marker (٣٣), and the word commented on, دَائِبَيْنِ, is from verse 33.]
The Exalted's saying (دَائِبَيْنِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the sun and the moon.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَآتَاكُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ وَإِنْ تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَظَلُومٌ كَفَّارٌ (٣٤)).
The Exalted's saying (مِنْ كُلِّ مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ): it is read with «كُلِّ» annexed to «مَا». Then, according to al-Akhfash, مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida); and according to Sībawayh the object is omitted, its implied form being: "of everything you asked Him, what you asked Him".
And (مَا) may mean الَّذِي (that which), or be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), or be maṣdariyya, the maṣdar then having the sense of the object. It is also read with tanwīn on «كُلِّ»; on this reading مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of آتَاكُمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَذَا الْبَلَدَ آمِنًا وَاجْنُبْنِي وَبَنِيَّ أَنْ نَعْبُدَ الْأَصْنَامَ (٣٥)).
The Exalted's saying (آمِنًا): the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «الْبَلَدَ» is a description of the first object.
And (اجْنُبْنِي): one says جَنَبْتُهُ, أَجْنَبْتُهُ and جَنَّبْتُهُ (I kept him away).
It has been read with a disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) and kasra on the nūn.
(أَنْ نَعْبُدَ): i.e. عَنْ أَنْ نَعْبُدَ ("from worshipping"); the disagreement about its position in the i'rab has been mentioned several times.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النَّاسِ فَمَنْ تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي وَمَنْ عَصَانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (٣٦)).
The Exalted's saying (وَمَنْ عَصَانِي): a conditional in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is «فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ»; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "to him". Its like was mentioned in (Surat) Yūsuf.

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبَّنَا إِنِّي أَسْكَنْتُ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوَادٍ غَيْرِ ذِي زَرْعٍ عِنْدَ بَيْتِكَ الْمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ وَارْزُقْهُمْ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ (٣٧)).
The Exalted's saying (مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي): the object is omitted, i.e. "some offspring of my offspring"; and according to the view of al-Akhfash it may be explained with «مِنْ» as redundant (zāʾida).
(عِنْدَ بَيْتِكَ): it may be an adjective (ṣifa) for «وَادٍ», or a badal (substitute) for it. (لِيُقِيمُوا): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَسْكَنْتُ. And (تَهْوِي) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of اجْعَلْ.
It is read with kasra on the wāw, and its past is هَوِيَ and its maṣdar (verbal noun) الْهَوَى. It is also read with fatḥa on the wāw followed by an alif, and its past is هَوِيَ يَهْوَى هَوًى. [Translator's note: the source gives هَوِيَ as the past for both readings; for the first reading (تَهْوِي) one would expect هَوَى يَهْوِي. Translated as written.] The two meanings are close, except that هَوَى is transitive by itself while هَوِيَ is transitive with إِلَى; however, the second reading was made transitive with إِلَى by treating it like تَمِيلُ ("inclines").

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي وَهَبَ لِي عَلَى الْكِبَرِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَسَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ (٣٩)).
The Exalted's saying (عَلَى الْكِبَرِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the yāʾ in «وَهَبَ لِي».

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةِ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَاءِ (٤٠)).
The Exalted's saying (وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the object in «اجْعَلْنِي», and the implied wording is: "and (make) of my offspring one who performs the prayer".

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ غَافِلًا عَمَّا يَعْمَلُ الظَّالِمُونَ إِنَّمَا يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ تَشْخَصُ فِيهِ الْأَبْصَارُ (٤٢)).
The Exalted's saying (إِنَّمَا يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ): it is read with nūn (نُؤَخِّرُهُمْ, "We defer them") as an expression of majesty, and with yāʾ because the name of Allah the Exalted comes before it.
(لِيَوْمٍ): i.e. for the sake of the recompense of a day. It is also said that it means إِلَى ("until").

ukberi-tibyan:43-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مُهْطِعِينَ مُقْنِعِي رُءُوسِهِمْ لَا يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ وَأَفْئِدَتُهُمْ هَوَاءٌ (٤٣) وَأَنْذِرِ النَّاسَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ الْعَذَابُ فَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا رَبَّنَا أَخِّرْنَا إِلَى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ نُجِبْ دَعْوَتَكَ وَنَتَّبِعِ الرُّسُلَ أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوا أَقْسَمْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ زَوَالٍ (٤٤)).
The Exalted's saying (مُهْطِعِينَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْأَبْصَارِ. This is permitted only because the implied wording is "on which the owners of the eyes stare", since one says شَخَصَ زَيْدٌ بَصَرَهُ ("Zayd fixed his gaze"); or (because) the eyes point to their owners, so the ḥāl was made from what is pointed to. It may also be the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "you see them مُهْطِعِينَ (hastening)".
(مُقْنِعِي رُءُوسِهِمْ): the annexation (iḍāfa) is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa), because it (the participle) refers to the future or the present. (لَا يَرْتَدُّ): a ḥāl from the pronoun in مُقْنِعِي, or a badal (substitute) for مُقْنِعِي. And (طَرْفُهُمْ) is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of the agent, because one says مَا طَرَفَتْ عَيْنُهُ ("his eye did not blink") and لَمْ يَبْقَ عَيْنٌ تَطْرُفُ ("no eye remained blinking"); and it has come in the plural. And (وَأَفْئِدَتُهُمْ هَوَاءٌ) is a clause in the position of the ḥāl as well; so the governor (ʿāmil) of the ḥāl may be «يَرْتَدُّ» or whatever governors before it are fit to govern it.
If it is said: how is «هَوَاءٌ» singular when it is the khabar (predicate) of a plural? It is answered: since the meaning of هَوَاء here is "empty, hollowed-out", it was made singular, just as it is permissible to make فَارِغَةٌ ("empty", feminine singular) singular; because the tāʾ of the feminine in it indicates the femininity of the plural in «أَفْئِدَتِهِمْ». Similar to it are أَحْوَالٌ صَعْبَةٌ ("hard states"), أَفْعَالٌ فَاسِدَةٌ ("corrupt deeds") and the like.
(يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ): it is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أَنْذِرْ; the implied wording is "and warn them of the punishment of a day". It may not be an adverb of time (ẓarf), because the warning does not take place on that day.

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَسَكَنْتُمْ فِي مَسَاكِنِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمْ كَيْفَ فَعَلْنَا بِهِمْ وَضَرَبْنَا لَكُمُ الْأَمْثَالَ (٤٥)).
The Exalted's saying (وَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمْ): its fāʿil (agent) is a concealed pronoun indicated by the context, i.e. "their state became clear to you".
And (كَيْفَ) is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by «فَعَلْنَا». It may not be the fāʿil of «تَبَيَّنَ», for two reasons. The first: an interrogative is not governed by what precedes it. The second: كَيْفَ can only be a khabar (predicate), or a ẓarf (adverbial) or a ḥāl (circumstantial), according to their disagreement on that.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَدْ مَكَرُوا مَكْرَهُمْ وَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَكْرُهُمْ وَإِنْ كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ الْجِبَالُ (٤٦)).
The Exalted's saying (وَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَكْرُهُمْ): i.e. the knowledge of their plotting, or the recompense of their plotting; the muḍāf (first term of the construct) was dropped.
(لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ): it is read with kasra on the first lām and fatḥa on the second, and it is the lām of kay (lām of purpose). On this reading there are two views about «إِنْ». The first: it means مَا (negation), i.e. "their plotting was not such as to remove the mountains"; and this is a likening (tamthīl) of the affair of the Prophet ﷺ. The second: it is lightened from the heavy (inna), and the meaning is: they plotted in order to remove what is like the mountains in firmness, and such plotting is futile. It is also read with fatḥa on the first lām and ḍamma on the second (لَتَزُولُ); on this reading إِنْ is lightened from the heavy, and the lām is for emphasis (tawkīd).
It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with fatḥa on both lāms, and that is according to the dialect of those who give fatḥa to the lām of kay. And «كَانَ» here may be the complete (tāmma) one, and it may be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) one.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقَامٍ (٤٧)).
The Exalted's saying (مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ): الرُّسُل is the first object and الْوَعْد is the second object. The annexation of مُخْلِف to الْوَعْد is a matter of latitude (ittisāʿ); the original is مُخْلِفٌ رُسُلَهُ وَعْدَهُ, but it became acceptable since each of the two is an object. It is close to their saying:
يَا سَارِقَ اللَّيْلَةِ أَهْلَ الدَّارِ
(O you who rob, in the night, the people of the house.)
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ (٤٨)).
The Exalted's saying (يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ): يَوْمَ here is an adverb of time (ẓarf) for «انْتِقَامٍ», or the object of an omitted verb, i.e. "remember the day". It may not be a ẓarf for مُخْلِف nor for وَعْدِهِ, because what comes before إِنَّ does not govern what comes after it; but it is permissible to extract from the meaning of the speech something that governs the ẓarf, i.e. "He does not break His promise on the day (the earth) is changed".
(وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ): its implied form is "and other than the heavens"; it (غَيْر) was dropped because what precedes indicates it.
(وَبَرَزُوا): it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), i.e. "and they will come forth".
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْأَرْض, with «قَدْ» intended along with it.
