ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَرَابِيلُهُمْ مِنْ قَطِرَانٍ وَتَغْشَى وُجُوهَهُمُ النَّارُ (٥٠)).
The Exalted's saying (سَرَابِيلُهُمْ مِنْ قَطِرَانٍ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْمُجْرِمِينَ, or from the pronoun in «مُقَرَّنِينَ». The majority take الْقَطِرَان as one word.
It is also read «قِطْرٍ آنٍ» as two words: الْقِطْر is copper, and الْآنِي is that which has reached the utmost heat.
And (تَغْشَى) is also a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِيَجْزِيَ اللَّهُ كُلَّ نَفْسٍ مَا كَسَبَتْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ (٥١)).
The Exalted's saying (لِيَجْزِيَ): i.e. "We did that for the sake of recompense"; it may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to بَرَزُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَذَا بَلَاغٌ لِلنَّاسِ وَلِيُنْذَرُوا بِهِ وَلِيَعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ وَلِيَذَّكَّرَ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ (٥٢)).
The Exalted's saying (وَلِيُنْذَرُوا بِهِ): the meaning is: the Qur'an is a communication to the people and for warning; so the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to الْبَلَاغ, or to something omitted if you make لِلنَّاسِ an adjective (ṣifa).
It may also be attached to something omitted, its implied form being "and that they may be warned by it, it was sent down" or "recited". And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الر كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ (١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كِتَابٌ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a Book". And «أَنْزَلْنَاهُ» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «كِتَابٌ», not a ḥāl (circumstantial), because «كِتَابًا» is indefinite. (بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ): in the position of the accusative; if you wish, as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "by reason of the permission"; and if you wish, in the position of a ḥāl from «النَّاسَ», i.e. "permitted", or from the agent pronoun, i.e. "being permitted (to do so)". (إِلَى صِرَاطِ): this is a badal (substitute) from His saying «إِلَى النُّورِ», with repetition of the preposition.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَوَيْلٌ لِلْكَافِرِينَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ (٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اللَّهِ الَّذِي): it is read in the genitive as a badal (substitute), and in the nominative on three views:
The first: as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what follows it as the khabar (predicate). The second: as a khabar, with the mubtadaʾ omitted, i.e. "He is Allah", and «الَّذِي» an adjective (ṣifa). The third: it is a mubtadaʾ, «الَّذِي» its adjective, and the khabar omitted, its implied form being "Allah, to whom belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, is the Almighty, the Praiseworthy"; it was omitted because it had been mentioned before.
And (وَيْلٌ) is a mubtadaʾ, and «لِلْكَافِرِينَ» its khabar.
(مِنْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ): in the position of the nominative as an adjective of «وَيْلٌ», after the khabar, and that is permissible. It may not be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «وَيْلٌ», because of the separation between them by the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَسْتَحِبُّونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا عَلَى الْآخِرَةِ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَيَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجًا أُولَئِكَ فِي ضَلَالٍ بَعِيدٍ (٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَسْتَحِبُّونَ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of «الْكَافِرِينَ»; or in the position of the accusative by an implied «أَعْنِي» ("I mean"); or in the position of the nominative by an implied «هُمْ» ("they are").
(وَيَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجًا): it has been mentioned in Āl ʿImrān.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ فَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "except speaking their language".
Among the irregular (shādhdh) readings it was read «بِلِسْنِ قَوْمِهِ», with kasra on the lām and sukūn on the sīn; it means "tongue (language)".
(فَيُضِلُّ) is in the nominative; it was not put in the accusative by conjunction with «لِيُبَيِّنَ», because conjunction makes the meaning of the maʿṭūf (conjoined) like the meaning of what it is conjoined to, and the messengers were sent to make clear, not to lead astray.
Al-Zajjāj said: had it been read in the accusative, with the lām being the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba), it would have been permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَى بِآيَاتِنَا أَنْ أَخْرِجْ قَوْمَكَ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ وَذَكِّرْهُمْ بِأَيَّامِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ (٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ أَخْرِجْ قَوْمَكَ): «أَنْ» means «أَيْ» ("that is"), so it has no grammatical position.
It may also be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun); the implied form is then "بِأَنْ أَخْرِجْ" ("with: bring out"); and this has been mentioned in more than one place.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ أَنْجَاكُمْ مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ وَيُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَاءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَاءَكُمْ وَفِي ذَلِكُمْ بَلَاءٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ أَنْجَاكُمْ): it has been mentioned at His saying (إِذْ كُنْتُمْ أَعْدَاءً).
(وَيُذَبِّحُونَ): another ḥāl (circumstantial), conjoined to (يَسُومُونَ).

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ وَلَئِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ إِنَّ عَذَابِي لَشَدِيدٌ (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ): conjoined to «إِذْ أَنْجَاكُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعَادٍ وَثَمُودَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ لَا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّهُ جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَرَدُّوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِي أَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَقَالُوا إِنَّا كَفَرْنَا بِمَا أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ وَإِنَّا لَفِي شَكٍّ مِمَّا تَدْعُونَنَا إِلَيْهِ مُرِيبٍ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَوْمِ نُوحٍ): a badal (substitute) from «الَّذِينَ».
(وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ): conjoined to it; on this view His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَعْلَمُهُمْ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ». It may also be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), and likewise «جَاءَتْهُمْ».
It may also be that «وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لَا يَعْلَمُهُمْ» its khabar (predicate); or (that «لَا يَعْلَمُهُمْ» is) a ḥāl from the "being settled" (al-istiqrār), and «جَاءَتْهُمُ» is the khabar.
(فِي أَفْوَاهِهِمْ): «فِي» has its usual meaning, an adverb (ẓarf) of «رَدُّوا»; and it is figurative, because when they silenced them, it was as though they put their hands in their mouths and thereby prevented them from speaking.
It is also said: it means «إِلَى» ("to"); and it is also said: it means the bāʾ ("with").

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَتْ رُسُلُهُمْ أَفِي اللَّهِ شَكٌّ فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَدْعُوكُمْ لِيَغْفِرَ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُؤَخِّرَكُمْ إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى قَالُوا إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنَا تُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَصُدُّونَا عَمَّا كَانَ يَعْبُدُ آبَاؤُنَا فَأْتُونَا بِسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَفِي اللَّهِ شَكٌّ): («شَكٌّ» is) the agent (fāʿil) of the adverbial phrase, because it relies on the hamza (of interrogation).
(فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ): an adjective (ṣifa) or a badal (substitute).
(لِيَغْفِرَ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ): the object is omitted, and «مِنْ» (with its noun) is an adjective of it, i.e. "something of your sins". According to al-Akhfash «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida).
Some of them said: «مِنْ» is for substitution (badal), i.e. "that He may forgive you in place of the punishment of your sins", as in His saying (أَرَضِيتُمْ بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ).
(تُرِيدُونَ): another adjective of «بَشَرٌ».

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَتْ لَهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ إِنْ نَحْنُ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَمُنُّ عَلَى مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَمَا كَانَ لَنَا أَنْ نَأْتِيَكُمْ بِسُلْطَانٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ (١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا كَانَ لَنَا أَنْ نَأْتِيَكُمْ): («أَنْ نَأْتِيَكُمْ» is) the noun of «كَانَ», and «لَنَا» is the khabar (predicate).
And (إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); it has been mentioned at the beginning of the sūra.
It may also be that the khabar is «بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ», and «لَنَا» is for clarification (tabyīn).

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا لَنَا أَلَّا نَتَوَكَّلَ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدَانَا سُبُلَنَا وَلَنَصْبِرَنَّ عَلَى مَا آذَيْتُمُونَا وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَلَّا نَتَوَكَّلَ): i.e. "in that we should not rely".
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "not relying". It has been mentioned in more than one place.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاسْتَفْتَحُوا وَخَابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ (١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاسْتَفْتَحُوا): it is also read irregularly in the form of the imperative (وَاسْتَفْتِحُوا).

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ وَيَأْتِيهِ الْمَوْتُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ وَمَا هُوَ بِمَيِّتٍ وَمِنْ وَرَائِهِ عَذَابٌ غَلِيظٌ (١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَتَجَرَّعُهُ): it may be an adjective (ṣifa) of «مَاءٍ», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يُسْقَى», or resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ كَرَمَادٍ اشْتَدَّتْ بِهِ الرِّيحُ فِي يَوْمٍ عَاصِفٍ لَا يَقْدِرُونَ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا عَلَى شَيْءٍ ذَلِكَ هُوَ الضَّلَالُ الْبَعِيدُ (١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "among what is recited to you is the parable of those who…".
And (أَعْمَالُهُمْ كَرَمَادٍ) is a resumptive clause explaining the parable. It is also said: the clause is the khabar of «مَثَلُ» according to the meaning. It is also said: «مَثَلُ» is a mubtadaʾ, and «أَعْمَالُهُمْ» its khabar, i.e. "their parable is the parable of their deeds"; and «كَرَمَادٍ» on this view is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are like ashes".
[Translator's note: the source reads «أَوْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ» ("or «أَعْمَالُهُمْ»") here, as written; the sense requires "and".]
It is also said: «أَعْمَالُهُمْ» is a badal (substitute) from «مَثَلُ», and «كَرَمَادٍ» is the khabar. Were it outside the Qurʾān, it would be permissible to make «أَعْمَالِهِمْ» a badal from «الَّذِينَ», and that would be a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl).
(فِي يَوْمٍ عَاصِفٍ): (i.e. "its wind is stormy"); then «الرِّيحُ» was omitted and the adjective was given to the day figuratively. It is also said: the implied form is "on a day possessing storminess", so it is by way of relation (nasab), as in their saying نَابِلٌ ("possessor of arrows") and رَامِحٌ ("possessor of a spear").
It was also read «يَوْمِ عَاصِفٍ» with the genitive construct, i.e. "on the day of a stormy wind".
(لَا يَقْدِرُونَ): resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ وَيَأْتِ بِخَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ): it is read irregularly with sukūn on the rāʾ in continuous speech (أَلَمْ تَرْ), on the basis that he treated it like the pause.
(خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ): it is read in the form of the past verb, and (خَالِقُ) on the pattern fāʿil; it refers to the past, so it becomes definite by the genitive construct.

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا فَقَالَ الضُّعَفَاءُ لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا لَكُمْ تَبَعًا فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُغْنُونَ عَنَّا مِنْ عَذَابِ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ قَالُوا لَوْ هَدَانَا اللَّهُ لَهَدَيْنَاكُمْ سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْنَا أَجَزِعْنَا أَمْ صَبَرْنَا مَا لَنَا مِنْ مَحِيصٍ (٢١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَبَعًا): if you wish, you may make it the plural of تَابِعٌ ("follower"), like خَادِمٌ and خَدَمٌ, غَائِبٌ and غَيَبٌ; and if you wish, you may make it the maṣdar (verbal noun) of تَبِعَ; the maṣdar is then in the position of the active participle, or the implied form is "possessors of following".
(مِنْ عَذَابِ اللَّهِ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it is originally an adjective (ṣifa) of «شَيْءٍ», its implied form being "مِنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْ عَذَابِ اللَّهِ", with «مِنْ» redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "anything being of the punishment of Allah"; and the verb is construed according to the meaning, its implied form being "will you ward off anything from us?". It may also be that «شَيْءٍ» stands in the position of the maṣdar, i.e. "any availing"; then «مِنْ عَذَابِ اللَّهِ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «مُغْنُونَ».

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Ibrāhīm
Meccan except for two of its verses, which were revealed in Medina: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ بَدَّلُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 28], up to His saying: ﴿وَبِئْسَ القَرارُ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 29]
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الر كِتابٌ أنْـزَلْناهُ إلَيْكَ﴾: ”كِتابٌ“ is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject); the meaning is: "this is a Book which We have sent down to you". Some said: ”كِتابٌ“ is nominative by His saying ”الـر“; but ”الـر“ is not the Book; it is only something of the Book. Do you not see His saying ﴿الر تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ وقُرْآنٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 1]? The Book is only the totality of the verses and the totality of the Qur'an.
And His saying: ﴿لِتُخْرِجَ النّاسَ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إلى النُّورِ بِإذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾: ”اَلظُّلُماتُ“ is the disbelief they were in, because disbelief is not clear, so it was likened to darkness; and faith is clear and luminous, so it was likened to light. The bāʾ is connected to ”تُخْرِجَ“; the meaning is "that you may bring people out by the permission of their Lord", i.e. by what Allah has permitted you of teaching them. And ”بِإذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ“ may mean that no one rightly guided is guided except by Allah's permission and His will. Then He made clear what the light is, saying: ﴿إلى صِراطِ العَزِيزِ الحَمِيدِ﴾. ”اَلْحَمِيدِ“ is genitive (khafḍ) as an attribute of ”اَلْعَزِيزِ“. The nominative is permissible in the sense of ”اَلْحَمِيدُ اللَّهُ“ ("the Praiseworthy is Allah"), with ”اَلْحَمِيدُ“ nominative as mubtadaʾ and your saying ”اَللَّهُ“ as the khabar. And it is permissible that ”اَللَّهُ“ be nominative and ”اَلْحَمِيدِ“ genitive as we described, with the name ”اَللَّهِ“ nominative as mubtadaʾ.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَبْغُونَها عِوَجًا﴾, i.e. they seek other than the straight way and the path of Allah, which is the straight way. ʿIwaj ("crookedness") in religion is built on the pattern ”فِعَلٌ“, while one says ”فِي العَصا عَوَجٌ“ ("there is a bend in the stick") with fatḥa on the ʿayn. ”عِوَجًا“ is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial): a maṣdar (verbal noun) placed in the position of the ḥāl.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما أرْسَلْنا مِن رَسُولٍ إلا بِلِسانِ قَوْمِهِ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ﴾, i.e. in the language of his people, so that his people might understand from him. ﴿فَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَن يَشاءُ﴾: the nominative is the proper way; it is the [correct] speech, and the reading is according to it. The meaning is: the sending only took place for clarification, not for leading astray. The accusative is permissible on a remote interpretation, so that it would be ”لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهم فَيُضِلَّ اللَّهُ مَن يَشاءُ ويَهْدِي“, and the cause of leading astray would be the outcome to which it leads, as He said: ﴿فالتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهم عَدُوًّا وحَزَنًا﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8], i.e. they picked him up, and that led to his becoming an enemy and a grief for them; they did not pick him up in order that he become an enemy and a grief for them. Likewise ”فَيُضِلَّ اللَّهُ مَن يَشاءُ“ would mean: "the matter would lead to their going astray, so Allah leads them astray". The first view is the [right] view, and the reading is according to it.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا﴾, i.e. the proof that indicated the truth of his prophethood, such as bringing out his hand white and the staff becoming a snake.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أنْ أخْرِجْ قَوْمَكَ﴾, i.e. ”بِأنْ أخْرِجْ قَوْمَكَ“ ("with: bring out your people"); the meaning is: "We sent him to bring his people out of the darkness into the light", i.e. from the darkness of disbelief to the light of Islam. ”أنْ“ here may be in the sense of the lightened ”أنْ“, or it may be explicative (mufassira), the meaning being: "We sent Mūsā with Our signs, that is: bring out your people", as though the meaning were: "We said to him: bring out your people".
Like this is: ﴿وانْطَلَقَ المَلأُ مِنهم أنِ امْشُوا﴾ [Ṣād: 6], i.e. "that is: walk on", and the interpretation is: "they said to them: walk on". Sībawayh said: you say ”كَتَبْتُ إلَيْهِ أنْ قُمْ، وأمَرْتُهُ أنْ قُمْ“ ("I wrote to him: stand; and I commanded him: stand"). If you wish, ”أنْ“ is joined to the imperative while the interpretation is that of a statement, the meaning being: "I wrote to him that he should stand, and I commanded him to stand"; only it has been joined to the imperative form addressed to the second person while the meaning is that of a statement, just as you say ”أنْتَ الَّذِي فَعَلْتَ“ ("you are the one who did [lit. you did]") and the meaning is ”أنْتَ الَّذِي فَعَلَ“. He said: and it may be in the sense of ”أيْ“ ("that is"); like it is: ”أرْسَلْتُ إلَيْهِ أنْ ما أنْتَ وذا؟“ ("I sent to him: what have you to do with this?").
And His saying: ﴿وَذَكِّرْهم بِأيّامِ اللَّهِ﴾: ”وَذَكِّرْهُمْ“ is conjoined to ”أخْرِجْ“. Reminding them of the days of Allah means reminding them of the blessings of Allah's days upon them, and of Allah's vengeances with which He took vengeance on the people of Nūḥ, ʿĀd and Thamūd; i.e. remind them of the days that passed for those who disbelieved and what befell them in them, and remind them of Allah's blessings.
The evidence that the reminding includes warning and cautioning against what befell those before them is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, after this verse: ﴿ألَمْ يَأْتِكم نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكم قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وعادٍ وثَمُودَ والَّذِينَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 9], i.e. have the reports of those and the calamities that befell them not come to them? ﴿لا يَعْلَمُهم إلا اللَّهُ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 9]: so Allah made known that after these there were nations whose reports passed away along with those who knew them. From this it has been said: ”كَذَبَ النَّسّابُونَ“ ("the genealogists have lied"), because they do not know who came after these; and this is related from the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿جاءَتْهم رُسُلُهم بِالبَيِّناتِ فَرَدُّوا أيْدِيَهم في أفْواهِهِمْ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 9]
It is related from Ibn Masʿūd that they bit their fingertips in rage at what the messengers brought them. It has been said: ”رَدُّوا أيْدِيَهم في أفْواهِهِمْ“ means they gestured to the messengers to be silent. And it has been said: in ”رَدُّوا أيْدِيَهُمْ“ the hāʾ and the mīm refer back to the messengers, the meaning being: they rejected the hands of the messengers, i.e. the favours of the messengers, because their coming with the clear proofs is a favour — you say ”لِفُلانٍ عِنْدِي يَدٌ“ ("so-and-so has a hand with me"), i.e. a favour; and the meaning of ”فِي أفْواهِهِمْ“ is "with their mouths", i.e. "they rejected those favours by speaking out in denial of what the messengers brought". The meaning is that the rejection came in this direction and its sense, as you say ”جَلَسْتُ في البَيْتِ“ and ”جَلَسْتُ بِالبَيْتِ“ ("I sat in the house"). ﴿وَقالُوا إنّا كَفَرْنا بِما أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 9]: this is the rejection.

zajjaj:15-15.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واسْتَفْتَحُوا وخابَ كُلُّ جَبّارٍ عَنِيدٍ﴾: by ”اِسْتَفْتَحُوا“ the messengers are meant; they asked Allah to open [victory] for them, i.e. to help them, and every victory is an opening (fatḥ). ”اَلْجَبّارُ“ is the one who sees no right of anyone over himself, and ”اَلْعَنِيدُ“ is the one who turns away from the straight course. One says: ”جَبّارٌ بَيِّنُ الجَبْرِيَّةِ، والجِبْرِيَّةِ - بِكَسْرِ الجِيمِ -، والجِبِرِيَّةُ - بِكَسْرِ الجِيمِ والباءِ -، والجَبَرُوَّةِ، والجَبَرَوَّةِ، والتَّجْبارِ، والجِبْرِياءِ، والجَبُّورَةِ، والجَبَرُوتِ“ ("a tyrant of manifest tyranny", with the variant forms of the verbal noun: jabriyya, jibriyya — with kasra on the jīm — jibiriyya — with kasra on the jīm and the bāʾ — jabaruwwa, jabarawwa, tajbār, jibriyāʾ, jabbūra and jabarūt).

zajjaj:16-16.t:
﴿مِن ورائِهِ جَهَنَّمُ﴾, i.e. "Hell is before him". ”وَراءَ“ is used for behind and in front; its meaning is only "what is hidden from you", i.e. "what is concealed from you"; it is not one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād), as some philologists say. Al-Nābigha said:
؎حَلَفْتُ فَلَمْ أتْرُكْ لِنَفْسِكَ رِيبَةً ولَيْسَ وراءَ اللَّهِ لِلْمَرْءِ مَذْهَبُ
(I swore, and left no doubt for your soul; and beyond Allah there is no way for a man to go.)
i.e. after the ways of Allah there is no way for a man. ﴿وَيُسْقى مِن ماءٍ صَدِيدٍ﴾, i.e. from the blood and pus that flows from the people of the Fire.

zajjaj:17-17.t: ﴿يَتَجَرَّعُهُ ولا يَكادُ يُسِيغُهُ﴾, i.e. he is unable to swallow it. One says: ”ساغَ لِيَ الشَّرابُ، وأسَغْتُهُ“ ("the drink went down easily for me, and I swallowed it easily"). ﴿وَمِن ورائِهِ عَذابٌ غَلِيظٌ﴾, i.e. after that.

zajjaj:18-18.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ﴾: it is nominative in the sense of: "and among what is recited to you is the likeness of those who disbelieved in their Lord", or: "the likeness of those who disbelieved in their Lord is among what is recited to you". And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that ”مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ“ means: "the description of those who disbelieved in their Lord: their deeds…", as though you said: "those who disbelieved in their Lord, their deeds…", just as you say ”صِفَةُ زَيْدٍ أسْمَرُ“, the meaning being ”زَيْدٌ أسْمَرُ“ ("Zayd is dark-skinned"). Its interpretation is that everything by which those who disbelieve seek to draw near to Allah is nullified. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ”حَبِطَتْ أعْمالُهم في الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ“ ("their deeds have come to nothing in this world and the Hereafter"); and like it is: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 1]

zajjaj:21-21.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾, i.e. Allah gathered them at their mustering, so the follower and the followed came together. ﴿فَقالَ الضُّعَفاءُ﴾ — they are the followers — ﴿لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ — they are the ones followed — ﴿إنّا كُنّا لَكم تَبَعًا﴾, i.e. we followed you in what you called us to. ”تَبَعًا“ is the plural of ”تابِعٌ“; one says ”تابِعٌ“ and ”تَبَعُ“, like ”غائِبٌ“ and ”غَيَبٌ“.
And it is possible that ”تَبَعٌ“ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a name, i.e. "we were people of following".
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَواءٌ عَلَيْنا أجَزِعْنا أمْ صَبَرْنا﴾: ”سَواءٌ“ is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and ”أجَزِعْنا“ is in the position of the khabar (predicate). ﴿ما لَنا مِن مَحِيصٍ﴾, i.e. we have no place of flight and no escape from the punishment. One says ”حاصَ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ، يَحِيصُ“ and ”جاصَ عَنْهُ، يَجِيصُ“ with one meaning ("to swerve away from something"); but this [latter] dialect form is not permissible in the Qur'an. And one says ”وَقَعَ في حَيْصَ بَيْصَ“, ”حاصَ باصَ“ and ”حاصٍ باصٍ“ when someone falls into something from which he cannot extricate himself.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
﴿وَقالَ الشَّيْطانُ لَمّا قُضِيَ الأمْرُ إنَّ اللَّهَ وعَدَكم وعْدَ الحَقِّ﴾: it is related that when the people of Paradise have settled in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire, Iblīs, may Allah's curse be upon him, will stand up as a preacher and say: "Allah promised you the promise of truth" — i.e. He promised Paradise to whoever obeyed Him and promised the Fire to whoever disobeyed Him — "and I promised you the opposite of that". ﴿وَما كانَ لِي عَلَيْكم مِن سُلْطانٍ﴾, i.e. I showed you no proof, ﴿إلا أنْ دَعَوْتُكم فاسْتَجَبْتُمْ لِي﴾, i.e. I seduced you and misled you, and you followed me.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioned the matter of Iblīs and what he will say at the Resurrection as a warning against his misleading and seducing.
﴿ما أنا بِمُصْرِخِكم وما أنْتُمْ بِمُصْرِخِيَّ﴾, i.e. I am not your rescuer, nor are you my rescuers. It was read ”بِمُصْرَخِيَّ“ [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source] with fatḥa on the yāʾ — this is how the people read it — and Ḥamza and al-Aʿmash [Translator's note: the source has «الأعشى» (al-Aʿshā); the reader usually named with Ḥamza here is al-Aʿmash] read ”بِمُصْرِخِيِّ“ with kasra on the yāʾ. This reading, according to all the grammarians, is poor and rejected, and it has no justification except a weak one mentioned by some grammarians.
That is because the yāʾ of annexation (the first-person possessive yāʾ), when there is no quiescent letter before it, is given a vowel, namely fatḥa; you say: ”هَذا غُلامِيَ قَدْ جاءَ“ ("this servant of mine has come"). That is because the pronoun, consisting of a single letter and being denied case inflection, was given the lightest of the vowels, as you say ”هُوَ قائِمٌ“ with fatḥa on the wāw, and ”أنا قُمْتُ“ with fatḥa on the nūn. Making the yāʾ quiescent is also permissible, because of the heaviness of a yāʾ preceded by kasra. But if there is a quiescent letter before the yāʾ, it is given fatḥa and nothing else, because its basic state is to have a vowel even with no quiescent letter before it, and when a quiescent letter precedes it its vowel becomes obligatory because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Whoever permits ”بِمُصْرِخِيِّ“ with kasra is obliged to say: ”هَذِهِ عَصايِ أتَوَكَّأُ عَلَيْها“. Al-Farrāʾ permitted the kasra on a weak basis, because the basic vowel for the meeting of two quiescent letters is kasra, and he recited:
؎قالَ لَها هَلْ لَكِ يا ثافِيِّ قالَتْ لَهُ ما أنْتَ بِالمَرْضِيِّ
(He said to her: would you like [it], O you of mine? She said to him: you are not one to be pleased with.)
This poetry is not to be heeded; composing the like of it is easy, the Arab who said it is not known, and it is not something to be cited as evidence regarding the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. ﴿إنِّي كَفَرْتُ بِما أشْرَكْتُمُونِ مِن قَبْلُ﴾: "I disbelieve in your associating me with Allah, O followers", as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ القِيامَةِ يَكْفُرُونَ بِشِرْكِكُمْ﴾ [Fāṭir: 14]. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿عَذابٌ ألِيمٌ﴾ means painful, causing pain.

zajjaj:24-24.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلا كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ أصْلُها ثابِتٌ وفَرْعُها في السَّماءِ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, struck a parable for faith in Him and a parable for disbelief in Him. He made the likeness of the believer — in his uttering of His oneness, his faith in His Prophet and his following of His law — like the good tree; He made the benefit of abiding by His oneness like the benefit of the good tree whose benefit and fruit do not cease. It has come in the exegesis that the good tree is the date palm. The evidence that this parable means the oneness of Allah and faith in His Prophet and His law is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالقَوْلِ الثّابِتِ في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وفي الآخِرَةِ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 27]

zajjaj:25-25.t:
And His saying: ﴿تُؤْتِي أُكُلَها كُلَّ حِينٍ بِإذْنِ رَبِّها﴾: people differed over the explanation of al-ḥīn ("time"). Some said: "every year"; some said: "every six months"; some said: "morning and evening"; and some said: ”اَلْحِينُ“ is two months. All the philologists we have met hold that al-ḥīn is a noun like al-waqt ("time"), applicable to all periods of time, long or short. So the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, ”تُؤْتِي أُكُلَها كُلَّ حِينٍ“ is that it is benefited from at every time, its benefit never ceasing at all. The evidence that al-ḥīn is equivalent to al-waqt is the verse of al-Nābigha — al-Aṣmaʿī recited it — describing the snake and the one bitten:
؎تَناذَرَها الرّاقُونَ مِن سُوءِ سُمِّها تُطْلِقُهُ حِينًا وحِينًا تَراجُعُ
(The charmers warned one another of her because of the evil of her venom: at one time it releases him, and at another time it returns.)
So the meaning is that the pain of the venom eases at one time and returns at another.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ﴾: it has been said that the evil tree is the colocynth (al-ḥanẓal), and it has been said: al-kūth. ﴿اجْتُثَّتْ مِن فَوْقِ الأرْضِ﴾: the meaning of ”اِجْتُثَّتْ“ is: it was uprooted from above the earth; and the meaning of ”اِجْتُثَّ“ in the language is: its whole body (juththa) was taken. ﴿ما لَها مِن قَرارٍ﴾: so the meaning is that the remembrance of Allah with His oneness remains forever and its benefit remains forever, and that disbelief and misguidance have no firmness.

zajjaj:27-27.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالقَوْلِ الثّابِتِ في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وفي الآخِرَةِ﴾: it is related that this verse was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave. When the dead person dies, he is asked: "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? And who is your Prophet?" If he says: "Allah is my Lord, Muḥammad is my Prophet, and Islam is my religion", then Allah has made him firm with the firm word in the Hereafter — because this is after his death — and has made him firm in this world, because he is not prompted with it in the Hereafter unless he had bound himself to it in this world.

zajjaj:28-28.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ بَدَّلُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ كُفْرًا وأحَلُّوا قَوْمَهم دارَ البَوارِ﴾: ”اَلْبَوارُ“ is destruction and extirpation.

zajjaj:29-29.t: ﴿جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَها﴾: ”جَهَنَّمَ“ is a badal (substitute) for His saying ”دارَ البَوارِ“, and explains it. ”جَهَنَّمَ“ is not given nunation (it is a diptote) because it is feminine and definite.

zajjaj:30-30.t: And His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أنْدادًا﴾: ”اَلنِّدُّ“ is the like; He made clear the manner of their disbelief. ﴿لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ﴾, and ”لِيَضِلُّوا“: it has been read both ways.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ لِعِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ﴾: if you wish you give the yāʾ a vowel, and if you wish you make it quiescent. ”يُقِيمُوا“ is jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the command. There is more than one view on it. The best of them is that it is indeclinable (mabnī), because it is in the place of the imperative. It is also possible that it is jussive with the sense of the lām [of command], except that the lām has been dropped because the command to the absent party is indicated by ”قُلْ“. You say: ”قُلْ لِزَيْدٍ: لِيَضْرِبْ عَمْرًا“ ("tell Zayd: let him strike ʿAmr"), and if you wish you say: ”قُلْ لِزَيْدٍ يَضْرِبْ عَمْرًا“; but ”قُلْ يَضْرِبْ زَيْدٌ عَمْرًا“ is not permissible here in the jussive until you say ”لِيَضْرِبْ“, because the lām of the absent party has no substitute here if you drop it.
There is a third view: as the answer to the command, in the sense of: "say to My servants who believe: establish the prayer, [and] they will establish the prayer", because when they believe and affirm, their affirmation consists in accepting the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
And His saying: ﴿مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ ولا خِلالٌ﴾: if you wish you put both al-bayʿ and al-khilāl in the nominative; if you wish you put both in the accusative without nunation; and if you wish you put one in the accusative and the other in the nominative. The accusative is by negation with ”لا“ (the lā of generic negation); we have explained that earlier in the book. ”اَلْخِلالُ“ and ”اَلْخُلَّةُ“ are in the sense of ”اَلصَّداقَةُ“ (friendship).

zajjaj:33-33.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الشَّمْسَ والقَمَرَ دائِبَيْنِ﴾: its meaning is "constant in setting right what they set right of people and plants, never slackening".

zajjaj:34-34.t:
﴿وَآتاكم مِن كُلِّ ما سَألْتُمُوهُ﴾, and it is read: ”مِن كُلٍّ ما سَألْتُمُوهُ“, with nunation on ”كُلٍّ“. [In the first reading] the position of ”ما“ is genitive by annexation, and the meaning is: "of all that you asked Him". Whoever reads ”مِن كُلٍّ ما سَألْتُمُوهُ“, the position of ”ما“ is accusative, and the meaning is: "and He gave you, of everything, the things you asked Him for".
If someone says: "But He has given the servants what they did not ask for", he is told: that does not contradict this verse. When He says: "and He gave you of all that you asked Him", this does not entail that He gave them nothing other than what they asked for. And it is possible that ”ما“ is negative, the meaning being: "and He gave you of all that you did not ask Him", i.e. "He gave you everything you did not ask Him for".
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ لَظَلُومٌ كَفّارٌ﴾: this is a generic noun by which the disbeliever specifically is intended, as He said: ﴿والعَصْرِ﴾ [al-ʿAṣr: 1] ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ لَفي خُسْرٍ﴾ [al-ʿAṣr: 2] ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ﴾ [al-ʿAṣr: 3]. The human being who is not a believer is most unjust and most ungrateful.

zajjaj:35-35.t: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ إبْراهِيمُ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَذا البَلَدَ آمِنًا﴾, meaning Mecca. ﴿واجْنُبْنِي وبَنِيَّ أنْ نَعْبُدَ الأصْنامَ﴾, and it is read: ”وَأجْنِبْنِي وبَنِيَّ“, from ”أجْنَبْتُهُ كَذا وكَذا“, when I put him to one side of it; and likewise ”جَنَّبْتُهُ كَذا وكَذا“. The meaning of the supplication of Ibrāhīm, upon him be peace, that he be kept away from worshipping idols while he was not a worshipper of them, is: "keep me firm in avoiding their worship", as He said: ﴿واجْعَلْنا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 128], i.e. "keep us firm in Islam".

zajjaj:36-36.t: ﴿رَبِّ إنَّهُنَّ أضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النّاسِ﴾, i.e. they were led astray because of them, since idols have no understanding and do nothing; as you say: ”قَدْ فَتَنَتْنِي هَذِهِ الدّارُ“ ("this house has captivated me"), i.e. I loved it, admired it and was captivated by it. ﴿فَمَن تَبِعَنِي فَإنَّهُ مِنِّي ومَن عَصانِي فَإنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, i.e. You are Forgiving and Merciful to him if he repents and believes; not that he is saying that whoever disbelieves, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful [to him], for Allah does not forgive him. Do you not see His saying about his father: ﴿فَلَمّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ أنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ لِلَّهِ تَبَرَّأ مِنهُ﴾ [al-Tawba: 114]?

zajjaj:37-37.t: ﴿فاجْعَلْ أفْئِدَةً مِنَ النّاسِ تَهْوِي إلَيْهِمْ﴾, i.e. make the hearts of a group of people yearn towards them. ”تَهْوى إلَيْهِمْ“ is also permissible. Whoever reads ”تَهْوِي إلَيْهِمْ“ takes it from ”هَوى يَهْوِي“, when something falls; and whoever reads ”تَهَوى إلَيْهِمْ“ [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source] takes it from ”هَوِيَ، يَهْوى“, when one loves. The first reading is the preferred one.

zajjaj:40-40.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلاةِ ومِن ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾, i.e. "and make of my offspring those who establish the prayer". ﴿رَبَّنا وتَقَبَّلْ دُعاءِ﴾: the reading is without the "yāʾ" in ”دُعائِي“ when you pause. When you continue, you have the choice: if you wish you say ”دُعاءِ“ without yāʾ, the kasra on the hamza standing in for the yāʾ — though the best is to keep the yāʾ — and if you wish you make it quiescent, and if you wish you give it fatḥa.

zajjaj:41-41.t: And His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا اغْفِرْ لِي ولِوالِدَيَّ ولِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: this was before it became clear to Ibrāhīm that his father was an enemy of Allah; when that became clear to him, he disowned him. It has been said that by his parents here he means Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ. It has also been read [Translator's note: the source says «وقيل أيضًا», "it has also been said", then calls it a reading]: ”وَلِوَلَدَيَّ“ ("and my two sons"), meaning by it Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq; but this reading is nothing, because it goes against what the people of the cities among the experts in the readings follow. ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الحِسابُ﴾ means the Day of Resurrection, and ”يَوْمَ“ is accusative by ”اِغْفِرْ لِي“.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
And His saying: ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ مُقْنِعِي رُءُوسِهِمْ﴾: ”مُهْطِعِينَ“ is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "He only defers them to a day on which their eyes will stare, hastening (muhṭiʿīn)", i.e. hurrying. The poet said:
؎بِدِجْلَةَ أهْلُها ولَقَدْ أراهم بِدِجْلَةَ مُهْطِعِينَ إلى السَّماعِ
(Its people are by the Tigris, and I have seen them by the Tigris hastening to listen.)
i.e. hurrying. And ”مُقْنِعِي رُؤُوسِهِمْ“ means raising them, stuck fast to their necks. ”اَلْمُقْنِعُ“ is the one raising, and ”اَلْمُقْنَعُ“ is the one raised. The poet said:
؎يُبادِرْنَ العِضاةَ بِمُقْنَعاتٍ ∗∗∗ نَواجِذُهُنَّ كالحِدَإ الوَقِيعِ
(They rush at the thorn trees with upraised [mouths], their molars like sharpened axe-heads.)
He is describing camels grazing on trees, and that their teeth are raised like axes.
And His saying: ﴿وَأفْئِدَتُهم هَواءٌ﴾, i.e. deviated, retaining nothing because of fear. It has been said: "their hearts have been torn from their insides". The poet said:
؎كَأنَّ الرَّحْلَ مِنها فَوْقَ صَعْلٍ ∗∗∗ مِنَ الظَّلْماءِ جُؤْجُؤُها هَواءُ
(As though the saddle on her were upon a small-headed ostrich of the dark, its breast hollow.)

zajjaj:46-46.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَكْرُهم وإنْ كانَ مَكْرُهم لِتَزُولَ مِنهُ الجِبالُ﴾: the reading with kasra on the first lām of ”لِتَزُولَ“ and fatḥa on the last lām is a good, fine reading. The meaning is: their plotting was not such that the mountains would cease to be by it, i.e. their plotting was not such that the cause of the Prophet ﷺ and the cause of the religion of Islam would cease to be by it — its firmness being like the firmness of the firmly set mountains — because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, promised His Prophet, upon him be peace, to make his religion prevail over all religions, saying: ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 33]. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْلِفَ وعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ إنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقامٍ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 47], i.e. He does not break what He promised them: helping them and making their prophethood and their word prevail.
And it is read: ”وَإنْ كانَ مَكْرُهم لَتَزُولُ مِنهُ الجِبالُ“, with the nominative and fatḥa on the first lām. Its meaning is a good and sound meaning, namely: "with Allah is their plotting, even if their plotting reaches in scheming to the removal of mountains"; for Allah helps His religion, and their plotting is with Him, not hidden from Him.
If someone says: "Did the mountains then cease to be because of their plotting?" — it has been related in some of the exegesis the story of the chest and the vultures, and that the mountains thought it was a mighty matter from among Allah's commands, so they shifted.
It has been said that this is in the story of Nimrūd ibn Kanʿān; but I see no mention of Nimrūd here. However, if the reports about it are sound, its meaning is that even if the plotting of these people reached the plotting of that one, they would not benefit from it. As for what the language and the Arabs' manner of address suggest, it is that the meaning is — even if no mountain ever ceased to be because of plotting — [that it is] hyperbole in describing a thing, to say: even if it reached what it is not thought it could reach, it would not benefit from it [Translator's note: this sentence is garbled in the source («وإن لم يكن جبل قط، زال لمكر المبالغة في وصف الشيء أن يقال…»); translated according to its evident intent]. Al-Aʿshā said:
؎لَئِنْ كُنْتَ في جُبٍّ ثَمانِينَ قامَةً ورُقِّيتَ أسْبابَ السَّماءِ بِسُلَّمِ
(Even if you were in a pit eighty fathoms deep, and were raised up the ropes of the sky by a ladder,)
؎لَيَسْتَدْرِجَنْكَ الأمْرُ حَتّى تَهُزَّهُ ∗∗∗ وتَعْلَمَ أنِّي عَنْكَ لَسْتُ بِمُلْجَمِ
(the matter would surely draw you on step by step until you stir it, and you know that I am not bridled [from speaking] about you.)
He was only exaggerating in the description, knowing that the man would not be raised up the ropes of the sky nor be in a pit eighty fathoms deep so that the speech would draw him on. So the meaning on this view is: even if their plotting removed the mountains, the cause of Islam and what the Prophet ﷺ brought would not cease to be.

zajjaj:47-47.t:
﴿فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْلِفَ وعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ﴾, and it was read: ”مُخْلِفٌ وعْدَهُ رُسُلَهُ“ [Translator's note: as printed; the reading meant is مُخْلِفَ وَعْدَهُ رُسُلِهِ, with وعد accusative and رسل genitive, as the next sentence says]. This reading, with the accusative on al-waʿd and the genitive on al-rusul, is anomalous (shādhdh) and poor: it is not permissible to separate the muḍāf from the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). They recited concerning the like of this:
؎فَزَجَّجْتُها بِمِزَجَّةٍ زَجَّ القَلُوصَ أبِي مَزادَةْ
(I thrust her with a spear, as Abū Mazāda thrusts the young she-camel.)
The meaning is: ”فَزَجَّجْتُها بِمِزَجَّةٍ زَجَّ أبِي مَزادَةَ القَلُوصُ“ [Translator's note: so in the source; القَلُوصَ (accusative) is expected]. The reading is: ”مُخْلِفَ وعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ“, as you say: ”هَذا مُعْطِي دِرْهَمٍ زَيْدًا“ ("this is the giver of a dirham to Zayd").

zajjaj:48-48.t:
﴿يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الأرْضُ غَيْرَ الأرْضِ﴾: if you wish, you put al-yawm in the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) [Translator's note: i.e. as a qualifier/substitute] of His saying: ”يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الحِسابُ يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الأرْضُ“; and if you wish, it may be accusative by His saying ”ذُو انْتِقامٍ“, the meaning being that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is Possessor of retribution, i.e. among them, on the day the earth is changed into another earth.
”اَلْأرْضُ“ is nominative as the noun of the verb whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), and ghayr is accusative as the object of the verb whose agent is not named. You say: ”بُدِّلَ الخاتَمُ خاتَمًا آخَرَ“ ("the ring was changed into another ring") when it is broken and fashioned in another form; and you may say ”بُدِّلَ زَيْدٌ“ when his condition has changed. So the meaning of ”تُبَدَّلُ الأرْضُ غَيْرَ الأرْضِ“ is the setting in motion of its mountains, the bursting forth of its seas, and its becoming level, with no crookedness or unevenness seen in it. This — and Allah knows best — is its changing.
﴿والسَّماواتُ﴾, i.e. and the heavens will be changed into other heavens; and the changing of the heavens is the scattering of their stars, their splitting and cleaving, the rolling up of their sun and the eclipse of their moon. ﴿وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ الواحِدِ القَهّارِ﴾, i.e. they came out of their graves, appearing openly.

zajjaj:49-49.t:
﴿وَتَرى المُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُقَرَّنِينَ في الأصْفادِ﴾: ”اَلْأصْفادُ“ are the shackles; its singular is ”صَفَدٌ“. One says ”صَفَدْتُهُ بِالحَدِيدِ“ and ”أصْفَدْتُهُ“ ("I bound him in iron"), but ”صَفَدْتُ“ is more common for iron; and ”أصْفَدْتُهُ“ when I gave him a gift, and ”صَفَدْتُهُ“ also when I gave him a gift, except that the preferred form for giving is ”أصْفَدْتُهُ“ and for iron ”صَفَدْتُهُ“. The poet said:
؎وَإنْ جِئْتُهُ يَوْمًا فَقَرَّبَ مَجْلِسِي وأصْفَدَنِي عَلى الزَّمانَةِ قائِدا
(And if I come to him one day, he brings my seat near and gives me, in my infirmity, a guide.)
Its meaning is: he gave me a guide.

zajjaj:50-50.t: ﴿سَرابِيلُهم مِن قَطِرانٍ﴾: ”اَلسِّرْبالُ“ is anything worn. Their garments were made of pitch (qaṭirān) — and Allah knows best — because pitch intensifies the blazing of fire on the skins. Had Allah wished to burn them intensely without fire and without pitch, He would have been able to do so; but He punishes with that through which the servants understand punishment, and warns them of what they know the reality of. And it was read: ”مِن قِطْرٍ آنٍ“ — a group read it so — ”اَلْقِطْرُ“ being copper and ”آنٍ“ meaning that whose heat has reached its extreme.
